if craftsmanship avoids engraving and carving,
and women's work avoids ornate patterns,
the state will be rich."
End of the five matters.
Divide the state into five districts,
each with a director.
Divide each district into five townships,
each with a chief.
Divide each township into ten wards,
each with a captain.
Divide each ward into ten neighborhoods,
each with a head.
Ten households form a shí,
five households form a wǔ,
and both shí and wǔ have leaders.
Build barriers and block hideouts,
unify the roads,
and control entry and exit.
Examine the village gates,
carefully manage the keys,
which are stored with the ward captain.
Appoint gate officials
to open and close at set times.
The gate officials observe those entering and exiting,
and report to the ward captain.
Whenever someone enters or exits at irregular times,
wears inappropriate clothing,
or any group or follower
acts contrary to the norm,
the gate officials who see it
report immediately.
If it involves the children, servants, subordinates, or guests of a household head,
the ward captain reprimands the neighborhood head,
the neighborhood head reprimands the shí and wǔ,
and the shí and wǔ reprimand the household head.
After reprimanding and warning, no further report is needed;
the first offense is pardoned,
the third is not forgiven.
All instances of filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, trustworthiness,
worthiness, goodness, and talent,
if found among the children, servants, subordinates, or guests of a household head,
are reported by the shí and wǔ to the neighborhood head,
the neighborhood head to the ward captain,
the ward captain to the township chief,
the township chief to the district director,
and the district director records it with the chief official.
All faults among associates,
if in a household,
implicate the household head;
if in a household head,
implicate the shí and wǔ leaders;
if in the shí and wǔ leaders,
implicate the neighborhood head;
if in the neighborhood head,
implicate the ward captain;
if in the ward captain,
implicate the township chief;
if in the township chief,
implicate the district director;
if in the district director,
implicate the chief official.
Reports are made every three months,
accounts are settled every six months,
and records are updated every twelve months.
In promoting the worthy, do not skip ranks,
in employing the capable, do not combine offices,
in punishing the guilty, do not target individuals alone,
in rewarding the meritorious, do not confer exclusively.
At the court of early spring,
the ruler personally holds audience,
discusses ranks, rewards, and examines officials,
for five days.
At the court of late winter,
the ruler personally holds audience,
discusses punishments, penalties, and executions,
also for five days.
On the first day of the first month,
all officials are in court,
and the ruler issues decrees, promulgating laws throughout the state.
The directors of the five districts,
and the chiefs of the five regions,
all receive the laws from the grand historian.
On the day of the grand court,
the directors of the five districts,
and the chiefs of the five regions,
all personally study the laws before the ruler.
After the grand historian promulgates the laws,
they are registered in the grand archive,
and the law registers are distributed before the ruler.
The directors of the five districts leave the court,
proceed to their district offices,
convey to their subordinates, down to the neighborhood heads,
all receiving the laws.
Once the laws are promulgated,
they return to report completion,
and only then dare to retire to their quarters.
If the laws are not promulgated,
and the report not submitted,
they dare not retire;
retiring to quarters
is called delaying the decree,
a crime punishable by death without pardon.
The five district ministers,
all arrived at court in carriages,
and upon leaving court did not dare to return to their residences,
but proceeded on their way.
On the day they reached the capital,
they went to the ancestral temple, summoned their subordinate officials,
and all received the statutes.
Once the statutes were promulgated,
messengers were dispatched to deliver the orders,
on the day the statutes were issued, whether early or late.
After the statutes were promulgated,
and the messengers had been sent out,
only then did they dare to return to their residences.
If the statutes were not yet promulgated,
and the messengers had not been dispatched,
they did not dare to return to their residences;
returning to their residences
was called delaying orders,
a crime punishable by death without pardon.
Once the statutes were promulgated,
those who did not implement them,
were called disobeying orders,
a crime punishable by death without pardon.
If an examination of the statutes revealed discrepancies with the records of the Grand Repository,
it was called extravagance and autocracy,
and insufficiency was called violating orders,
a crime punishable by death without pardon.
Once the primary statutes were promulgated,
then the statutes could be implemented.
End of the primary statutes.
Whenever an undertaking is to be initiated,
the orders must be issued first.
It is said that when an action is about to be taken,
the measures of rewards and punishments,
must be made clear beforehand.
Those in charge of affairs
strictly adhere to the orders in carrying out rewards and punishments,
assess the affairs and report to the orders,
and reiterate where rewards and punishments are applied.
If there is any inconsistency with what the orders specify,
even if there are achievements and benefits,
it is called autocracy,
a crime punishable by death without pardon.
Once the initial orders for the undertaking are issued,
then the undertaking can be initiated.
End of the initial undertaking.
Establish fire regulations,
respect mountains, marshes,
forests, thickets, and accumulated grasses;
where natural resources are produced,
regulate their closure and opening according to the season,
so that the people have enough for the use of their homes,
and accumulate firewood and kindling,
this is the duty of the Yúshī.
Drain floodwaters,
clear ditches and channels,
repair dams and barriers,
secure water storage,
so that even if seasonal waters are excessive,
they do not harm the five grains,
and even in years of severe drought,
there is something to harvest,
this is the duty of the Sīkōng.
Survey the high and low lands,
inspect the fertile and barren soils,
observe the suitability of the land,
clarify the times for decrees,
guide the farmers in sequence,
and regulate evenly according to the season,
so that the five grains, mulberries, and hemps
all thrive in their places,
this is the duty of the Sītián.
Tour the villages and hamlets,
inspect the homes,
observe the planting of trees,
select the six domestic animals,
and regulate evenly according to the season,
encourage and urge the common people,
to labor diligently without negligence,
cherish and enjoy their households,
and be reluctant to leave their hometowns,
this is the duty of the Xiāngshī.
Evaluate the various artisans,
examine the seasonal tasks,
distinguish between well-made and coarse work,
promote completeness and benefit,
oversee and unify the five districts,
and regulate evenly according to the season,
so that carved decorations and ornate patterns,
dare not be produced in the districts,
this is the duty of the Gōngshī.
End of the review of officials.
Determine clothing according to rank,
measure wealth according to salary.
Food and drink have their measures,
clothing has its regulations,
homes have their limits,
the six domestic animals and servants have their numbers,
boats, carriages, and displayed vessels have their restrictions.
In life, there are distinctions for carriages and caps, official robes and positions, grain salaries, lands, and residences;
in death, there are measures for inner and outer coffins, shrouds and coverings, graves and mounds.
Even if one has a worthy person or noble status,
without the rank
one dare not wear its clothing;
even if one has a wealthy family and abundant resources,
without the salary
one dare not use its wealth.
The Son of Heaven wears patterned robes with distinctions,
and the consort dare not wear them for leisure or to feast in the temple,
generals and high officials wear them to court,
officials and clerks by command,
scholars stop at sashes and trims.
Commoners dare not wear mixed colors,
artisans and merchants may not wear long fur or sable.
Those punished or disgraced dare not wear certain headgear, nor keep carriages with teams.
End of clothing regulations.
If the doctrine of disarming troops prevails,
then strategic points will not be defended.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to disarmament,
then the ministers and guests will not dare to speak of military affairs,
and thus internally they will not know the order or chaos of the state,
externally they will not know the strength or weakness of the feudal lords,
in such a case,
the city walls will be destroyed,
with no one to repair them,
armor will be worn out and weapons decayed,
with no one to maintain them.
In such a case,
the preparations for defense will be ruined.
Plans for distant lands,
the training of border soldiers,
and the people's will to defend against enemies will be lost;
hence it is said:
"If the doctrine of disarming troops prevails,
then strategic points will not be defended."
If the doctrine of universal love prevails,
then soldiers will not fight.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to universal love,
then he will see the people of the world as his own people,
and see other states as his own state,
in such a case,
there will be no intention to annex or seize,
no events of destroying armies or defeating generals.
But then archers, charioteers, and men of courage will not receive generous salaries,
ministers who destroy armies and kill generals will not be honored with ranks,
in such a case,
archers, charioteers, and men of courage will leave to serve abroad,
we may refrain from attacking others,
but cannot prevent others from attacking us,
if they demand land and we give it,
it is not what we desire,
if we do not give and instead fight,
we will surely not win.
They have trained officers,
we have driven masses,
they have excellent generals,
we have incompetence,
their defeat would mean the destruction of armies and loss of generals,
hence it is said:
"If the doctrine of universal love prevails,
then soldiers will not fight."
If the doctrine of preserving life prevails,
then integrity and shame will not be established.
If the ruler has no preference for preserving life,
then all ministers will preserve their lives,
and life further nurtures life,
what is this nurturing?
It is said:
"Flavors and delicacies,
music and beauty,"
then considered as nurturing life,
but then following desires and acting recklessly,
without distinction between men and women,
reverting to beasts,
then propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame are not established,
and the ruler has nothing to uphold himself with.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of preserving life prevails,
then integrity and shame are not established."
If the doctrine of private opinions and self-importance prevails,
then the ruler's commands are not carried out.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to private opinions and self-importance,
then the people will withdraw quietly and hide,
seeking caves in the mountains,
criticizing the world and superiors,
disdaining official ranks and salaries and looking down on officials,
then orders are not carried out,
and prohibitions are not enforced,
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of private opinions and self-importance prevails,
then the ruler's commands are not carried out."
If the doctrine of factions forming cliques prevails,
then the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to factions forming cliques,
then ministers will form cliques,
concealing the good and promoting the evil,
then the true situation of the state does not appear to the ruler,
thus,
those with cliques are placed in front,
those without cliques are placed behind;
when those with cliques are placed in front,
the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished,
then conflicts and struggles arise,
and the ruler is in danger;
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of factions forming cliques prevails,
then the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished."
If the doctrine of gold, jade, goods, and wealth prevails,
then official ranks and robes flow downward.
If the ruler only does not covet gold, jade, goods, and wealth,
he must desire to obtain what he likes,
then there must be something to exchange for it,
what is used to exchange for it?
High offices and尊贵 positions;
if not,
then尊贵 ranks and heavy salaries,
thus,
then the unworthy are in high positions.
Then the worthy will not serve below,
the wise will not offer plans,
the trustworthy will not make agreements,
the brave will not die for the cause,
thus,
then the state is driven to ruin;
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of gold, jade, goods, and wealth prevails,
then official ranks and robes flow downward."
If the doctrine of spectacles, music, and curios prevails,
then wicked people are in high positions.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to spectacles, music, and curios,
then he will not be ruined,
all spectacles and music,
palaces, towers, and ponds,
pearls, jade, music, and singing;
these all waste wealth and exhaust effort,
ways to harm the state,
and those who serve the ruler with these,
are all wicked people,
and if the ruler listens to them,
how can he avoid ruin?
Then the treasuries and granaries are empty,
accumulated stores exhausted;
moreover, with wicked people in high positions,
they block and suppress the worthy from advancing,
then when the state encounters troubles,
then actors and dwarfs rise to discuss state affairs,
this is driving the state to ruin;
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of spectacles, music, and curios prevails,
then wicked people are in high positions."
If the doctrine of requests and recommendations prevails,
then standards are not correct.
If the ruler only refrains from listening to requests and recommendations,
then all ministers will make requests for each other,
then requests are granted by the superior,
factions form in the countryside,
thus,
then bribes circulate in the state,
laws and regulations are destroyed by officials,
ministers strive to be clever and seek employment,
then there are those without rank who are尊贵,
without salary who are rich;
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of requests and recommendations
prevails,
then standards are not correct."
If the doctrine of flattery and covering up faults prevails,
then the cunning and artful are employed.
If the ruler only does not listen to flattering and fault-covering words,
then he will not be ruined,
how do we know this is so?
Flattering ministers,
often make their lord not regret his faults,
nor correct his errors.
Thus the lord is deluded and does not know himself,
thus,
then planning ministers die and flattering ministers are尊贵,
therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of flattery and covering up faults
prevails,
then the cunning and artful are employed."
Above are the nine causes of ruin.
Arriving when expected,
going when sent,
the people setting aside themselves and taking the superior as their heart,
this is what education aims for.
Beginning with what cannot be seen,
ending with what cannot be matched,
one person complies,
ten thousand people follow,
this is what training aims for.
Acting without being ordered,
going without being sent,
the superior not applying encouragement,
yet the people exhaust themselves fully,
this is what custom aims for.
Likes and dislikes formed in the heart,
the people transformed below,
punishments not yet carried out but the people fear,
rewards not yet given but the people are encouraged,
this is what sincerity and trust aim for.
Acting without harm,
succeeding without criticism,
gaining without anyone able to contend,
this is what the Way of Heaven aims for.
Doing and succeeding,
seeking and obtaining,
what the superior desires,
whether great or small, is always accomplished,
this is what affairs aim for.
Orders are carried out,
prohibitions are enforced,
wherever the law reaches,
wherever custom extends,
like the hundred limbs following the heart,
this is what governance aims for.
Above are the seven observations.
In establishing a capital city,
if not below a great mountain
then necessarily above a broad river.
High, not too close to drought
so that water supply is sufficient,
low, not too close to water
so that ditches and defenses are minimal.
Utilizing natural resources,
adapting to geographical advantages,
thus city walls need not conform to compass and square,
roads need not conform to level and line.
Above on establishing the state.
The non-active become emperors,
those who act without forcing become kings,
those who act without boasting become hegemons.
Not considering oneself尊贵,
this is the way of the ruler;
尊贵 without excess,
this is the way of the minister.
Above on the great principles.
Land is the foundation of governance,
the court is where righteousness is administered,
the market sets the standard for goods,
gold serves as the measure of expenditure,
and the territory of the feudal lords,
a state of a thousand chariots,
determines the system of implements.
These five principles can be understood,
and there is a way to implement them.
Land is the foundation of governance;
thus, land can rectify governance.
If land is not equitably distributed and harmonized,
then governance cannot be rectified.
If governance is not rectified,
then affairs cannot be properly managed.
Spring, autumn, winter, and summer
are the transitions of yīn and yáng;
the shortening and lengthening of seasons
are the utilization of yīn and yáng;
the alternation of day and night
is the transformation of yīn and yáng.
Thus, yīn and yáng are correct;
even if they are not,
what is excessive cannot be reduced,
and what is insufficient cannot be increased.
It is the way of heaven, and no one can reduce or increase it.
Therefore, what can rectify governance is land.
Hence, it must be rectified.
To rectify land,
its measurements must be correct.
Long is also correct,
short is also correct,
small is also correct,
large is also correct,
all lengths and sizes must be entirely correct.
If correctness is not maintained,
then officials cannot manage affairs;
if officials cannot manage affairs,
then matters cannot be handled;
if matters cannot be handled,
then goods will not be abundant.
How then can one know that goods are abundant?
It is said:
when affairs are well managed;
how can one know that affairs are well managed?
It is said:
when goods are abundant.
With abundant goods and well-managed affairs,
then what is demanded from the world is minimal.
There is a way to achieve this.
On yīn and yáng.
The court is where righteousness is administered.
Thus, when ranks and positions are correct, the people do not resent;
if the people do not resent,
there will be no disorder,
and then righteousness can be administered.
If not correct,
it cannot be
administered.
Therefore, not everyone in a state
can be noble,
for if all are noble,
then affairs will not be accomplished and the state will not benefit.
To prevent affairs from failing
and the state from suffering,
if there are no nobles,
then the people cannot govern themselves.
Thus, by distinguishing the honor and humility in the hierarchy of ranks,
one understands the sequence of precedence
and the principle of nobility and baseness.
There is a way to achieve this.
On ranks and positions.
The market sets the standard for goods.
Thus, if all goods are cheap,
then excessive profits cannot be gained;
if excessive profits cannot be gained,
then all affairs are well managed;
if all affairs are well managed,
then all expenditures are regulated.
Thus, affairs arise from deliberation,
are accomplished through diligence,
and fail through negligence.
Without deliberation, they do not arise;
without diligence, they are not accomplished;
without negligence, they do not fail.
Therefore, it is said:
the market can reveal order and disorder,
can show abundance and scarcity,
but cannot create abundance or scarcity.
There is a way to achieve this.
On market affairs.
Gold serves as the measure of expenditure.
By understanding the principle of gold,
one knows extravagance and frugality;
knowing extravagance and frugality,
then all expenditures are regulated.
Thus, frugality harms affairs,
while extravagance harms goods.
Frugality makes gold cheap,
and cheap gold means affairs are not accomplished,
hence harming affairs.
Extravagance makes gold expensive,
and expensive gold makes goods cheap,
hence harming goods.
Only when goods are exhausted does one realize insufficiency—
this is ignorance of measure;
only after affairs are completed
does one realize there is a surplus of goods—
this is ignorance of regulation.
Ignorance of measure
and ignorance of regulation are unacceptable.
This is called having a way.
Under heaven, when harnessing horses and oxen,
their load capacity has its limits.
With a journey of one night's stay,
the distance of the road has its measure.
Thus, knowing the territory of the feudal lords, a state of a thousand chariots,
is how one knows the size of the land,
and how one knows the weight of the burden.
To reduce only after it is too heavy
is ignorance of burden;
to increase only after it is too light
is ignorance of capacity.
Ignorance of burden and ignorance of capacity are unacceptable.
There is a way to achieve this.
Land that cannot be cultivated for food,
mountains without trees,
count as one for every hundred.
Dry marshes,
count as one for every hundred.
Land without grass or trees,
count as one for every hundred.
Where thorns and brambles grow thickly,
and people cannot enter,
count as one for every hundred.
Marshes,
where sickles and ropes can enter,
count as one for every nine.
Rolling hills,
where trees can be used for timber,
or for axles,
and where axes can enter,
count as one for every nine.
Steep mountains,
where trees can be used for coffins,
or for carts,
and where axes can enter,
count as one for every ten.
Flowing water,
where nets and traps can be used,
count as one for every five.
Forests,
where trees can be used for coffins,
or for carts,
and where axes can enter,
count as one for every five.
Marshes,
where nets and traps can be used,
count as one for every five.
This is called: land equalization
based on actual figures.
An area of six lǐ square
is called a bào,
five bào are called a bù,
five bù are called a jù.
A jù has a market,
without a market the people will be in want.
Five jù are called a certain xiāng,
four xiāng are called a fāng.
This is the administrative system.
When the administration is established, settlements are formed:
five households make a wǔ,
ten households make a lián,
five lián make a bào,
five bào make a zhǎng,
which is called a certain xiāng;
four xiāng are called a dū.
This is the settlement system.
When settlements are formed, affairs are regulated:
four jù make one lí,
five lí make one zhì,
five zhì make one tián,
two tián make one fū,
three fū make one jiā.
This is the system for affairs.
When affairs are regulated, equipment is organized:
an area of six lǐ square
is the land for one shèng.
One shèng
consists of four horses.
For one horse, there are seven armored soldiers,
and five shield bearers;
for one shèng,
there are twenty-eight armored soldiers,
twenty shield bearers,
and thirty unarmed attendants serving two chariots.
This is the system for equipment.
An area of six lǐ square
is the land for one shèng;
one lǐ square
is the farmland for nine fū.
One yì of gold
is the expense for one hundred shèng for one night.
If there is no gold, then silk is used instead,
with thirty-three zhì of seasonal silk equivalent to one yì.
If there is no silk, then cloth is used,
with one hundred liǎng of quán bào cloth equivalent to one yì.
One yì of gold
feeds one hundred shèng for one night.
Thus, the land allocated
yields one dǒu per six bù,
which is called an average year.
If there is a market, without a market
the people will be in want.
An area of six lǐ square
is named a shè,
and if it has a settlement,
it is named yāng.
This also involves taxes from passes and markets.
One hundred yì of gold makes one qiè,
and one gǔ lóng of goods is worth ten qiè,
with thirty merchants in the market,
in the first and twelfth months,
each paying one yì of gold.
This is called the zhēng.
In spring, it is called recording comparisons,
at the start of summer, monthly assessments,
in autumn, major inspections;
this tracks the population's increases and losses.
Every three years, boundaries are repaired,
every five years, borders are repaired,
every ten years, the system is renewed,
this is the constant regulation.
If water is seen at one rèn, there will be no great flood,
if at five chǐ, no great drought.
If water is seen at one rèn, taxes are reduced
by one-tenth; at two rèn, by two-tenths; at three
rèn, by three-tenths; at four rèn, by four-tenths;
at five rèn, by half,
comparable to mountains.
If water is seen at five chǐ,
taxes are reduced by one-tenth,
at four chǐ, by two-tenths,
at three chǐ, by three-tenths,
at two chǐ, by four-tenths,
at one chǐ, where water is seen,
comparable to marshes.
From outside the state gates,
to the extremities within the four borders,
each adult man works two plowings,
each child of five chǐ works one plowing,
as three days' labor.
In the first month,
farmers are ordered to begin work,
serving on the public fields for farming.
When the snow melts,
plowing begins,
and weeding ends.
Scholars, who are knowledgeable, widely
learned, and perceptive,
but do not serve as rulers or ministers,
contribute labor but do not share in the distribution.
Merchants, who know the prices of goods,
come to the market daily,
but are not official merchants,
contribute labor but do not share in the distribution.
Artisans, who refine appearances and skills,
come to the market daily,
but are not official artisans,
contribute labor but do not share in the distribution.
If they cannot be employed as artisans,
they are assessed based on the value of their goods and pay in grain.
Thus, what the wise understand,
the foolish do not,
cannot be taught to the people;
what the skilled can do,
the unskilled cannot,
cannot be taught to the people.
If the people do not comply with a single order,
one cannot achieve great goodness;
if not everyone can do it,
one cannot achieve great merit.
Therefore, insincere merchants shall not profit from trade,
insincere artisans shall not profit from craftsmanship,
insincere farmers shall not profit from farming,
untrustworthy scholars shall not stand in court.
Thus, offices remain vacant, yet none dare seek them,
the ruler possesses precious chariots and armor, yet none dare claim them,
when the ruler undertakes affairs,
ministers dare not falsely claim abilities they lack.
The ruler knows the ministers,
and the ministers know the ruler knows them.
Hence, none dare not exert their utmost, all bringing their sincerity forward.
The Way says:
Equalize land and divide labor,
so the people understand timing.
Then the people know the earliness or lateness of the seasons,
the insufficiency of days and months,
and how hunger and cold befall them.
Thus, they retire late and rise early,
fathers, sons, brothers
do not forget their tasks,
work without weariness,
and the people do not fear toil and hardship.
So, the harm of inequality is that
land's benefits cannot be fully utilized,
and the people's strength cannot be exhausted.
If not informed of the timing,
the people remain unaware;
if not guided in affairs,
the people remain inactive.
Share the produce with them,
and the people will know their due portion;
clarify their shares,
and the people will exert their full effort.
Thus, without coercion, fathers, sons, and brothers do not forget their tasks.
Above: Scholars, Farmers, Artisans, Merchants.
The reason sages are sages
is their skill in dividing among the people.
If a sage cannot divide among the people,
they are no different from common folk.
If they themselves are lacking,
how can they be called sages?
Thus, when there are tasks, resources are used;
when there are none, they are returned to the people.
Only the sage is skilled at entrusting enterprises to the people.
The nature of the people
is that when open, they are benevolent;
when closed, they become rebellious.
If the superior acts as one,
the subordinates will act as two.
Above: The Sage.
The timing of affairs is precise,
and cannot be stored away or discarded.
Hence it is said,
if nothing is done today,
goods will be lost tomorrow.
The days of the past have gone and will not return.
(On the right: Losing the opportunity.)
In the upper territories of eighty lǐ square,
there is one state with ten thousand households,
and four capitals with one thousand households.
In the middle territories of one hundred lǐ square,
there is one state with ten thousand households,
and four capitals with one thousand households.
In the lower territories of one hundred twenty lǐ square,
there is one state with ten thousand households,
and four capitals with one thousand households.
Taking the upper territories of eighty lǐ
and the lower territories of one hundred twenty lǐ,
they are equivalent to the middle territories of one hundred lǐ square.
(On the right: Geography.)
To affirm what is right but not establish it,
to deny what is wrong but not abolish it,
to have achievements but not reward them,
to have crimes but not punish them—
if one can govern the people under such conditions,
it has never happened.
What is right must be established,
what is wrong must be abolished,
achievements must be rewarded,
crimes must be punished;
can this ensure orderly governance?
Not yet.
Why is that?
It is said:
if the conditions and tools are not in place,
it is still ungovernable.
When conditions and tools are in place, and these four aspects are complete,
then it is governable.
One who cannot govern the people
but can strengthen their military
has never existed.
If one can govern the people,
but does not understand the methods of military preparation,
it is still not possible.
One who cannot strengthen their military
but can surely defeat enemy states
has never existed.
If one can strengthen their military,
but does not understand the principles of defeating enemy states,
it still leads to defeat.
One whose military is not certain to defeat enemy states
but can rectify the world
has never existed.
If the military is sure to defeat enemy states,
but one does not understand the proper division of rectifying the world,
it is still not possible.
Hence it is said:
Governing the people requires tools,
preparing the military requires methods,
defeating enemy states requires principles,
rectifying the world requires proper division.
Principles,
symbols,
laws,
transformation,
decisions and blockages,
mental techniques,
calculations and numbers:
Rooted in the qì of heaven and earth,
the harmony of cold and heat,
the nature of water and soil,
the life of people, birds, beasts, and plants,
though things are numerous,
all have balance,
and never change—
this is called "principles."
Righteousness,
names,
timing,
resemblance,
categories,
comparisons,
forms—
these are called "symbols."
Measurements of length,
ink lines,
compasses and squares,
weighing stones,
pecks and hú,
horn measures—
these are called "laws."
Gradual influence,
compliance,
refinement,
duration,
submission,
habituation—
these are called "transformation."
Giving and taking,
danger and ease,
benefit and harm,
difficulty and ease,
opening and closing,
killing and giving life—
these are called "decisions and blockages."
Substance,
sincerity,
generosity,
bestowal,
measurement,
forgiveness—
these are called "mental techniques."
Firmness and softness,
lightness and heaviness,
largeness and smallness,
solidity and emptiness,
distance and proximity,
abundance and scarcity—
these are called "calculations and numbers."
Without understanding principles,
yet wanting to set up instruments and draw up
systems,
is like setting a sundial on a moving wheel,
or trying to steady the tip of a leaning pole.
Without understanding symbols,
yet wanting to assess talents and employ them carefully,
is like cutting the long to make it short,
or joining the short to make it long.
Without understanding laws,
yet wanting to govern the people and unify the masses,
is like writing with the left hand while resting the right.
Without understanding transformation,
yet wanting to change customs and alter teachings,
is like shaping a wheel in the morning and wanting to ride in the carriage by evening.
Without understanding decisions and blockages,
yet wanting to drive the masses and relocate the people,
is like trying to make water flow backward.
Without understanding mental techniques,
yet wanting to issue commands to people,
is like turning away from the target and insisting on shooting it.
Without understanding calculations and numbers,
yet wanting to undertake great endeavors,
is like having no boat or oar yet wanting to cross treacherous waters.
Hence it is said:
To set up instruments and draw up systems,
not knowing principles is impossible;
to assess talents and employ them carefully,
not knowing symbols is impossible;
to govern the people and unify the masses,
not knowing laws is impossible;
to change customs and alter teachings,
not knowing transformation is impossible;
to drive the masses and relocate the people,
not knowing decisions and blockages is impossible;
to issue orders that must be carried out,
not knowing mental techniques is impossible;
to undertake endeavors that must succeed,
not knowing calculations and numbers is impossible.
(On the right: The Seven Methods.)
Various hidden evils harm the ruler's authority,
corrupt officials harm the laws of the office,
wicked people harm customs and teachings,
bandits and thieves harm the state's populace.
When authority is harmed,
power shifts downward;
when laws are harmed,
wealth flows upward;
when teachings are harmed,
those who follow orders do not cooperate;
when the populace is harmed,
the common people cannot live in peace.
With power shifted downward,
orders will not be carried out,
If goods flow upward, then official virtue is destroyed.
If those who follow orders are not harmonized,
then all endeavors will lack achievement.
If the common people cannot live in peace,
then the idle will stay while the diligent will scatter.
If the idle stay and the diligent scatter,
then the land will not be cultivated.
If the land is not cultivated,
then the six types of livestock will not be raised.
If the six types of livestock are not raised,
then the state will be poor and resources insufficient.
If the state is poor and resources insufficient,
then the military will be weak and soldiers not fierce.
If the military is weak and soldiers not fierce,
then battles cannot be won and defenses cannot be secured.
If battles cannot be won and defenses cannot be secured,
then the state will not be secure.
Therefore it is said:
If constant laws are not clear,
then all hidden evils will prevail.
If official ranks are not clear,
then treacherous officials will prevail.
If tallies and registers are not clear,
then treacherous people will prevail.
If penal laws are not clear,
then robbers and thieves will prevail.
When these four fundamental principles of the state are corrupted,
and the ruler is negligent, danger appears.
If the ruler is negligent,
then those who speak the truth will not come forward.
If those who speak the truth do not come forward,
then the true conditions of the state will not reach the ruler.
What ordinary rulers value are treasures;
what they are close to are relatives;
what they love are the people;
what they esteem are titles and emoluments.
An enlightened ruler is not like this.
What he values most are not treasures;
what he is closest to are not relatives;
what he loves most are not the people;
what he esteems most are not titles and emoluments.
Thus he does not compromise his commands for valuable treasures.
Therefore it is said:
"Commands are more precious than treasures."
He does not endanger his altars of soil and grain for the sake of loved ones.
Therefore it is said:
"The altars of soil and grain are closer than relatives."
He does not bend the law for the sake of loving people.
Therefore it is said:
"The law is more loved than people."
He does not share his authority for the sake of high ranks and emoluments.
Therefore it is said:
"Authority is weightier than ranks and emoluments."
If one does not comprehend these four principles,
then one reverts to having nothing.
Therefore it is said:
Governing people is like managing floodwaters;
nurturing people is like raising the six types of livestock;
employing people is like using plants and trees.
If in personal conduct one discusses the Way and practices reason,
then all ministers will obey instructions,
all officials will strictly adjudicate,
and none will dare to practice favoritism.
In evaluating achievements and calculating merits,
they never deviate from the laws.
Even favored courtiers,
close attendants,
powerful clans,
the honored and noble,
and high ministers
cannot have their achievements exaggerated.
Even the distant,
the lowly and humble,
and the obscure unknown people
will not have their labors forgotten.
Thus those who are guilty do not resent their superiors,
and those who receive rewards have no greedy hearts.
Then the soldiers in battle arrays
will all regard death lightly and face hardship calmly,
in order to accomplish their superiors' tasks—
this is the ultimate in military affairs.
Above: (Bǎi Nì) Four Harms.
The methods for military preparation:
lie in accumulating wealth,
so that wealth has no match;
lie in discussing craftsmanship,
so that craftsmanship has no match;
lie in manufacturing weapons,
so that weapons have no match;
lie in selecting soldiers,
so that soldiers have no match;
lie in administration and education,
so that administration and education have no match;
lie in training and practice,
so that training and practice have no match;
lie in comprehensive knowledge of the world,
so that comprehensive knowledge of the world has no match;
lie in understanding opportunities and strategies,
so that understanding opportunities and strategies has no match.
Thus, before the army has left the borders,
there are eight aspects without match.
Therefore, to rectify the world,
if one's wealth does not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If wealth surpasses the world's,
but craftsmanship does not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If craftsmanship surpasses the world's,
but weapons do not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If weapons surpass the world's,
but soldiers do not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If soldiers surpass the world's,
but education does not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If education surpasses the world's,
but training does not surpass the world's,
one cannot rectify the world.
If training surpasses the world's,
but one does not have comprehensive knowledge of the world,
one cannot rectify the world.
If one has comprehensive knowledge of the world,
but does not understand opportunities and strategies,
one cannot rectify the world.
Therefore, understanding opportunities and strategies
is the strategic advantage in using military force.
The great aspect is timing,
the small aspect is planning.
The Way of the King is not abandoned,
and none in the world dare to spy on it,
because of the king's correctness.
Balancing and storing
is the ritual of the Son of Heaven.
Therefore, when weapons are perfected and soldiers selected,
then the soldiers know they will be victorious.
With comprehensive knowledge of the world
and careful mastery of opportunities and strategies,
one can act alone and be without match.
For the countries one loves,
one exclusively benefits them;
for the countries one hates,
one exclusively harms them.
Then orders will be implemented and prohibitions observed.
Therefore, the sage kings valued this.
Defeat one and make a hundred submit—
then the world will fear you.
Establish few and influence many—
then the world will be drawn to you.
Punish the guilty
and reward the meritorious—
then the world will follow you.
Therefore, gather the finest wealth of the world,
discuss the sharpest weapons of all craftsmen.
In spring and autumn, hold competitive trials
for training,
with the elite and sharpest being superior.
Finished weapons not inspected are not used,
not tested are not stored.
Gather the outstanding talents of the world,
possess the heroes and champions of the world.
Then raising them is like flying birds,
moving them is like thunder and lightning,
deploying them is like wind and rain.
None can stand before them,
none can harm them behind.
They advance and withdraw alone,
with none daring to stop or obstruct them.
To achieve success and establish affairs,
one must conform to principles and righteousness.
Thus, without principles, one cannot prevail over the world;
without righteousness, one cannot overcome others.
Therefore, a wise and knowledgeable ruler
must position himself in an invincible situation,
so he can rectify the world with none daring to resist him.
The above discusses the methods of military affairs.
As for flexible organization and timely actions,
do not miss the opportune moments of heaven,
nor neglect the advantages of earth.
The numbers and quantities,
their essence must stem from calculation.
Thus, in the way of attack and campaign,
plans must first be settled internally,
then troops can be sent beyond the borders.
If plans are not settled internally
and troops are sent beyond the borders,
this means fighting leads to self-defeat,
attacking results in self-destruction.
Hence, deploying armies but being unable to fight,
besieging cities but being unable to attack,
gaining territory but being unable to secure it—
if any one of these three appears,
then defeat and destruction can follow.
Thus, without understanding the enemy's governance,
one cannot engage them;
without understanding the enemy's situation,
one cannot make agreements;
without understanding the enemy's generals,
one should not advance the army;
without understanding the enemy's troops,
one should not form battle lines.
Therefore, using many to strike few,
order to strike chaos,
wealth to strike poverty,
capability to strike incapability,
trained soldiers and drilled troops to strike motley crowds and raw recruits—
thus ten battles bring ten victories,
a hundred battles bring a hundred victories.
Thus, if affairs lack preparation,
troops have no leadership,
then early knowledge is impossible;
if fields are not cultivated,
lands have no officials,
then there will be no reserves;
if offices lack constancy,
subordinates resent superiors,
then equipment will not be effective;
if the court lacks governance,
then rewards and punishments are unclear;
if rewards and punishments are unclear,
then the people rely on luck for survival.
Thus, knowing the enemy early allows independent action,
having reserves
enables endurance without exhaustion,
effective equipment
allows campaigning without waste,
clear rewards and punishments
mean the people do not rely on luck
for survival,
and when people do not rely on luck
for survival,
then brave warriors are encouraged.
Therefore, in military affairs,
scrutinize the maps of the land,
consult the celestial officials,
measure the reserves,
unite the brave warriors,
comprehend the world thoroughly,
and carefully control opportunities and strategies—
these are the tasks of the military leader.
With movements like wind and rain,
thus one can cover long distances without hindrance.
With advances like flying birds,
thus one can traverse mountains and rivers without peril.
With battles like thunder and lightning,
thus one can act alone and be invincible.
With effects like flood and drought,
thus one can attack states and rescue cities.
With defenses like a metal wall,
thus one can secure the ancestral temples,
and nurture sons and daughters.
With governance as one integrated body,
thus one can issue commands
and clarify laws and regulations.
Movements like wind and rain
mean speed.
Advances like flying birds
mean lightness.
Battles like thunder and lightning
mean the troops are not aligned.
Effects like flood and drought
mean fields are not harvested,
plowing yields no gain.
Defenses like a metal wall
involve using wealth,
and setting up spies.
Governance as one integrated body
means eliminating strange doctrines,
and prohibiting extravagant customs.
Covering long distances without hindrance,
thus one can awe the people of remote regions.
Traversing mountains and rivers without peril,
thus one can subdue states relying on strong defenses.
Acting alone and being invincible,
thus orders are followed and prohibitions heeded.
Thus, in attacking states and rescuing cities,
one does not rely on allied states,
so wherever directed, they must obey.
Securing the ancestral temples,
nurturing sons and daughters,
with none in the world able to harm them,
only then can one possess a state.
Establishing regulations and laws,
issuing commands,
with none failing to respond,
only then can one govern the people and unify the masses.
In general, to establish affairs,
correct that heavenly planting,
the model laws
emulate the positions of heaven and earth,
imitate the movements of the four seasons,
to govern the world.
The movements of the four seasons,
have cold and heat,
the sage emulates them,
thus there are civil and military aspects.
The positions of heaven and earth,
have front and back,
left and right,
the sage emulates them,
to establish order and principles.
Spring gives birth on the left,
autumn executes on the right,
summer grows in the front,
winter stores in the back.
The affairs of growth and life
are civil;
the affairs of storage and execution
are military;
thus civil affairs are on the left,
military affairs on the right,
the sage emulates this.
To implement laws and orders,
and manage affairs with reason.
In all legal matters,
the handling must be correct;
if handling is incorrect,
then adjudication is unfair;
if adjudication is unfair,
then governance does not fully follow reason.
Affairs are not fully responsive;
if governance does not fully follow reason,
then the distant and lowly have nowhere to appeal;
if affairs are not fully responsive,
then benefits and achievements are not fully realized;
if benefits and achievements are not fully realized,
then the state becomes poor and distant.
If the lowly have nowhere to appeal, then the people suffer;
thus it is said:
"In general, to establish affairs,
correct that heavenly planting";
heavenly planting
is the heart;
if heavenly planting is correct,
then one does not favor close relatives,
nor harm the distant;
not favoring close relatives,
nor harming the distant,
then no benefits are overlooked,
no governance is hidden;
no benefits overlooked,
no governance hidden,
then affairs are fully accomplished,
and nothing is left out.
Neither wind nor rain fails its duty,
whether far or near, high or low,
each receives its proper succession.
To understand the heart of Heaven,
it is clearly shown through wind and rain.
Hence it is said:
"Neither wind nor rain fails its duty,
whether far or near, high or low,
each receives its proper succession."
When the three guiding principles are well-ordered,
the ruler possesses the state.
All things honor Heaven,
and value wind and rain.
The reason they honor Heaven
is because nothing fails to receive its mandate from it.
The reason they value wind and rain
is because nothing moves without awaiting the wind,
and nothing is moistened without awaiting the rain.
If all things were to abandon Heaven and receive their mandate elsewhere,
abandon wind and look elsewhere for movement,
abandon rain and look elsewhere for moisture,
then there would be no reason to honor Heaven and value wind and rain.
Now what makes a ruler secure in his dignity
is that his authority is established and his commands are carried out.
The reason he can establish authority and enforce commands
is that the control of power and benefit lies entirely with the ruler.
If control of power and benefit is not exclusively with the ruler,
but is dispersed elsewhere,
then the ruler becomes increasingly insignificant,
and his authority and benefits daily decline—
this is the path to encroachment and violence.
Hence it is said:
"When the three guiding principles are well-ordered,
the ruler possesses the state."
Do not reward out of personal joy,
nor execute out of personal anger.
Rewarding out of joy,
executing out of anger—
this gives rise to resentment,
and commands are abandoned.
When repeated commands go unheeded,
the people's hearts turn outward.
When they form factions externally,
calamity begins to sprout.
What the masses resent,
the few cannot control.
As summer approaches its fullness,
carefully administer punishments and rewards—
principles must be clearly defined.
Set forth righteousness and establish laws,
decide matters with reason.
Empty your spirit and calm your heart,
then discard anger and joy.
If you violate laws and abandon commands,
acting on anger and joy,
disorder and calamity will arise,
and the ruler's position will be endangered.
Hence it is said:
"Do not reward out of personal joy,
nor execute out of personal anger."
Rewarding out of joy,
executing out of anger—
this gives rise to resentment,
and commands are abandoned.
When repeated commands go unheeded,
the people's hearts turn outward.
When they form factions externally,
calamity begins to sprout.
What the masses resent,
the few cannot control.
When promoting what you admire,
you must observe its final outcome;
when abolishing what you dislike,
you must consider its ultimate consequences.
In winter, when all is stored away,
all activities cease,
past affairs are fully concluded,
and future affairs have not yet begun.
While winter brings no pressing matters,
carefully examine beginnings and ends,
and scrutinize the principles of affairs.
Some matters appear easy at first but become difficult later;
some show little promise at the start but achieve unreachable success in the end.
This is why constant benefits often go unrealized,
and why affairs often end in困境.
When matters seem easy at first,
people undertake them lightly;
undertaking them lightly,
they inevitably encounter difficulties in achieving success.
When beginnings show little promise,
people abandon them lightly;
abandoning them lightly,
they inevitably lose the chance for unreachable achievements.
Frequently encountering difficulties in completing tasks,
while constantly missing opportunities for unreachable achievements—
this is the path to decline and exhaustion.
Therefore,
an enlightened ruler scrutinizes the principles of affairs,
carefully examines beginnings and ends,
so that in acting he must know what will be accomplished,
in accomplishment he must know its utility,
and in utility he must know its benefits and harms.
To act without knowing what will be accomplished,
to accomplish without knowing its utility,
to utilize without knowing its benefits and harms—
this is called reckless action.
In reckless action,
the affair is not accomplished,
and the achievement is not established.
Hence it is said:
"When promoting what you admire,
you must observe its final outcome.
When abolishing what you dislike,
you must consider its ultimate consequences."
Reward the diligent and reverent to honor them,
enrich the meritorious to encourage them,
and ennoble the renowned to glorify them.
All rulers
desire that their people possess ritual and righteousness.
If the people lack ritual and righteousness,
then high and low will be disordered, and noble and base will contend.
Hence it is said:
"Reward the diligent and reverent to honor them,
enrich the meritorious to encourage them,
and ennoble the renowned to glorify them."
Universal love without omission—
this is called the ruler's heart.
First there must be obedient instruction,
then the myriad people will follow the influence,
benefiting from morning till night,
and the masses will become competent.
All rulers
desire that the masses be attached to their superiors and inclined to their intentions,
and that they be competent in their tasks.
But if the masses are not loved,
they will not be attached;
if not attached,
they will not be enlightened.
Without obedient instruction,
they will not incline to your intentions.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler practices universal love to draw them close,
and provides clear instruction to guide them,
easing their circumstances,
benefiting their preparations,
cherishing their strength,
and not depriving them of their seasons to their benefit.
Thus,
the masses will be attached to their superiors and inclined to their intentions,
and competent in their tasks.
Hence it is said:
"Universal love without omission"
is called the ruler's heart. First there must be obedient instruction,
then the myriad people will follow the influence.
Benefiting from morning till night,
the masses will become competent.
Employ others as you would yourself,
accomplish tasks with substance.
The foundation of governance has two aspects:
first, people;
second, affairs.
People must be employed as needed,
affairs must be accomplished with skill.
People may be compliant or resistant,
affairs require proper measurement.
If people's hearts are resistant,
they cannot be employed.
If affairs lack proper measurement,
they cannot be accomplished skillfully.
Unskillful accomplishment brings harm,
unemployed people bring resentment.
Hence it is said:
"Employ others as you would yourself,
accomplish tasks with substance."
Scrutinize the use of resources,
be cautious in bestowing and repaying,
and examine the balance of measures.
Therefore, in using resources, one must not be stingy,
and in exerting effort, one must not be harsh.
Using resources stingily leads to waste,
exerting effort harshly leads to exhaustion.
To accomplish tasks with substance,
one must use proper measures.
To select people based on oneself,
is to act with empathetic consideration.
Empathetic consideration means
measuring by one's own standards.
What one finds discomforting oneself,
should not be imposed on others;
Hence it is said:
"Scrutinize the use of resources,
be cautious in bestowing and repaying,
and examine the balance of measures.
Therefore, in using resources, one must not be stingy,
and in exerting effort, one must not be harsh,
using resources stingily leads to waste,
exerting effort harshly leads to exhaustion."
When the people are impoverished,
decrees become disgraceful;
when the people suffer calamity,
decrees cannot be enforced.
When bestowals and repayments are not received,
calamities begin to flourish;
if calamities flourish unawares,
the people will take matters into their own hands.
How do we know this is so?
Exerting effort harshly makes tasks unskillful; unskillful tasks
require repeated redoing, hence called exhaustion. Using resources stingily
fails to satisfy people's hearts; failing to satisfy people's hearts
gives rise to resentment. Using resources yet breeding resentment,
hence called waste. Resentment arises
and does not revert; the masses labor
without rest,
then surely there will be thoughts of collapse and ruin.
Hence it is said: "When the people are impoverished, decrees
become disgraceful; when the people suffer calamity, decrees cannot be enforced. When bestowals and repayments are not received, calamities
begin to flourish; if calamities flourish
unawares, the people will take matters into their own hands."
Upright laws and straight measures,
punishing crimes without pardon,
executions and penalties must be trustworthy,
so the people fear and dread.
Once martial authority is clear,
decrees need not be issued twice.
Any state without laws
leaves the masses not knowing what to do.
Without measures,
affairs lack mechanism.
Having laws but not upright,
having measures but not straight,
leads to biased governance,
biased governance causes state disorder;
Hence it is said:
"Upright laws and straight measures,
punishing crimes without pardon.
Executions and penalties must be trustworthy,
so the people fear and dread.
Once martial authority is clear,
decrees need not be issued twice."
Reprimand the lazy and weary to shame them,
punish crimes and pardon
mistakes to discipline them,
execute and penalize offenders to震慑 them.
All people dislike punishment and fear crime,
thus the ruler uses strict teachings to demonstrate,
and clear penalties to enforce;
Hence it is said:
"Reprimand the lazy and weary to shame them,
punish crimes and pardon
mistakes to discipline them,
execute and penalize offenders to震慑 them."
Firmly planted and unmoving,
deviant forces then fear.
When deviant changes are curbed,
decrees go forth and the people follow.
Governing a state has three tools,
disordering a state has six assaults,
an enlightened ruler can overcome the six assaults and establish the three tools,
then the state is governed,
an unworthy ruler cannot overcome the six assaults and establish the three tools,
thus the state is not governed.
What are the three tools?
They are:
"Commands, the axe of authority, and official rewards."
What are the six assaults?
They are: kinship, nobility, wealth, beauty,
flattery, and amusements.
How are the three tools used?
It is said:
"Without commands, there is no way to direct subordinates,
without the axe of authority, there is no way to awe the masses,
without official rewards, there is no way to encourage the people."
How do the six assaults cause ruin?
It is said:
"Even if disobeying, one can still survive,
even if violating prohibitions, one can still be exempt,
even without merit, one can still become wealthy;"
If in a state, there are those who disobey yet can survive,
then commands are insufficient to direct subordinates.
If there are those who violate prohibitions yet can be exempt,
then the axe of authority is insufficient to awe the masses.
If there are those without merit who can become wealthy,
then official rewards are insufficient to encourage the people;
if commands are insufficient to direct subordinates,
the axe of authority insufficient to awe the masses,
official rewards insufficient to encourage the people,
then the ruler has nothing to secure himself with;
Then what should an enlightened ruler do?
The enlightened ruler does not change commands for the six,
does not hesitate or misplace the axe of authority for the six,
does not increase or decrease official rewards for the six;
Hence it is said:
"Firmly planted and unmoving,
deviant forces then fear.
When deviant changes are curbed,
decrees go forth and the people follow."
Emulate Heaven and unite with virtue,
imitate Earth and show no favoritism.
All rulers
shelter and carry the myriad people, possessing them all,
illuminate and oversee all clans, employing and directing them;
Therefore, they take Heaven, Earth, sun, moon, and the four seasons as their basis and substance,
to govern the world.
Heaven covers all without exclusion.
Its virtue is omnipresent;
Earth carries all without abandonment,
secure and firm, unmoving;
Thus all things multiply and grow.
Sages emulate this,
to shelter and carry the myriad people,
so all obtain their proper nature and duties,
obtaining their proper nature and duties;
then all become useful;
Hence it is said:
"Emulate Heaven and unite with virtue,
imitate Earth and show no favoritism,"
Align with the sun and moon,
assist with the four seasons.
The brightness of the sun and moon is impartial,
so all receive light;
Sages emulate this,
to illuminate the myriad people,
thus able to scrutinize thoroughly,
leaving no good unrecognized.
No villainy hidden.
No good unrecognized,
no villainy hidden,
then punishments and rewards are trustworthy and certain;
punishments and rewards trustworthy and certain,
then goodness is encouraged and villainy stops;
Hence it is said:
"Align with the sun and moon."
The operation of the four seasons,
trustworthy, certain, and clearly manifest,
Sages emulate this,
to serve the myriad people,
thus not missing timely achievements,
Hence it is said:
"Coordinate with the four seasons."
Joy lies in bestowing,
gaining the masses lies in abolishing selfishness.
As for the masses,
love them and they become close,
benefit them and they come;
Therefore, the enlightened ruler sets up benefits to attract them,
and demonstrates love to draw them close;
If only benefiting without loving,
the masses come but are not close;
If there is only affection without benefit,
then the masses will be close but not come;
when both affection and beneficence are practiced,
then rulers and ministers are pleased,
friends are pleased, brothers are pleased, fathers and sons are pleased,
where affection and beneficence are established,
even fourfold fortifications cannot hold;
therefore it is said:
"The key lies in affection and beneficence."
Generally, the reason why a ruler can have the masses,
is due to the virtue of affection and beneficence,
if affection shifts elsewhere,
and benefits become concentrated,
then one cannot fully possess them;
therefore it is said:
"To have the masses lies in abolishing selfishness."
Attracting the distant lies in cultivating the near,
the virtue of affection and beneficence,
though practiced without selfishness,
if internal conduct is not cultivated,
then one cannot make the rulers of distant lands pay homage;
therefore, by rectifying the principles between ruler and minister, superior and inferior,
adorning the principles between father and son, brothers and husband and wife,
adorning the distinctions between men and women,
differentiating the gaps between closeness and distance,
making the ruler virtuous and ministers loyal,
fathers kind and sons filial,
elder brothers loving and younger brothers respectful,
with ritual and righteousness clearly manifest,
thus,
those nearby will be affectionate,
and those far away will submit,
therefore it is said:
"Attracting the distant lies in cultivating the near,"
preventing calamity lies in eliminating resentment.
Preventing calamity lies in eliminating resentment
not that there is resentment then eliminate it where affairs occur
but constantly having no resentment at all. Generally, calamity
and disorder arise
from resentment and blame;
resentment and blame
arise from
unreasonableness. Therefore, an enlightened ruler in managing the masses must carefully employ them,
must guide with reciprocity,
must speak appropriately,
must have punishments
that are reasonable.
Thus the masses
will have no suppressed resentment in their hearts,
no regretful or hateful intentions.
In this way,
calamity and disorder do not arise,
and the ruler's position is not endangered. Therefore it is said: preventing calamity lies in eliminating resentment.
Preparing for the long term lies in employing the worthy,
generally, the reason why a ruler is respected and secure,
is due to worthy assistants;
if assistants are worthy,
then the ruler is honored, the state secure, and the people orderly;
without assistants,
then the ruler is demeaned, the state endangered, and the people chaotic;
therefore it is said:
"Preparing for the long term lies in employing the worthy."
High security lies in sharing benefits.
Generally, all people desire benefit and detest harm,
therefore, one who shares benefits with the world,
is upheld by the world.
One who monopolizes the world's benefits,
is conspired against by the world.
One conspired against by the world,
though established, will surely fall.
One upheld by the world,
though high, is not endangered.
Therefore it is said:
"Security in high position lies in sharing benefits."

forms generate and principles emerge.
Abiding in emptiness and maintaining stillness,
with people and things ordered, then imperial.
Constantly reaching the mandate,

Personally benevolent and practicing righteousness,

Examining plans and displaying ritual,

Securing life and managing death,

Trustworthy rewards and careful punishments,

Calculating totals and attending to outcomes,

Connect them with the Way,
nurture them with kindness,

With one move, superiors and inferiors achieve their ends,
with two moves, the people all follow,
with three moves, land is opened and grain ripens,
with four moves, farmers rest and grain increases tenfold,
with five moves, labor lightens and metal multiplies ninefold,
with six moves, clearly understanding affairs and changes,
with seven moves, internal and external are utilized,
with eight moves, victories prevail and authority is established,
with nine moves, imperial affairs take form.
The nine foundations are broad and great,
they are the ruler's responsibility.
The eight divisions with their duties,
are the ministers' responsibility.
The seven victories fully prepared with authority,
are the general's responsibility.
The six principles carefully detailed,
are the worthy's responsibility.
The five disciplines not neglected,
are the common people's responsibility.
In action, none fail to follow,
in stillness, none fail to harmonize.
The roots of order and chaos are three,
the interactions of low and high are four,
the outcomes of wealth and poverty are five,
the principles of prosperity and decline are six,
the pivots of safety and danger are seven,
the responses of strength and weakness are eight,
the numbers of survival and destruction are nine.
Train them by dispersing groups and organizing offices,
generally managing resources and offices.
Execute offenders to gather wealth,
encourage and urge to move the masses,
make these two aspects both have their basis.
Initiating goodness must be carefully secret,
wielding authority must be clear at the center.
This resides in the center of the diagram square.

The way to win people's hearts
is none other than to benefit them;
The way to benefit them
is none other than to instruct them through governance.
Thus, those skilled in governance
see fields cultivated and cities prosperous,
courts serene and offices orderly,
public laws upheld and private crookedness ceased,
granaries full and prisons empty,
worthy men advanced and wicked people dismissed.
Their nobles value integrity and despise flattery;
their scholars and people prize martial courage and scorn undue profit;
their commoners favor farming and dislike excessive feasting.
Thus, wealth and resources suffice,
and food, drink, firewood, and vegetables abound.
Therefore, the rulers must be generous
and grant remissions,
the people must obey
without resentment or complaint,
superiors and inferiors harmonize
with ritual and righteousness,
hence dwell in security and act with authority,
win battles and defend firmly,
thus in one campaign rectifying the feudal lords.
Those incapable in governance
see fields barren and cities desolate,
courts turbulent and offices chaotic,
public laws abandoned and private crookedness rampant,
granaries empty and prisons full,
worthy men dismissed and wicked people advanced.
Their nobles value flattery and despise integrity;
their scholars and people prize undue profit and scorn martial courage;
their commoners favor feasting and dislike farming.
Thus, wealth and resources dwindle,
and food, drink, firewood, and vegetables are scarce.
Rulers become more cruel and oppressive
without remissions,
people grow more defiant and disobedient,
superiors and inferiors conflict without harmony,
hence dwelling in insecurity and acting without authority,
losing battles and defending weakly.
Thus the lesser suffer military defeat and territorial loss,
the greater face personal death and state destruction.
Therefore, from this perspective,
governance must be undertaken with caution.
Virtue has six promotions,
righteousness has seven embodiments,
ritual has eight constants,
law has five duties,
authority has three measures.
What are called the six promotions?
It is said:
Open up fields and farmlands,
regulate dwellings and estates,
cultivate trees and arts,
encourage scholars and people,
urge on farming and harvesting,
repair walls and houses—
this is called enriching their livelihood.
Develop hidden benefits,
transport stored surpluses, repair roads and paths,
facilitate passes and markets,
carefully manage lodging and stays—
Channel the waterways,
maintain the banks and ditches,
dredge the silted islets,
clear the stagnant mud,
open the blocked passages,
and carefully manage the ferries and bridges—
this is called providing them with benefits.
Reduce taxes and levies,
lighten the burdens of tribute,
relax the penal codes,
pardon crimes and offenses,
and forgive minor faults—
this is called easing their governance.
Support the elderly,
cherish the young and orphaned,
comfort the widowed and solitary,
inquire after the sick,
and mourn with the bereaved—
this is called relieving their urgent needs.
Clothe the freezing,
feed the hungry and thirsty,
aid the impoverished,
relieve the destitute and exposed,
and supply the desperate and deprived—
this is called succoring their poverty.
All these six aspects
are the means to promote virtue.
Once these six are implemented,
then the people's desires
will all be fulfilled.
Only when the people's desires are met
will they heed their superiors;
heeding their superiors,
then governance can be well executed.
Thus it is said:
Virtue must be promoted.
It is said:
When the people understand virtue,
but do not yet know righteousness,
then demonstrate conduct to guide them to righteousness.
Righteousness has seven embodiments.
What are these seven embodiments?
They are:
Filial piety, fraternal duty, kindness, and benevolence
to support one's family;
respect, reverence, loyalty, and trustworthiness
to serve one's ruler;
uprightness, fairness, and appropriateness
to practice ritual and moderation;
orderliness, restraint, and humility
to avoid punishment and disgrace;
frugality and thrift in expenditure
to prepare for famine;
sincerity, simplicity, and steadfastness
to guard against calamity and chaos;
harmony, cooperation, and amity
to defend against invasion and warfare.
All these seven aspects
are the embodiments of righteousness.
The people must understand righteousness to be upright and fair,
being upright and fair leads to harmony and coordination,
harmony and coordination enable them to dwell in peace,
dwelling in peace then allows for mobilization of authority,
and mobilizing authority enables victory in battle and secure defense.
Thus it is said: Righteousness must be practiced.
It is said:
When the people understand righteousness,
but do not yet know ritual,
then adorn the eight principles to guide them to ritual.
What are these eight principles?
They are:
Superiors and inferiors have their propriety,
the noble and the humble have their distinctions,
the elder and the younger have their hierarchy,
the poor and the rich have their measures.
All these eight aspects
are the principles of ritual.
Thus, if superiors and inferiors lack propriety, there is chaos;
if the noble and the humble lack distinctions, there is conflict;
if the elder and the younger lack hierarchy, there is rebellion;
if the poor and the rich lack measures, there is loss.
With chaos between superiors and inferiors,
conflict between noble and humble,
rebellion between elder and younger,
and loss between poor and rich,
for a state not to fall into disorder—
such a thing has never been heard of.
Therefore, the sage kings adorned these eight rituals
to guide their people.
When all eight are properly realized,
then the ruler
is upright and impartial,
the ministers
are loyal and trustworthy without factionalism,
the father
is kind and benevolent in teaching,
the son
is filial and respectful in solemnity,
the elder brother
is tolerant and generous in instruction,
the younger brother
is obedient and reverent,
the husband
is sincere and steadfast,
the wife
is diligent and chaste.
Thus, inferiors do not rebel against superiors,
ministers do not slay their ruler,
the humble do not surpass the noble,
the young do not oppress the old,
the distant do not alienate the close,
the new do not alienate the old,
the small do not override the great,
and licentiousness does not undermine righteousness.
All these eight aspects
are the principles of ritual.
One must understand ritual to be respectful,
being respectful leads to deference and yielding,
deference and yielding prevent the young and old, noble and humble from overstepping their bounds,
and when the young and old, noble and humble do not overstep their bounds,
then chaos does not arise and disasters do not occur.
Thus it is said: Ritual must be carefully observed.
It is said:
When the people understand ritual,
but do not yet know their duties,
then promulgate laws to assign responsibilities.
There are five duties in assigning responsibilities.
What are these five duties?
They are:
The ruler selects ministers and appoints officials,
the great officers serve in office and manage affairs,
the officials undertake tasks and uphold their duties,
the scholars cultivate themselves and develop talents,
the common people farm and plant crops.
When the ruler selects ministers and appoints officials,
then affairs are not chaotic;
when the great officers serve in office and manage affairs,
then actions are timely;
when the officials undertake tasks and uphold their duties,
then movements are harmonious;
when the scholars cultivate themselves and develop talents,
then the worthy and virtuous emerge;
when the common people farm and plant crops,
then resources are sufficient.
Thus it is said:
All these five aspects
are the duties of effort.
The people must know their duties,
then their minds become unified,
unified minds lead to concentrated will,
and with unified minds and concentrated will,
then achievements become worthy of admiration.
Thus it is said:
Effort must be diligently pursued.
It is said:
When the people know their duties,
but do not yet know assessment,
then examine the three measures to guide their actions.
What are these three measures?
They are:
Assess the auspiciousness of heaven above,
assess the suitability of earth below,
and assess the harmony of humanity in between—
these are called the three measures.
Thus it is said:
If the heavenly timing is inauspicious,
there will be floods and droughts;
if the earthly conditions are unsuitable,
there will be famines;
if human relations are disharmonious,
there will be calamities and chaos.
The arrival of these three
is summoned by governance.
It is said:
Assess the timing to initiate affairs,
use affairs to mobilize the people,
use the people to mobilize the state,
use the state to mobilize the world.
When the world is mobilized,
then achievements and fame can be accomplished.
Thus, the people must understand strategic judgment,
then actions can be appropriate;
when actions are appropriate, the people will be harmonious and united,
when the people are harmonious and united, achievements and fame are established.
Therefore, it is said:
Strategic judgment must be measured.
Once the five regulations are promulgated,
then pursue the wicked people,
investigate deceit and fraud,
banish slander and evil,
and do not listen to corrupting words,
do not create extravagant crafts.
If the people have corrupt conduct and depraved nature,
propagate corrupting words,
create extravagant crafts,
to flatter the ruler above
and delude the common people below,
shaking the state and stirring the masses,
harming the people's livelihoods,
their punishment shall be death or exile.
Hence it is said,
Whenever a ruler loses the people internally,
loses the feudal lords externally,
suffers military defeats and territorial reductions,
his reputation humbled and his state weakened,
the altars of land and grain destroyed,
and his person endangered,
it has never been heard that this did not arise from corruption and flattery.
How do we know this is so?
It is said,
corrupt sounds please the ear,
corrupt sights please the eye.
What the ears and eyes favor, pleases the heart.
What the heart favors, harms the people.
It has never been heard that when the people are harmed, the ruler's person is not endangered.
It is said:
Fill the wastelands,
cultivate the fields,
repair walls and houses,
then the state will be wealthy;
moderate in eating and drinking,
be frugal with clothing,
then resources will be sufficient;
promote the worthy and virtuous,
focus on merits and achievements,
spread virtue and kindness,
then the worthy will advance;
expel the wicked,
investigate deceit and fraud,
remove slander and evil,
then the wicked will cease;
prepare for famine,
relieve disasters,
aid the destitute and exposed,
then the state will be stable.
The tasks of an enlightened king
lie in strengthening fundamental endeavors,
eliminating the useless,
then the people can be made prosperous;
evaluate the worthy,
employ the capable,
and the people can be made orderly;
lighten taxes,
do not oppress the people,
treat them with loyalty and care,
and the people can be made close.
These three
are the affairs of a hegemon or true king.
Affairs have their roots,
and benevolence and righteousness are their essence.
Now, artisans are skilled,
yet the people lack adequate supplies,
the delight is in curios and luxuries;
farmers labor,
yet the world suffers hunger,
the delight is in rare delicacies;
women are skillful,
yet the world suffers cold,
the delight is in embroidered finery.
Therefore, broad sashes are pared down,
large sleeves are reduced,
embroideries are dyed plain,
carvings are cut away,
engravings are smoothed,
passes are inspected but not taxed,
market stalls are provided but not levied.
The good artisans of old
did not weary their wisdom and skill for curios.
Thus, useless objects
are not produced by those who uphold the law.
On the left, grasp the five tones,
on the right, hold the five flavors.
Embrace the marking-line and the compass-square,
fully prepare the compass and axle,
reduce flow to achieve great completion,
this is the node of timely virtue.
In spring, gather the young,
in autumn, gather the fruits,
in summer, dwell in shade,
in winter, dwell in warmth,
the virtue of the great worthy endures.
Clarity leads to wisdom,
wisdom leads to clarity,
vigor leads to tranquility,
clarity and wisdom lead to great conduct.
Endure poison without anger,
hold resentment without words,
have desires without scheming.
Greatly measure and model,
as if waking from sleep,
as if distinguishing dark and light,
as if Ao was under Yáo.
Do not consult the cunning,
do not harbor the flatterers,
do not nurture the vicious,
do not mirror the slanderers.
If not correct, expand its wasteland.
Do not use their petty means.
Birds fly by the marking-line.
Investigate fully and balance the extremes,
simplify governance and benefit the people.
Do not incur their calamity,
do not approach their demands,
but keep their worries distant.
If dwelling is made lofty,
danger at the peak, none can save it.
Can be shallow or deep,
can float or sink,
can be curved or straight,
can speak or be silent;
heaven does not have one season only,
earth does not have one benefit only,
humans do not have one affair only.
Can be upright in vision,
steady in step,
deep in traces.
For heaven and earth have both danger and ease,
as a drum has its drumstick,
when poked, it strikes.
Heaven and earth are the sack of all things,
the scope of the universe contains heaven and earth.
"On the left, grasp the five tones,
