facing mountains, with left and right
bordered by rivers or lakes,
internally constructing drainage channels,
leading into major rivers and discharging there.
The land, with its natural resources and produce,
benefits and nourishes the people, rearing the six domestic animals.
The people under the Son of Heaven,
all submit to his virtue and cherish his righteousness.
Then, separate and demarcate it:
what is called a district is a 'shù',
smaller than a shù is called a 'lǐ'.
Thus, a hundred households form a lǐ,
ten lǐ form a shù,
ten shù form a zhōu,
ten zhōu form a dū,
ten dū form a hegemon state.
Less than a hegemon state is a state.
To serve the Son of Heaven,
the Son of Heaven has ten thousand feudal lords,
among them are dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.
The Son of Heaven resides centrally,
this is called utilizing Heaven's materials,
harnessing Earth's benefits.
Build an inner wall for the city,
outside the city build an outer wall,
outside the outer wall construct an earth barrier:
where the land is high, dig moats,
where low, build dikes.
Call it a golden city.
Plant it with thorns,
with intertwined growth above,
to make it secure.
Yearly repairs and expansions without cease,
timely repairs and expansions without end,
bring blessings to descendants,
this is called a benefit for humanity for ten thousand generations without exhaustion,
and what the ruler preserves.
Ministers serve with utmost loyalty to the ruler,
the ruler embodies this to oversee the world,
thus able to lead the people of the world.
This is the prime minister's responsibility,
and the ministers' duty.
Therefore, those skilled at governing a state,
must first eliminate its five harms,
then the people can be free from calamities lifelong and practice filial piety and kindness."
Duke Huán said:
"I wish to hear about the five harms."
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Floods,
are one harm;
drought,
is one harm;
wind, fog, hail, frost,
are one harm;
pestilence,
is one harm;
insects,
are one harm.
These are called the five harms.
Among the five harms,
floods are the greatest.
Once the five harms are eliminated,
the people can be governed."
Duke Huán said:
"I wish to hear about flood hazards."
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Floods vary in size,
and in distance.
Water that emerges from mountains and flows into the sea,
is called a main river;
water that diverges from other waters,
and enters a large water body or the sea,
is called a branch river;
In the ravines of mountains,
those that sometimes have water
and sometimes are without water
are named valley waters;
waters that emerge from the earth, flowing
into large waters and the sea,
are named river waters;
those that emerge from the earth but do not flow
are named abyssal waters.
These five types of water,
one can follow their benefits and direct them,
or control them by their nature,
but if not managed long-term,
there will often be danger. 」
Huán Gōng said:
"Can water be controlled to make it go east, west, south, north, and even upward?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Yes.
The nature of water
is that it flows swiftly from high to low,
so much so that it can wear through stone;
but from low to high,
it stagnates and does not move.
Therefore, elevate its source,
channel it with gutters,
with a gradient of three-tenths per foot,
and over a distance of forty-nine lǐ,
the water can be made to flow.
Then divert its course to extend it,
utilizing the momentum to direct it.
The nature of water
is that when it reaches a bend
it must slow and retreat,
when full, it pushes from behind to the front,
on low ground it flows level,
on high ground it is restrained,
at sharp bends it erodes and destroys.
If blocked at a bend, it surges,
surging then deflects,
deflecting then swirls,
swirling then centers,
centering then accumulates,
accumulating then blocks,
blocking then shifts,
shifting then restrains,
restraining then water runs wild,
water running wild then harms people,
harming people then causes hardship,
hardship leads to disregard for laws,
disregard for laws makes governance difficult,
difficult governance leads to lack of filial piety,
lack of filial piety leads to lack of loyalty.
Thus, among the five hazards,
those that cause injury and death,
misfortune and fortune are interconnected.
Knowing how to prepare for these five,
a ruler becomes like heaven and earth. 」
Huán Gōng said:
"May I ask the way to prepare against the five hazards?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"To eliminate the five hazards,
start with water.
I propose establishing water officials,
appointing those skilled with water as officers:
one chief and one assistant chief,
leading a sufficient number of section chiefs and assistants.
Then select one person each from the left and right of the water,
to serve as chief artisans and water engineers.
Order them to inspect waterways,
city walls,
river embankments,
ditches and ponds,
government offices,
temples, and within the districts, whatever needs repair,
provide adequate labor and resources.
Issue the order:
Always at the end of the autumn year,
review the people,
register households
by land,
fix the numbers by groups of ten and five,
separate men, women, and children,
those unfit for service
are exempted,
those with chronic illness unable to work
are treated,
those capable of reduced work
are given half duties.
Also, use this to determine armored soldiers,
the number to be armed,
and report to the capital.
The capital oversees the lower levels,
inspecting areas of surplus or shortage,
and refers to the water officials.
The water officials also match the number of armored soldiers to be armed,
and with the village elders,
local officials,
and squad leaders,
tour the villages,
accompanied by parents for inspection.
Check the readiness of water equipment,
during the idle winter time.
Baskets, shovels, planks, and rammers, six of each per ten,
earth carts one per ten,
rain covers two per ten.
Two sets of eating utensils,
each person to have them,
stored securely in the village,
to supply for losses.
Afterwards, regularly order water officials
and chief artisans, with the village elders,
local officials,
and squad leaders,
to conduct inspections.
Begin on the first day of the month, check the equipment,
select the intact and sturdy,
repair the worn and old,
discard the poor and inferior.
Always in winter when tasks are few,
order armored soldiers in shifts to gather more firewood,
piling it by the water's edge.
The district chief leads them,
ensuring no delay.
The piling of firewood
is for when work is done;
the moving of earth
is for before tasks arise.
When heaven and earth are harmonious,
the days are long-lasting.
From this perspective,
the benefits are a hundredfold.
So always prepare equipment when there's no trouble,
to use when trouble arises,
water can then be controlled,
and prevented from causing damage.
This is called being always prepared and ready in advance. 」
Huán Gōng said:
"When should the work be done?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"In the three months of spring,
when heaven and earth are dry,
and water is clear and cold.
Mountains and streams recede,
the celestial qi descends,
the terrestrial qi rises,
and all things interact.
Thus, old tasks are finished,
new tasks not yet begun,
and budding grasses and trees are edible.
Cold and heat are balanced,
day and night are equal,
after the equinox,
nights gradually shorten,
days gradually lengthen.
It is beneficial for earthwork projects,
as the soil becomes firmer.
Order armored soldiers to build embankments beside large waters,
broad at the base,
narrow at the top,
following the water's course.
Where land does not grow grass,
must be made into reservoirs.
Large ones with dams,
small ones with barriers.
Encircling the water on all sides,
crops remain unharmed.
Yearly increase their height,
plant with brambles,
to stabilize the ground.
Mix with cypress and poplar,
to guard against breaches.
The people gain abundance from it,
this is called flowing richness.
Order the poor to maintain them,
marking boundaries throughout,
so they may not fail.
During the three months of summer,
heaven and earth's energy is robust,
the great heat arrives,
all things flourish,
favorable for quickly
eradicating weeds and removing impurities,
orders should not cause disturbance,
the mandate is not long-lasting.
Unfavorable for undertaking earthwork projects,
set aside farming,
benefits are all reduced by half,
earthworks will not succeed.
During the three months of autumn,
mountains, rivers, and numerous springs surge,
rainfall descends,
mountain waters flow out,
sea routes are blocked,
rain and dew connect,
heaven and earth converge.
Favorable for diligent work,
gather and store without delay.
One day's grasp,
sustains for a hundred days.
People, regardless of gender,
all work in the fields.
Unfavorable for undertaking earthwork projects,
dampness increases daily,
soil becomes weak and hard to solidify.
Benefits reduced by six-tenths,
earthwork projects also cannot be established.
During the three months of winter,
heaven and earth close and store,
summer rains cease,
great cold arises,
all things mature and ripen.
Favorable for filling empty gaps,
repairing border walls,
plastering outer paths,
standardizing measures,
adjusting scales,
emptying prisons,
filling granaries,
the ruler cultivates music,
communing with the spirits.
All annual affairs are completed,
promote the meritorious,
reward the virtuous,
punish the guilty,
transfer officials and rank them.
Unfavorable for undertaking earthwork projects,
benefits reduced by seven-tenths,
soil is hard and unyielding.
Days gradually shorten,
while nights gradually lengthen,
favorable for building rooms,
unfavorable for constructing halls.
When the four seasons are properly managed,
the four harms are all subdued. "
Huán Gōng said:
"I am confused,
do not know how the four harms are subdued
and what to do? "
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"If earthworks are done in winter,
disturbing the earth's storage,
then summer will have many rainstorms,
autumn rains will not cease.
If in spring, dried bones and decayed spines are not collected,
dry trees cut down and removed,
then summer drought will arrive.
Summer has heavy dew and plain mist,
choking the lower grasses,
if people gather and eat them
it harms humans.
Many people fall ill without end,
the people then become fearful and imperiled.
The ruler orders the officials of the five departments, along with the sānlǎo,
lǐyǒusī,
wǔzhǎng,
to tour the villages and pacify them,
command households to light fires for warmth,
cover wells in fields and residences,
do not let poison descend
onto eating utensils, which would harm when drinking.
There are insects below that damage crops.
Whenever natural calamities descend,
the noble person cautiously avoids them,
thus not eight or nine out of ten die.
Great cold, great heat,
strong winds, heavy rain,
their arrival at untimely moments,
these are called the four punishments.
Some encounter them and die,
some encounter them and survive,
the noble person avoids them,
for they also harm people.
Thus officials are there to teach and guide,
sānlǎo,
lǐyǒusī,
wǔzhǎng,
are there to set examples.
When these five are in place,
the people have no desires,
but wish for completion.
Therefore, often in winter, guide the sānlǎo,
lǐyǒusī,
wǔzhǎng,
using winter for rewards and punishments,
making each receive their due reward and accept their punishment.
If these five are not harmed,
then the ruler's laws are upheld.
This is shown to the people and easily seen,
thus the people do not form cliques. "
Huán Gōng said:
"Throughout the twelve months of the year,
undertaking earthworks,
if done at the right time it succeeds,
if at the wrong time it fails,
how should one prepare for it? "
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Constantly order the water officials,
in winter to inspect the dikes,
those that can be repaired
report to the capital.
The capital should start work in spring when tasks are few.
After work begins,
regularly inspect them.
If dikes have damage or need construction,
during heavy rain,
each protects their section, repairable ones rush to fix,
using convict labor.
In heavy rain, dikes that can be covered should be covered;
against rushing water, those that can be fortified should be fortified.
The goal throughout the year is to prevent failure.
This is called preparing in ordinary times,
from where would disaster come?
The reason for this is,
muddy water carrying soil, naturally blocking and flowing,
refers to rivers.
Raise the dikes higher each year,
so they do not submerge.
In spring and winter, take soil from within,
in autumn and summer, take soil from outside,
so when muddy water enters
it cannot cause damage. "
Huán Gōng said:
"Good.
Zhòngfù's words to me are complete,
so then what should I do?
Quickly instruct my ministers for me. "

Divide into three, remove the multiple,

The teacher imparts instruction,
and the students follow it as the rule,
being warm, respectful, humble, and empty of self,
fully receiving the teachings.
Upon seeing goodness, they follow it;
hearing of righteousness, they submit to it.
Be gentle, kind, filial, and fraternal,
do not be arrogant or rely on force.
Let your will be free from falsity and evil,
and your conduct must be upright and straight.
In travel and residence, maintain constancy,
and always approach those with virtue.
Keep your countenance orderly,
and your inner heart must be reverent.
Rise early and retire late,
ensuring your attire and belt are neat;
study in the morning and review in the evening,
with careful and cautious diligence.
Maintain this consistently without slackening,
and this is called the rule of learning.
For the duties of the young,
retire late and rise early.
After sweeping, washing, and rinsing,
perform tasks with reverence.
Adjust your clothing and prepare the washbasin,
then the teacher will arise.
Pour water for washing, clear the basin,
sprinkle and sweep, straighten the mat,
then the teacher will sit.
Enter and exit with respect,
as if meeting guests.
Sit upright facing the teacher,
with a countenance free from shame.
The order of receiving lessons
must begin with the elders;
this is done for the first round,
but not necessarily for the rest.
When beginning to recite, one must stand;
for subsequent recitations, it may be omitted.
In all speech and action,
take moderation as the guiding principle.
Those of ancient times who were to rise to prominence
always started from this.
If arriving late, take your seat quietly,
and if the space is narrow, stand up.
If there are guests,
the students quickly rise.
Do not decline in responding to guests,
but answer and promptly act,
hurrying forth to receive instructions.
Even if what is sought is not available,
one must return to report.
Then resume sitting and continue studies.
If there are any doubts,
raise your hands respectfully to ask.
When the teacher leaves, all stand.
When it is mealtime,
and the teacher is about to eat,
the students prepare and serve the meal.
Arrange the lapels, wash, and rinse,
then kneel and sit to serve.
Place the sauces and arrange the food,
setting out the dishes without error.
In arranging the food:
for poultry, game, fish, and turtle,
serve vegetable soup first.
Soup and minced meat are placed separately,
with minced meat before the sauces,
and the setup should be square.
Rice is served last,
with wine on the left and fermented drink on the right.
Announce that all is ready and step back,
standing with hands clasped.
For three servings of rice, use two dǒu measures,
holding the empty vessel in the left hand,
and the serving spoon in the right.
Circling around to serve second portions,
only observing the empty bowls.
For those with empty bowls at the same time, follow age order,
circling ensures a proper beginning,
holding a foot-long ladle without kneeling,
this is called the rule for second servings.
When the teacher has finished eating,
the disciples then clear away.
Hastening to bring water for rinsing,
sweeping in front and gathering the offerings.
Only when the teacher gives the command,
do the disciples eat.
Arranged according to age,
sitting must fill the mat.
Rice must be held with both hands,
soup not taken by hand.
One may rest hands on knees,
but must not conceal elbows.
After eating until full,
wipe mouth and cover hands.
Shake garments and sweep the mat,
those who have eaten rise,
lifting their robes to descend.
Turning toward the mat,
each clears their own utensils,
as if serving guests.
After clearing all vessels,
return and stand.
The method for sweeping:
fill water in the basin,
roll sleeves up to elbows,
in the hall sprinkle widely,
in the room sweep by hand.
Hold the dustpan chest-high,
with the broom inside.
Enter the room and stand,
the ceremony must not be neglected.
Take the broom from the dustpan,
lean it by the door.
The rule for sweeping,
must begin from the southwest corner.
Bowing and bending like a chiming-stone,
sweep without overturning.
Sweep forward while retreating,
gather dirt near the door.
Sit and push it together,
with the leaves toward oneself,
place the broom in the dustpan.
If the teacher rises,
then stand and decline.
Sitting, hold it then stand,
then go out and discard it.
After sweeping return to stand,
coordinating and checking.
Evening meal repeats the ritual.
At dusk when lighting fires,
hold the torch and sit in corner.
The method for arranging firewood,
place crosswise at sitting place.
Depending on the torch's length,
then tend its flame,
positioning square as a carpenter's square.
Between faggots leave space for faggots.
The burning ones stay below,
hold the bowl to catch sparks.
Right hand holds the torch,
left hand adjusts the firewood.
If someone drops out, take over the torch,
when sitting alternately, do not turn back to elders.
Then take the firewood,
and go out to dispose of it.
When the teacher prepares to rest,
all disciples rise.
Respectfully present pillow and mat,
ask where to place feet;
arrange bedding when requested,
otherwise follow routine.
After the teacher has rested,
each joins their friends.
Mutually encouraging and discussing,
each improving their manners.
Circling then starting anew,
this is called the discipline for disciples.

Mountains are
the highest among things.
Benevolence is
the highest conduct of rulers.
Kindness is
the highest conduct of parents.
Loyalty is
the highest conduct of ministers.
Filial piety is
the highest conduct of children and wives.
Thus, if mountains remain high without collapsing, sacrificial sheep will arrive;
if rulers remain benevolent without slackening, the people will support and nourish them;
if parents remain kind without slackening, children and wives will be obedient;
if ministers remain loyal without slackening, ranks and emoluments will come;
if children and wives remain filial without slackening, a good reputation will follow.
Therefore, maintaining height without slackening
leads to obtaining what is desired.
Slackening leads to not obtaining it.
Hence it is said:
"If mountains remain high without collapsing, sacrificial sheep will arrive."
Abysses are
where all things are born;
if they can remain deep without drying up,
then jade offerings will sink to them.
Rulers are
those whom people look up to for survival;
if they can be generous, sincere, and thick-hearted without being harsh or resentful,
then the people will adhere to them.
Parents are
those from whom children and wives receive instruction;
if they can be kind and benevolent in teaching without losing reason,
then children and wives will be filial.
Ministers are
those employed by rulers;
if they can exhaust their strength in serving their superiors,
then they will satisfy their rulers.
Children and wives are
those through whom parents find comfort;
if they can be filial, respectful, and obedient to their parents,
then they will satisfy their parents.
Thus, if an abyss dries up and has no water, jade offerings will not sink to it;
if a ruler is harsh and not thick-hearted, the myriad people will not adhere to him;
if parents are violent and without kindness, children and wives will not be close to them;
if ministers are negligent and not loyal, they will face humiliation and poverty;
if children and wives do not comfort their parents, misfortune and worry will arrive.
Therefore, if an abyss does not dry up,
what is desired will come;
if it dries up, it will not come.
Hence it is said:
"If an abyss is deep and does not dry up, jade offerings will reach it."
Heaven covers all things,
controls cold and heat,
moves the sun and moon,
and orders the stars and constellations;
this is Heaven's constancy.
It governs through principle,
ending and beginning again.
Rulers shepherd the myriad people,
govern the world,
and oversee all officials;
this is the ruler's constancy.
They govern through laws,
ending and beginning again.
Harmonizing descendants
and uniting relatives
is the constancy of parents.
They govern through righteousness,
ending and beginning again.
Being earnest, respectful, loyal, and trustworthy
is the constancy of ministers.
They serve their rulers
ending and beginning again.
Loving parents and providing well for them,
thinking respectfully and following teachings
is the constancy of children and wives.
They serve their parents
ending and beginning again.
Thus, if Heaven does not lose its constancy,
cold and heat will occur at their proper times,
and the sun, moon, stars, and constellations will follow their proper order.
If rulers do not lose their constancy,
ministers will uphold their righteousness,
and all officials will maintain their duties.
If parents do not lose their constancy,
descendants will be harmonious and obedient,
and relatives will be joyful with one another.
If ministers do not lose their constancy,
affairs will be without fault,
and official duties will be well governed.
If children and wives do not lose their constancy,
the old and young will be orderly, and close and distant relations will be harmonious.
Therefore, those who use constancy achieve order,
while those who lose constancy face chaos.
Heaven has never changed,
which is why it achieves order.
Hence it is said:
"Heaven does not change its constancy."
The earth gives birth and nourishes all things;
this is the earth's rule.
Governing and pacifying the common people
is the ruler's rule.
Teaching and protecting family affairs
is the parents' rule.
Offering upright remonstrance and dying for principles
is the ministers' rule.
Exerting full effort in providing support
is the rule for children and wives.
The earth does not alter its rule,
so all things are born.
Rulers do not alter their rule,
so the common people are pacified.
Parents do not alter their rule,
so family affairs are accomplished.
Ministers do not alter their rule,
so rulers are without fault.
Children and wives do not alter their rule,
so parental care is fully provided.
Therefore, using
"rule"
leads to peace,
while not using
"rule"
leads to danger.
The earth has never changed,
which is why it achieves peace.
Hence it is said:
"The earth does not change its rule."
Spring is when
the yang energy begins to rise,
so all things are born.
Summer is when
the yang energy fully rises,
so all things grow.
Autumn is when
the yin energy begins to descend,
so all things are harvested.
Winter is when
the yin energy fully descends,
so all things are stored.
Thus, growth in spring and summer
and storage in autumn and winter
are the rhythms of the four seasons.
Rewards and punishments
are the rhythms of rulers.
The four seasons never fail to give life and take it;
rulers never fail to reward and punish.
Hence it is said:
"Spring, autumn, winter, and summer do not change their rhythms."
Heaven covers all things and controls them;
the earth carries all things and nourishes them;
the four seasons
give life to all things and store them.
From ancient times to the present,
their way has not changed.
Therefore, it is said:
"The ancient and the present are one."
The jiāolóng
is the spiritual creature among water-dwellers.
When it rides on water, its spirit is established;
when it loses water, its spirit is abandoned.
The ruler
is the one who holds authority in the world.
Gaining the people establishes his authority;
losing the people abandons his authority.
The jiāolóng must obtain water before establishing its spirit;
the ruler must gain the people before achieving his authority.
Hence it is said:
"The jiāolóng obtains water, and its spirit can be established."
Tigers and leopards
are the fiercest among beasts.
When they dwell in deep forests and vast marshes, people fear their majesty and respect them.
The ruler
is the one who holds power in the world.
When he dwells deeply, people fear his power.
Thus, if tigers and leopards leave their seclusion and approach people,
people can capture them and diminish their majesty.
If the ruler leaves his gates and presses close to the people,
the people will轻视 him and disdain his power.
Therefore, it is said:
"Tigers and leopards rely on seclusion, and their majesty can be respected."
Wind is what
blows things about.
What the wind blows does not avoid noble or base, beautiful or ugly.
Rain is what
moistens things.
Where the rain falls does not avoid small or large, strong or weak.
Wind and rain are utterly impartial and without selfishness;
where they go has no fixed direction,
and though people encounter being blown or moistened, none resent them.
Hence it is said:
"Wind and rain have no fixed direction, and resentment does not reach them."
The reason why rulers' orders are followed and prohibitions are heeded
is that they must order what the people desire and prohibit what the people detest.
The nature of the people is none do not desire life and detest death,
none do not desire benefit and detest harm.
Therefore, if superiors order life
and benefit people,
orders will be followed;
if they prohibit killing
and harming people,
then prohibitions are enforced.
The reason decrees are carried out,
must be that the people delight in the governance,
and thus decrees are implemented.
Therefore it is said:
"The noble have the means to enforce decrees."
The reason why rulers can make subordinates exert their efforts and remain close to superiors,
must be because they bring benefits and eliminate harms for the world.
Thus when virtuous influence extends throughout the world,
and generous favors are bestowed upon all things,
fathers and sons can live in peace,
and all living beings can be nurtured,
therefore the myriad people joyfully exhaust their strength and delight in serving their superiors.
At home they focus on fundamental work and labor diligently to fill the granaries,
abroad they fulfill their duties and die fighting enemies to secure the state,
even if toilsome, humble, and disgraceful, they dare not complain.
This is how the humble lose their lowliness.
Therefore it is said:
"The humble have the means to lose their lowliness."
When daily routines are timely,
eating and drinking are moderate,
and exposure to cold and heat is appropriate,
then the body benefits and lifespan increases.
When daily routines are untimely,
eating and drinking are immoderate,
and exposure to cold and heat is inappropriate,
then the body suffers and lifespan decreases.
If people are lazy and extravagant then they become poor,
if diligent and frugal then they become rich.
Nothing comes without cause,
there must be a reason for it.
Therefore it is said:
"Long life, early death, poverty, and wealth do not come without reason."
When laws are established and the people delight in them,
when decrees are issued and the people embrace them,
when laws and decrees align with the people's hearts,
like tally slips matching perfectly,
then the ruler is honored and exalted.
Therefore it is said:
"Embracing decrees brings the ruler honor."
When the ruler speaks,
if it follows reason,
and accords with the people's sentiments,
then the people accept his words.
When the people accept his words, his reputation becomes illustrious.
Therefore it is said:
"Accepting words spreads one's fame."
The enlightened ruler's governance of the world,
keeps the people tranquil without disturbance,
and allows the people leisure without toil.
Without disturbance, the people naturally follow order,
without toil, the people naturally test themselves.
Therefore it is said:
"When the ruler does nothing, the people naturally test themselves."
When the ruler establishes his standards,
sets forth the divisions of duties,
clarifies the legal forms,
to oversee his people,
and does not use words to lead them,
then the people follow the correct path.
What is called holding the Shǔ,
refers to sacrificial vessels.
Therefore it is said:
"Holding the Shǔ without speaking, yet the temple is already well-ordered."
The magnificent swan goose,
is beautiful in appearance.
Beautiful in appearance,
therefore the people sing of it.
Virtue and righteousness,
are beautiful in conduct.
Beautiful in virtue and righteousness,
therefore the people delight in them.
What the people sing of and delight in,
are beautiful appearance, virtue, and righteousness,
and the enlightened ruler possesses the swan goose's qualities.
Therefore it is said:
"The magnificent swan goose,
the people sing of it."
The multitude of talents,
refers to sincere dignity in handling affairs;
the many scholars,
are those with many strengths.
King Wén of Zhōu was sincere and dignified in handling affairs,
therefore the state was well-governed.
His ministers understood principle to assist their ruler,
therefore the ruler was enlightened.
The ruler enlightened and the state well-governed,
the entire realm received his beneficial influence,
the people of Yīn raised their heads to gaze at King Wén,
wishing to become King Wén's subjects.
Therefore it is said:
"With a multitude of talents,
the Yīn people were transformed."
When Zhòu was ruler,
he exhausted the people's strength,
seized the people's wealth,
endangered the people unto death.
Unjust and violent decrees,
were imposed upon the hundred surnames;
cruel and poisonous emissaries,
were sent throughout the world.
Therefore great ministers were not close,
common people bitterly resented,
the world turned against him and wished to be King Wén's subjects -
Zhòu brought this upon himself.
Therefore it is said:
"Zhòu's failure."
Without standards, laws, or models,
flying and shaking without settling,
this is called the question of flying thistledown.
The question of flying thistledown,
the enlightened ruler does not listen to.
Words without measure,
the enlightened ruler does not approve.
Therefore it is said:
"The question of flying thistledown,
is not among what is honored."
When the Way prevails then ruler and ministers are close,
father and son are secure,
and all beings are nurtured.
Therefore the enlightened ruler's task,
lies in practicing the Way,
not minding small things.
Swallows and sparrows,
are small creatures.
Therefore it is said:
"The gathering of swallows and sparrows,
when the Way prevails, is not minded."
The enlightened ruler's actions accord with principle and righteousness,
his commands follow the people's hearts,
his executions match the crimes,
his rewards match the achievements,
therefore even without using sacrificial animals and jade tablets to pray to spirits and deities,
the spirits and deities assist him,
heaven and earth support him,
and undertakings bring good fortune.
The chaotic ruler's actions lack righteousness and principle,
his commands oppose the people's hearts,
his executions do not match the crimes,
his rewards do not match the achievements,
therefore even using sacrificial animals and jade tablets to pray to spirits and deities,
the spirits and deities do not assist,
heaven and earth do not support,
and undertakings bring misfortune.
Therefore it is said:
"Sacrificial animals and jade tablets are insufficient to please spirits."
What the ruler considers achievement,
is wealth and power.
Therefore when the state is rich and the military strong,
then feudal lords submit to his governance,
neighboring enemies fear his might,
even without using precious goods to serve feudal lords,
feudal lords dare not attack.
What the ruler considers fault,
is poverty and weakness.
Therefore when the state is poor and the military weak,
in war they cannot win,
in defense they cannot hold firm,
even presenting famous vessels and precious treasures to serve neighboring enemies,
they cannot avoid the disaster of destruction.
Therefore it is said:
"If the ruler's achievements have foundation,
what use are precious goods?"
Yì, was an expert archer in ancient times.
He adjusted his bow and arrows and maintained them firmly.
In handling his bow,
he assessed the height and distance,
having the way to certainly hit,
therefore he could shoot frequently and hit frequently.
The enlightened ruler,
is like Yì.
He balances his laws,
examines what to abolish and establish and maintains them firmly,
having the way to certainly govern well,
therefore he can undertake many tasks and succeed in many.
The Way,
is how Yì certainly hits,
and how the ruler certainly governs well.
Shooting,
is releasing arrows from the bowstring.
Therefore it is said:
"Yì's Way is not just shooting."
Zàofǔ,
was skilled at handling horses.
He carefully watched his horses,
regulated their feeding,
measured their strength,
examined their running,
therefore he could cover long distances without the horses tiring.
The enlightened ruler,
is like Zàofǔ.
He skillfully governs his people,
measures their strength,
examines their abilities,
therefore he achieves merit without the people suffering hardship.
Thus method,
is how Zàofǔ covers long distances,
and how the ruler achieves merit and fame.
Handling horses,
means holding the reins.
Hence it is said:
"Zàofǔ's skill does not lie in driving."
When Xīzhòng made chariots and implements,
their squares, circles, curves, and straight lines all conformed to compasses, squares, hooks, and marking lines,
so the mechanisms meshed perfectly,
their use was secure and efficient,
and the finished products were sturdy.
An enlightened ruler,
is like Xīzhòng.
His words and actions
all conform to methods and principles,
so various principles align properly,
and superiors and subordinates are mutually affectionate.
Skillfulness is
what Xīzhòng used to create implements,
and what the ruler uses to govern.
What carves and pares
are the axe and knife.
Hence it is said:
"Xīzhòng's skill does not lie in carving and paring."
The people come when it benefits them,
and leave when it harms them.
The people's pursuit of benefit
is like water flowing downward,
making no choice among the four directions.
Therefore, those who wish to attract the people
must first create benefits for them;
then even without summoning, the people will come of their own accord.
If what they detest is established,
even if summoned, the people will not come.
Hence it is said:
"Those who summon the distant need not exert effort."
Governing the people like parents
makes the people affectionate and loving.
If the way is pure and sincere,
and treatment is substantial,
even without saying "I am affectionate to the people,"
the people will be affectionate.
Governing the people like enemies
makes the people distant.
If the way is insincere,
and treatment is insubstantial,
with deception and falsehood arising together,
even if saying "I am affectionate to the people,"
the people will not be affectionate.
Hence it is said:
"Those who are closely affiliated need not speak of it."
The enlightened ruler's ability to make the distant come and the near be affectionate
lies in his heart.
What is called "nocturnal conduct"
is the conduct of the heart.
If one can conduct virtue in heart,
then none under heaven can contend with him.
Hence it is said:
"Only the nocturnal conductor uniquely possesses it."
To be a ruler yet cruel,
to be parents yet violent,
to be ministers yet disloyal,
to be children or wives yet unfilial—
these four are great faults in humans.
With great faults in person,
even if there are minor virtues,
one cannot be considered worthy.
What is called a plain
is low marshland.
Even with small mounds,
it cannot be considered high.
Hence it is said:
"On the plain's path,
what height is there?"
To be a ruler yet kind,
to be parents yet compassionate,
to be ministers yet loyal,
to be children or wives yet filial—
these four are lofty conducts in humans.
With lofty conducts in person,
even if there are minor faults,
one is not considered unworthy.
What is called a great mountain
is the high part of the mountain.
Even with small depressions,
it is not considered deep.
Hence it is said:
"In the great mountain's hollow,
what depth is there?"
Slandering the worthy is called calumny;
praising the unworthy is called flattery.
If calumniators and flatterers are employed,
then the ruler's clarity is obscured,
and slanderous and praising words arise.
If entrusted with great tasks,
the tasks will not succeed and calamities will arrive.
Hence it is said:
"Calumniators and flatterers,
do not assign them great responsibilities."
When an enlightened ruler considers affairs,
planning for the world,
it is called grand strategy.
Grand strategy ensures the land within the seas receives its benefits,
benefits spread throughout the world,
and later generations enjoy its achievements long into the future, with advantages multiplying.
Hence it is said:
"Those with grand strategy can undertake far-reaching endeavors."
The sage chooses what can be spoken before speaking,
and what can be done before acting.
To stealthily gain profit only to have harm later,
or stealthily gain pleasure only to have sorrow later—
the sage does not do such things.
Thus, the sage in choosing words must consider their burdens,
and in choosing actions must consider their worries.
Hence it is said:
"Those who consider worries can attain the Way."
Petty persons
distort the Way to gain favor,
cater to the ruler's wishes for fleeting pleasure,
and follow profit for illicit gains.
Such people,
though they gain quickly,
also face calamities urgently.
Therefore, the sage discards and does not use them.
Hence it is said:
"Plans that are swift with worries near at hand—
let them go and do not summon them back."
To promote one thing that brings long-term benefit to the world
is called promoting longevity.
Promoting longevity means many receive its benefits,
and virtue and righteousness are seen far and wide.
Hence it is said:
"Those who promote longevity can see far."
Heaven's capacity is vast,
so it can cover all things;
Earth's capacity is vast,
so it can carry all things;
the ruler's capacity is vast,
so he accommodates many things and the masses can rely on him.
Hence it is said:
"Those with vast capacity are relied upon by the masses."
Nobility, wealth, honor, and prominence
make the people submit and delight in them,
and no ruler fails to desire this.
Therefore, to desire the people's affection and delight in oneself,
one must practice morality without weariness,
and the people will cherish and delight in it.
Hence it is said:
"To desire people's affection,
steadfastly practice without weariness."
When the sage seeks tasks,
he first examines their principles and righteousness,
and assesses their feasibility.
Thus, if righteous, he seeks them;
if unrighteous, he stops;
if feasible, he seeks them;
if infeasible, he stops.
Therefore, the tasks he obtains
are always personal treasures.
When petty persons seek tasks,
they do not examine principles and righteousness,
nor assess feasibility.
Unrighteous, they still seek;
infeasible, they still seek.
Thus, the tasks they obtain
are never reliable.
Hence it is said:
"Inevitably obtained matters
are not reliable."
When the sage makes promises,
he first examines their principles and righteousness,
and assesses their feasibility.
Righteous, he promises;
unrighteous, he stops;
feasible, he promises;
infeasible, he stops.
Thus, his promises are never untrustworthy.
Petty persons promise even the unrighteous,
and promise even the infeasible,
promising whatever they say.
Thus, their promises are not necessarily trustworthy.
Hence it is said:
"Inevitably promised words
are not trustworthy."
Prudent in one family,
one establishes oneself in one family;
prudent in one village,
one establishes oneself in one village;
prudent in one state,
one establishes oneself in one state;
prudent in the world,
one establishes oneself in the world.
Therefore, if one's prudence is small,
one's establishment is also small;
if one's prudence is great,
one's establishment is also great.
Hence it is said:
"Small prudence does not lead to great establishment."
The sea does not refuse water,
so it can achieve its vastness;
the mountain does not refuse earth and stones,
so it can achieve its height;
the enlightened ruler does not weary of people,
so he can achieve his multitude;
A scholar never tires of learning,
thus he can achieve sagehood.
Being picky about food,
one dislikes many things.
Remonstrance
is the means to secure the ruler;
eating
is the means to nourish the body.
If the ruler dislikes remonstrance, he will not be secure;
if a person is picky about food, he will not be nourished.
Hence it is said:
"One who is picky about food does not nourish the body."
Those who speak of virtue, morality, loyalty, trustworthiness, filial piety, and fraternal duty—
these words are never to be discarded.
Heaven is impartial and without selfishness,
thus it covers all, beautiful and ugly;
Earth is impartial and without selfishness,
thus it carries all, great and small.
Words that are never discarded,
impartial and without selfishness,
thus are employed by all, worthy and unworthy.
Therefore, words that are never discarded
align with the selflessness of Heaven and Earth.
Hence it is said:
"One who possesses words that are never discarded
must align them with Heaven and Earth."
An enlightened ruler appoints things to office
by utilizing their strengths,
not their weaknesses,
thus no task is left unaccomplished and no achievement is left unrealized.
A chaotic ruler does not understand that each thing has its strengths and weaknesses,
and demands perfection in all.
In planning affairs and settling matters,
distinguishing and clarifying rites and righteousness—
these are human strengths but the weaknesses of monkeys;
scaling heights and traversing dangers—
these are the strengths of monkeys but human weaknesses.
To demand of humans what monkeys excel at,
thus his orders are abandoned and demands unfulfilled.
Therefore it is said:
"A cliff drop of three rèn
is a great difficulty for humans,
yet monkeys drink from it."
An enlightened ruler in undertaking affairs
employs the wisdom of sages,
utilizes the strength of the masses,
without intervening personally.
Thus affairs succeed and blessings arise.
A chaotic ruler considers himself wise,
and does not rely on the wisdom of sages;
boasts of his efforts and claims credit,
without utilizing the strength of the masses;
relies solely on himself,
and does not heed proper remonstrance.
Thus affairs fail and disasters arise.
Hence it is said:
"Boastful and fond of acting alone,
such is the disaster in undertaking affairs."
Horses
are used to travel the wilds.
Thus even if not traveling the wilds,
the care and feeding of horses
should never be neglected.
The people
are relied upon for defense and battle.
Thus even if not defending or battling,
the governance and care of the people
should never be neglected.
Therefore it is said:
"Not traveling the wilds,
do not neglect the horses."
Heaven gives birth to the four seasons,
Earth gives birth to all resources,
to nurture all things without taking anything.
An enlightened ruler matches Heaven and Earth.
He teaches the people according to the seasons,
encourages them in plowing and weaving,
to enrich their livelihood,
without boasting of his achievements,
without privatizing the benefits.
Hence it is said:
"Able to give without taking—
such is the match for Heaven and Earth."
Negligence and disrespect,
in serving the ruler, lead to disloyalty;
in serving parents, lead to unfiliality;
in undertaking affairs, lead to failure.
Therefore it is said:
"The lazy and weary fall short."
Using compass and square, circles and squares are formed;
using inches and feet, lengths are measured;
using laws and standards, the people are governed peacefully.
Thus, affairs not exceeding principle
succeed as if by divine power.
Hence it is said:
"Without excess, one appears divine."
Serving the ruler without full effort incurs punishment;
serving parents without full effort loses affection;
receiving instruction and learning without diligence leads to failure.
Thus, if not striving to advance in the morning,
by evening no achievement is seen.
Therefore it is said:
"Forget the task in the morning,
lose the achievement by evening."
Sincere and truthful within, then reputation is fine;
conduct cautious and respectful, then honor and prominence follow.
Without sincerity within, then reputation is poor;
conduct disrespectful and negligent, then disgrace arises.
Hence it is said:
"When evil qi invades within,
the upright countenance fades."
As a ruler, if unaware of the principles between ruler and minister to correct his ministers,
then ministers will not understand their duty to serve their ruler.
Therefore it is said:
"If the ruler is not a ruler, the minister is not a minister."
As a father, if unaware of the principles between father and son to teach and discipline his son,
then the son will not know the way of a son to serve his father.
Hence it is said:
"If the father is not a father, the son is not a son."
When ruler and minister are close,
superior and inferior harmonious,
and all the people united,
then if the ruler has orders, the people follow them;
if superiors prohibit, the people do not violate.
If ruler and minister are not close,
superior and inferior not harmonious,
and all the people not united,
then orders are not carried out,
prohibitions are not heeded.
Thus it is said:
"When superior and inferior are not harmonious,
orders are not carried out."
If speech is trustworthy,
actions dignified,
attire proper,
then subordinates are respectful.
If speech is disrespectful,
actions deficient,
attire negligent,
then subordinates轻视 them.
Therefore it is said:
"If attire is not proper, the guests are not respectful."
Ritual forms
are the standard for all things.
Laws and measures
are the model for all people;
rites and righteousness
are the model for noble and humble.
Thus, with ritual forms in action, orders are carried out;
without ritual forms, orders are not carried out.
Hence it is said:
"Without ritual in advance and retreat, government orders are not carried out."
A ruler,
if gentle, kind, and generous, the people will love him;
if orderly and stern, the people will fear him.
Thus, if loved, they draw close;
if feared, they are used.
When the people are close and can be used,
this is what the ruler urgently needs.
Therefore it is said:
"Both cherishing and awe-inspiring, then the way of the ruler is complete."
If a ruler can secure his people,
they will serve him as they serve their parents.
Thus, if the ruler has sorrows, they share them;
if there is danger, they die for him.
If the ruler treats the people as dirt,
then the people cannot be used.
If the ruler has sorrows, they do not share them;
if there is danger, they do not die for him.
Hence it is said:
"If not made happy, they will not share sorrow;
if not given life, they will not die for it."
The reason the people defend and fight to the death without decline
is that the superiors bestow generously upon them.
Thus, if superiors bestow generously,
the people repay them generously;
if superiors bestow meagerly,
the people repay them meagerly.
Therefore, meager bestowal with high demands—
a ruler cannot get this from ministers,
a father cannot get this from a son.
So it is said:
"If what is given does not reach,
what comes back does not arrive."
The Dào
supports all things,
enabling them to grow and nurture,
and each to complete its nature and destiny.
Thus, some use it to govern a village,
some to govern a state,
some to govern the world.
Therefore it is said:
"What the Dào speaks of is one,
but its applications differ."
Hearing the Dào and using it to govern one village,
making fathers and sons close,
brothers harmonious,
customs corrected,
so the people delight in their superiors,
and are content with their land,
One who governs a village
is a member of that village.
Hence it is said:
"Those who understand the Way and are devoted to their villages
are true villagers."
The people's adherence to those who possess the Way
is like the hungry seeking food first,
like the cold seeking clothing first,
like the heat-stricken seeking shade first.
Thus, with the Way, the people gather around;
without the Way, the people depart.
Therefore it is said:
"When the Way departs, people do not come;
when the Way arrives, people do not leave."
The Way is
what transforms one's person toward correct principles.
Thus, with the Way embodied, speech naturally aligns,
actions naturally correct,
serving the ruler naturally loyal,
serving the father naturally filial,
interacting with others naturally reasonable.
Hence it is said:
"Where the Way is established,
the person is transformed."
Heaven's Way
is full without overflowing,
flourishing without declining.
Enlightened rulers emulate Heaven's Way,
thus noble without arrogance,
wealthy without extravagance,
acting with principle without laziness.
Therefore they can long maintain nobility and wealth,
possessing the world enduringly without losing it.
Thus it is said:
"Those who maintain fullness align with Heaven."
Enlightened rulers save the world from calamity,
securing the world from danger.
Saving from calamity and securing from danger
must rely on the multitude being employable,
then it can be accomplished.
Therefore it is said:
"Security and danger depend on people."
Vast territory and wealthy state,
numerous people and strong army—
this is a flourishing, full state.
Though already flourishing and full,
without virtuous generosity to secure it,
without measured methods to govern it,
then the state is not their state,
and the people are not their people.
Hence it is said:
"Losing Heaven's measure,
though full, it will surely dry up."
When ministers are not close to their ruler,
the common people do not trust their officials,
superiors and subordinates estranged and discordant,
though seemingly secure,
they will certainly face danger.
Therefore it is said:
"When superiors and subordinates are discordant,
though secure, they will surely be endangered."
If the ruler possesses Heaven's Way
to guide his people,
then the people unite in heart and serve their superior,
thus achieving nobility, wealth, and long-lasting rule over the world.
Losing Heaven's Way,
the people rebel and disobey,
thus the ruler is endangered and cannot long rule the world.
Hence it is said:
"Wanting to rule the world but losing Heaven's Way,
the world cannot be ruled."
If rulers devote themselves to learning methods and techniques,
practicing correct principles,
then transformation progresses daily,
reaching great achievements,
yet foolish people do not perceive it.
Chaotic rulers indulge in excess and wickedness,
daily acting without the Way,
until destruction,
yet remain unaware.
Thus it is said:
"None know it is being done,
yet the achievement is complete;
none know it is being abandoned,
hidden without form."
In ancient times, the Three Sovereigns and Five Hegemons all benefited the world as rulers,
thus their persons were noble and illustrious, and descendants received their blessings.
Jié, Zhòu,
Yōu, Lì all harmed the world as rulers,
thus their persons suffered and were ruined, and descendants inherited their misfortune.
Therefore it is said:
"Those doubting the present examine the past;
those unknowing of the future look to what has passed."
Shénnóng taught farming to grow grain,
bringing benefits to the people.
Yǔ personally dredged rivers,
leveling heights and bridging lows,
bringing benefits to the people.
Tāng and Wǔ campaigned against those without the Way,
executing the violent and chaotic,
bringing benefits to the people.
Thus, though the actions of enlightened kings differ,
their benefiting the people is the same.
Hence it is said:
"In undertaking all tasks,
different beginnings share the same end,
ancient and modern are one."
When a warped beam cannot bear the load and the house collapses,
people do not resent it,
for such is the natural principle.
A young child,
beloved by a kind mother.
If without reason (
textual addition) removing tiles, the kind mother will whip him.
Thus, acting according to principle,
even collapsing a house draws no resentment;
acting without principle,
removing tiles warrants whipping.
Therefore it is said:
"A green beam collapsing the house—
no resentment or anger follows;
a young child removing tiles—
the kind mother wields the rod."
Practicing Heaven's Way,
upholding public principle,
then the distant naturally draw close;
abandoning Heaven's Way,
acting selfishly,
then mother and child resent each other.
Thus it is said:
"At the pinnacle of Heaven's Way,
the distant naturally draw close;
when human affairs arise,
close kin create resentment."
In ancient times,
King Wǔ's territory was no more than a hundred lǐ square,
his troops no more than ten thousand men,
yet he could triumph in battles and conquests,
being established as the Son of Heaven,
and the world calls him a sage king—
he knew the method of accomplishing it.
Jié and Zhòu, noble as Sons of Heaven,
rich possessing all within the seas,
with vast territories,
numerous troops,
yet died personally and their states perished,
becoming scorned by the world—
they did not know the method of accomplishing it.
Thus, capable of accomplishing it,
the small can become great,
the lowly can become noble.
Incapable of accomplishing it,
even as Son of Heaven,
others may still seize it.
Hence it is said:
"The skillful have surplus; the clumsy have shortage."
Enlightened rulers above do not oppose Heaven,
below do not waste the earth,
thus Heaven grants the seasons,
earth produces wealth.
Chaotic rulers above oppose Heaven's Way,
below disrupt earth's principles,
thus Heaven grants no seasons,
earth produces no wealth.
Therefore it is said:
"Those whose deeds accord with Heaven,
Heaven assists;
those whose deeds oppose Heaven,
Heaven resists."
In ancient times,
King Wǔ
was assisted by Heaven.
Thus, though his land was small and people few,
he still became Son of Heaven.
Jié and Zhòu,
were resisted by Heaven.
Thus, though their land was vast and people numerous,
they still met hardship, disgrace, and death.
Hence it is said:
"Those assisted by Heaven,
though small, will surely become great;
those resisted by Heaven,
though great, will surely be diminished."
In interacting with others,
much deceit and insincerity,
opportunistically seizing everything,
is called a flock-of-crows gathering.
A flock-of-crows gathering,
initially joyful,
later必然 mutual reproach.
Thus it is said:
"A flock-of-crows gathering,
though seemingly good, is not intimate."
When sages form covenants with others,
they observe above how they serve the ruler,
within how they serve their parents,
ensuring there are discernible principles,
then form covenants.
Covenants not aligned with principle
will later必然 be betrayed.
Hence it is said:
"A knot that is not double-layered,
though firm, will inevitably come undone.
In the application of the Dào,
what is valued is its layered depth."
An enlightened ruler consults with sages,
thus his plans succeed;
when he undertakes affairs with them,
thus his endeavors achieve completion.
A chaotic ruler consults with the unworthy,
thus his strategies fail;
when he undertakes affairs with them,
thus his endeavors end in defeat.
When strategies fail and endeavors are defeated,
this is the crime of collaborating with the incapable.
Hence it is said:
"Do not collaborate with the incapable."
An enlightened ruler measures what people are capable of accomplishing,
and only then employs them.
Therefore, when commands are within people's capabilities,
then the commands are carried out;
when tasks are assigned within people's capabilities,
then affairs are accomplished.
A chaotic ruler does not gauge people's capabilities,
issuing commands for what people cannot accomplish,
thus his commands are abandoned;
assigning tasks beyond people's capabilities,
thus his affairs end in failure.
When commands are issued but abandoned,
and endeavors undertaken but defeated,
this is the crime of forcing the incapable.
Hence it is said:
"Do not force the incapable."
To mad and deluded people,
if one explains the principles of ruler and minister,
the reasoning between father and son,
the distinctions between noble and base,
they do not believe the words of sages,
but instead harm and injure them.
Therefore, sages do not instruct them.
Hence it is said:
"Do not instruct the unknowing."
Collaborating with the unworthy in undertakings,
then affairs will fail;
assigning tasks beyond people's capabilities,
then commands will be abandoned;
instructing mad and deluded people,
then one's person will be harmed.
Hence it is said:
"Collaborating with the incapable,
forcing the unable,
instructing the unknowing -
this is called labor without achievement."
Always using words to highlight one's associations with others,
one's affection for others,
one's virtuous deeds toward others -
using this to make friends will not create intimacy,
using this to form connections will not create bonds,
using this to show virtue toward others will not be repaid.
Hence it is said:
"Friendship that displays association,
approaches non-intimacy;
connections that display affection,
approach non-bonding;
virtue that displays giving,
approaches non-repayment.
What all quarters return to
is the practice of the heart."
An enlightened ruler does not use his own wisdom,
but employs the wisdom of sages;
does not use his own strength,
but employs the strength of the multitude.
Therefore, using the wisdom of sages for contemplation,
there is nothing unknown;
using the strength of the multitude to initiate affairs,
there is nothing unaccomplished.
Being able to set aside oneself and rely on the world's wisdom and strength to act,
then one's person is at ease and blessings are abundant.
A chaotic ruler exclusively uses his own wisdom,
and does not employ the wisdom of sages;
exclusively uses his own strength,
and does not employ the strength of the multitude,
thus his person is labored and calamities are abundant.
Hence it is said:
"A state that relies exclusively on itself,
is labored and full of calamities."
An enlightened ruler internally practices his laws and measures,
externally practices his principles of righteousness.
Thus neighboring states are close to him,
and allied states trust him.
When he has troubles, neighboring states worry for him,
when he has difficulties, neighboring states rescue him.
A chaotic ruler internally loses his people,
externally is not trusted by neighboring states.
Thus when he has troubles, none worry for him,
when he has difficulties, none rescue him.
Both externally and internally failing,
isolated and without allies,
thus the state is weak and the ruler humiliated.
Hence it is said:
"The ruler of an isolated state,
is lowly and lacks authority."
An enlightened ruler in governing the world,
must employ sages,
and only then will the world be well-governed;
a woman seeking a husband's household,
must use a matchmaker,
and only then will the household matter be accomplished.
Therefore, governing the world without employing sages,
then the world becomes discordant and chaotic and the people are not close;
seeking a husband's household without using a matchmaker,
then it is shameful and people do not believe it.
Hence it is said:
"A woman who acts as her own matchmaker,
is shameful and not believed."
An enlightened ruler,
whom people have not yet seen yet feel closeness in their hearts,
has the way to make people feel close to him.
Thus his position is secure and people go to him.
Hence it is said:
"One not yet seen yet felt close to,
can be approached."
Yáo and Shùn,
enlightened rulers of antiquity,
the world praised them without weariness,
honored them without disgust,
and after long ages did not forget them,
because they had the way to make people not forget.
Thus their positions were secure and people came to them.
Hence it is said:
"Long remembered without forgetting,
can be drawn to."
The sun and moon,
illuminate and examine all things,
but if the sky has many clouds,
and there are numerous coverings and obstructions,
then the sun and moon are not bright.
The ruler of men,
is like the sun and moon,
if many ministers establish treachery and private interests,
thereby obstructing and covering the ruler,
then the ruler cannot clearly examine his ministers and subordinates,
and the situation of ministers and subordinates cannot reach upward.
Thus treacherous and evil persons daily increase and the ruler becomes increasingly obscured.
Hence it is said:
"When the sun and moon are not bright,
it is not that heaven has changed."
Mountains are the highest of things.
If the terrain is dangerous, filthy, and not level,
then mountains cannot be seen.
The ruler of men,
is like a mountain,
if his close associates form cliques and collude to block his view,
then the ruler cannot be seen.
Hence it is said:
"When mountains are high but not seen,
it is not that the earth has changed."
When a ruler speaks without opposing the people's hearts,
without contradicting principles of righteousness,
what he says is sufficient to pacify the world,
and people only fear that he will not speak again.
When his speech severs the closeness between father and son,
alienates the way of ruler and minister,
harms the multitude of the world,
this is speech that should not be repeated,
therefore an enlightened ruler does not speak it.
Hence it is said:
"Speech that cannot be repeated,
the ruler does not speak."
When a ruler's personal conduct is upright and proper,
treating people with courtesy,
meeting people with trustworthiness,
and actions emanating from his person become models for the world,
people only fear that he will not act again.
When his personal conduct is not upright,
treating people with cruelty,
meeting people without trustworthiness,
and actions emanating from his person become laughingstocks for the world,
this is conduct that cannot be repeated,
therefore an enlightened ruler does not practice it.
Hence it is said:
"Conduct that cannot be repeated,
the ruler does not practice."
Speech that cannot be repeated -
such speech is untrustworthy;
conduct that cannot be repeated -
such conduct is harmful and violent.
Therefore, speaking without trustworthiness then the people will not adhere;
acting with harm and violence then the world will resent.
When the people do not adhere,
and the world resents,
this is from where destruction and demise arise,
therefore an enlightened ruler prohibits it.
Hence it is said:
"All speech that cannot be repeated,
all conduct that cannot be repeated -
these are great prohibitions for those who possess a state."
If the ruler only listens to the advocacy of disarmament,
then none among the ministers and guests dare to speak of military affairs.
Consequently, internally, he remains unaware of the state's order or chaos,
and externally, he remains ignorant of the strength or weakness of the feudal lords.
In such a case, the city walls will fall into disrepair,
with no one to rebuild or mend them;
armor will wear out and weapons deteriorate,
with no one to repair or maintain them.
Thus, the preparations for defense will be ruined.
Schemes for distant lands will arise,
and border guards will become lax,
leaving the common people without the will to resist the enemy.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of disarmament prevails,
then even strategic barriers will not be defended."
If the ruler only listens to the doctrine of universal love,
he will regard the people of the world as his own people,
and view other states as his own state.
In this way, there will be no intention to annex or seize,
and no incidents of destroying armies or defeating generals.
However, then skilled archers, charioteers, and brave warriors will not receive generous salaries,
and ministers who have crushed armies and slain enemy generals will not be honored with high ranks.
Thus, these skilled and brave men will leave to serve abroad.
We may refrain from attacking others,
but we cannot prevent others from attacking us.
If they demand territory and we cede it,
that is not what we desire;
if we refuse and go to war,
we will surely not prevail.
They employ trained soldiers,
while we use driven masses;
they have excellent generals,
while we have incompetents.
Their defeat would mean the destruction of armies and loss of generals.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of universal love prevails,
then officers and soldiers will not fight."
If the ruler has no fondness for preserving life fully,
then all ministers will fully preserve their own lives, , ?
And yet they nurture life—
what does nurturing life entail?
It is said: rich flavors,
music and beauty,
these then constitute nurturing life.
However, this leads to indulging desires and promiscuous conduct,
no distinction between men and women,
reverting to beasts.
Thus, propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame are not established,
and the ruler has nothing to uphold himself with.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of preserving life fully prevails,
then integrity and shame will not be established."
If the ruler only listens to private opinions and self-aggrandizement,
then the people will withdraw into quiet seclusion,
dwelling in caves in the mountains,
criticizing the world and their superiors,
despising official ranks and salaries and looking down on authorities.
Consequently, orders will not be carried out and prohibitions will not be enforced.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of private opinions and self-aggrandizement prevails,
then the ruler's commands will not be implemented."
If the ruler has a fondness for gold, jade, goods, and wealth,
and must obtain what he desires,
then there must be a means to acquire them.
What is the means to acquire them?
High offices and esteemed positions,
or else noble titles and heavy salaries.
Thus, the unworthy will hold high positions.
Then the worthy will not serve in lower posts,
the wise will not offer counsel,
the trustworthy will not make agreements,
and the brave will not sacrifice their lives.
In this way, the state is driven to ruin and abandoned.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of gold, jade, goods, and wealth prevails,
then ranks and honors will flow downward to the unworthy."
If the ruler only listens to cliques and factions,
then the ministers will form cabals,
concealing the good and exposing the bad.
Thus, the true situation of the state will not reach the ruler.
In this case, those with factions will be promoted,
while those without will be left behind.
When factions are in front,
the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished,
then struggles and conflicts arise,
and the ruler is placed in peril.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of cliques and factions prevails,
then the worthy
and unworthy will not be distinguished."
If the ruler only indulges in spectacles, music, and curios,
he will be ruined.
All spectacles and amusements—
palaces,
towers and ponds,
pearls and jades,
music and sounds—
these are all ways to waste wealth, exhaust strength, and harm the state.
And those who serve the ruler with these
are all treacherous individuals.
If the ruler listens to them,
how can he avoid ruin?
Then the treasuries and granaries will be empty,
reserves exhausted,
and with treacherous men in power,
they will block and prevent the worthy from advancing.
When the state faces calamity,
then actors and dwarfs will rise to discuss state affairs.
This is driving the state to ruin and abandoning it.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of spectacles, music, and curios prevails,
then treacherous men will hold high positions."
If the ruler only listens to requests and recommendations,
then all ministers will engage in mutual solicitation.
Thus, petitions will succeed with the superiors,
and cliques will form in the localities.
In this way, bribery will circulate in the state,
and laws and regulations will be destroyed by officials.
Ministers will strive to form cliques and seek employment,
resulting in those without rank becoming noble,
and those without salary becoming rich.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of requests and recommendations prevails,
then the standards of law will not be upright."
If the ruler only listens to flattering and fault-concealing words,
he will be ruined.
How do we know this is so?
Flattering ministers
often cause their lord not to regret his errors nor correct his faults,
so the lord is deluded and unaware of himself.
Thus, loyal ministers perish while flattering ministers are honored.
Therefore it is said:
"If the doctrine of flattery and fault-concealing prevails,
then the cunning and sycophantic will be employed."
The law,
models the positions of heaven and earth,
imitates the operations of the four seasons,
to govern the world.
The operations of the four seasons
include cold and heat;
the sage models them,
hence there are civil and military affairs.
The positions of heaven and earth
have front and rear,
left and right;
the sage models them,
to establish order.
Spring gives birth on the left,
autumn executes on the right;
summer flourishes in front,
winter stores in the rear.
The affairs of growth and flourishing
are civil;
the affairs of storage and execution
are military.
Therefore, civil affairs are on the left,
military affairs on the right;
the sage models this,
to implement laws and decrees,
and manage affairs with principle.
In all legal matters,
the handling must be upright.
If handling is not upright, then adjudication is not fair.
If adjudication is not fair, then governance does not fully follow principle,
and affairs are not fully responsive.
If governance does not fully follow principle,
then the distant and lowly have no means to appeal;
if affairs are not fully responsive,
then benefits and achievements are not fully realized.
If benefits and achievements are not fully realized, the state becomes poor;
if the distant and lowly have no means to appeal, the foundation is shaken.
Hence it is said:
"In all endeavors to be established,
correct that heavenly planting."
Heavenly planting
refers to the heart.
If the heavenly planting is correct,
then one does not favor close relatives,
nor harm the distant.
Not favoring close relatives,
nor harming the distant,
then no benefits are overlooked,
no governance is hidden.
With no benefits overlooked,
no governance hidden,
then all affairs are accomplished,
and nothing is omitted.
To see the heart of heaven,
it is revealed through wind and rain.
Hence it is said:
"Wind and rain do not err,
far and near, high and low,
each attains its succession."
All things revere heaven and value wind and rain.
The reason for revering heaven
is that all receive their mandate from it;
the reason for valuing wind and rain
is that all await the wind to move and the rain to moisten.
If all things were to abandon heaven and receive mandates elsewhere,
abandon wind and look elsewhere to move,
abandon rain and look elsewhere to be moistened,
then there would be no reason to revere heaven and value wind and rain.
Now, what the ruler holds secure and revered
is due to his established authority and effective decrees.
The reason he can establish authority and enforce decrees
is that the control over power and benefit lies entirely with the ruler.
If control over power and benefit is not solely with the ruler,
but is dispersed,
then the ruler becomes increasingly lightweight, and authority and benefits decline daily,
which is the path to invasion and turmoil.
Hence it is said:
"When the three principles are set in order,
the ruler possesses the state."
Riding the growth of summer,
carefully administer punishments and rewards.
One must clarify the order,
set forth righteousness and establish laws,
and decide affairs with principle.
With empty qi and a calm heart,
then remove anger and joy.
If one acts with anger and joy contrary to laws and decrees,
calamity and chaos arise,
and the ruler's position is endangered.
Hence it is said:
"Do not reward out of joy,
nor kill out of anger.
Rewarding out of joy,
killing out of anger,
grievances arise,
and decrees are abandoned.
Repeated decrees that go unenforced
cause the people's hearts to turn outward,
and with external alliances,
calamity begins to sprout.
What the masses resent,
the few cannot handle."
When winter has stored away,
all affairs cease,
past events are fully recorded,
future events have not yet arisen.
While winter is uneventful,
carefully observe the end and beginning,
and scrutinize the principles of affairs.
Some affairs start easy but become difficult later,
some beginnings are unremarkable but endings unattainable.
This is why constant benefits are not realized,
and affairs become troubled.
Affairs that start easy
are taken lightly by people;
if people take them lightly,
they will inevitably face difficult tasks;
beginnings that are unremarkable
are easily abandoned by people;
if people easily abandon them,
they will lose unattainable achievements.
Frequently facing difficult tasks
and often losing unattainable achievements
is the path to decline and exhaustion.
Therefore, the enlightened ruler scrutinizes the principles of affairs,
carefully observes the end and beginning,
so that actions must know their outcomes,
outcomes must know their utility,
and utility must know its benefits and harms.
To act without knowing the outcome,
achieve without knowing the utility,
use without knowing the benefits and harms
is called reckless action.
Reckless action
leads to affairs not accomplished,
and achievements not established.
Hence it is said:
"In promoting what is good, one must observe its end;
in abolishing what is bad, one must consider its limits."
All rulers
desire the people to have ritual and righteousness.
If the people lack ritual and righteousness,
then high and low become chaotic, and noble and base contend.
Hence it is said:
"Reward and encourage diligence and respect to make them evident,
enrich and ennoble the meritorious to motivate them,
honor and title the renowned to glorify them."
All rulers
desire the masses to be close to the superior and follow his intentions,
and to be competent in their tasks.
As for the masses,
without love, they will not be close;
without teaching and guidance, they will not follow intentions.
Therefore, the enlightened ruler loves all to draw them close,
clearly teaches and guides to lead them,
facilitates their circumstances,
benefits their preparations,
cherishes their strength,
and does not rob them of their time, thus benefiting them.
Thus, the masses will be close to the superior and follow his intentions,
and be competent in their tasks.
Hence it is said:
"Love all without omission,
this is called the ruler's heart.
First, follow teaching,
and the myriad people will follow the custom.
Benefit them day and night,
then the masses will be competent."
The foundations of governance are two:
first, people,
second, affairs.
People must be employed,
affairs must be skillful.
People have compliance and opposition,
affairs have measure and weight.
If people's hearts are opposed, they will not be employed;
if measure and weight are lost, affairs will not be skillful.
If affairs are not skillful, there is harm;
if people are not employed, there is resentment.
Hence it is said:
"Employ people as you would yourself,
accomplish affairs with substance."
Accomplishing affairs with substance
means using measure and weight;
employing people as you would yourself
means acting with measured empathy.
Measured empathy
means measuring by oneself;
what one finds unsettling oneself,
do not impose on others.
Hence it is said:
"Examine the use of resources,
carefully give and repay,
scrutinize measure and weight.
Therefore, using resources should not be stingy,
using strength should not be harsh.
Using resources stingily leads to waste,
using strength harshly leads to exhaustion."
How do we know this is so?
Using strength harshly makes affairs unskillful,
When tasks are inefficiently executed yet repeatedly redone,
it is said to be laborious.
Being stingy with resources fails to satisfy people's hearts,
and failing to satisfy them gives rise to resentment.
Using wealth yet breeding resentment,
is thus called wasteful.
Once resentment arises and is not reversed,
with the masses toiling without rest,
they are bound to harbor thoughts of collapse and ruin.
Hence it is said:
"When the people are impoverished,
commands are disgraced;
when the people suffer calamity,
orders go unheeded.
If rewards and retributions are not justly given,
disasters begin to flourish;
if disasters flourish unawares,
the people will take matters into their own hands."
In general, a state without laws leaves the masses unsure of what to do,
and without standards, affairs lack proper form.
If laws exist but are not upright,
or standards are not impartial,
then governance becomes corrupt.
Corrupt governance leads to national chaos.
Therefore it is said:
"With upright laws and impartial standards,
crimes are punished without pardon,
executions and penalties are carried out reliably,
making the people fearful and cautious.
Once martial authority is clearly established,
commands need not be repeated."
All people,
without exception, dislike punishment and fear guilt.
Thus, the ruler uses strict teachings to demonstrate,
and clear penalties to instill respect.
Hence it is said:
"Use labor and hardship to shame them,
punish offenses to chastise them,
execute and penalize violators to震慑 them."
Governing a state relies on three tools,
while a chaotic state faces six assaults.
An enlightened ruler can overcome the six assaults and establish the three tools,
thereby ordering the state;
an unworthy ruler cannot overcome the six assaults or establish the three tools,
so the state remains disordered.
What are the three tools?
They are: commands,
the axe of authority,
and official rewards.
What are the six assaults?
They are: favoritism toward kin,
the noble,
wealth,
beauty,
flattery,
and indulgences.
How are the three tools used?
It is said: without commands, there is no way to direct subordinates;
without the axe, there is no means to awe the masses;
without rewards, there is no way to encourage the people.
How do the six assaults cause ruin?
It is said: if some can survive without obeying,
violate prohibitions yet escape penalty,
or gain wealth without merit,
then if there are those who can survive without obeying,
commands are insufficient to direct subordinates;
if some can violate prohibitions and avoid penalty,
the axe is insufficient to awe the masses;
if some can gain wealth without merit,
rewards are insufficient to encourage the people.
When commands cannot direct subordinates,
the axe cannot awe the masses,
and rewards cannot encourage the people,
the ruler has nothing to secure himself with.
So what should an enlightened ruler do?
He does not alter commands for the six assaults,
hesitate or misapply the axe for them,
nor increase or decrease rewards for them.
Therefore it is said:
"Firmly planted and unmoving,
then deceit and evil fear.
When deceit transforms and evil reforms,
commands go forth and the people follow."
All rulers,
cover and carry the myriad people, possessing them wholly,
illuminate all clans and employ them.
