from conduct, they exhaust the way without losing righteousness;
from the Yì, they maintain the distinction between fortune and misfortune, good and bad without confusion.
This is called the ruler's control."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"I have heard about the methods of power and control,
but how to secure the state firmly?"
He said:
"If all talents are officially appointed,
all timings are officially managed,
the principles of gain and loss,
the beginning and end of all things,
are all under the ruler's official control,
then everything else can be managed through methods."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'managed through methods' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Grain is the people's lifeline,
wisdom is the people's support.
If the people are wise and the ruler foolish,
the lower levels rich and the ruler poor,
or the lower levels poor and the ruler rich,
this is called the duality of affairs.
The state's mechanism
lies only in the pace of speed and slowness.
The way of the ruler
is about setting laws and standards.
For the people's hearts,
it is about prohibiting errors."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'setting laws and standards' mean?
And what does 'prohibiting errors' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"'Setting laws and standards' means
measuring people's capabilities to undertake tasks.
'Prohibiting errors' means
learning from the past to warn the future.
Thus, disasters do not arise and spread,
and the people are free from calamity and blame."
Duke Huán said:
"Please explain the prohibitions of the heart."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In Jìn, there were ministers disloyal to their ruler,
plotting to kill their lord,
which was called a public offense.
Families involved in such public offenses
must not be allowed to serve the ruler.
This was Jìn's error.
In Qí, for public offenses,
establish clear hierarchies in seating and standing,
so that evil is met with punishment,
and goodness with honor.
This is a warning.
This is called the state's warning."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"The balancing of light and heavy has been implemented,
are the strategies exhausted here?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Not yet.
We will harness spirits and utilize treasures."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'harnessing spirits and utilizing treasures' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In the northern outskirts, someone dug and unearthed a turtle,
which can secure an area of several hundred lǐ."
Duke Huán said:
"How can obtaining a turtle secure a hundred lǐ of land?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"For the one who obtained the turtle in the northern outskirts,
have it placed on a flat plate.
I ask the ruler to send an envoy with ten chariots,
carrying a hundred jīn of gold,
and command the family that found the turtle in the northern outskirts:
'We bestow upon you the robes of a middle-ranking official.'"
Said:
'The son of the East Sea resembles a turtle,
entrusted to dwell with you.
I bestow upon you the robes of a senior official
to last your lifetime,
and reward you with a hundred jīn of gold.'
This turtle was deemed priceless,
and stored in the grand tower,
fed daily with four oxen,
designated a treasure called 'Priceless.'
Four years later,
when attacking Gūzhú,
the grain from the Dīng family's stores
could feed the army's troops
for five months.
Summoning Dīng, he commanded:
'I possess this Priceless treasure here,
and now I am about to undertake a great campaign,
so I ask to pledge the treasure to you
in exchange for your local grain.'
Dīng faced north and bowed twice, then provided the grain,
not daring to accept the treasure as pledge.
Duke Huán ordered Dīng:
'I am old,
and as my subject, you do not understand this calculation.
Accept my pledge!'
Dīng returned,
renovated his house, and prepared a place to store the turtle.
Four years later,
during the campaign against Gūzhú,
the grain from the Dīng family
supplied the army's food for five months.
Duke Huán established tribute rates:
patterned tortoise shells were valued at seven thousand gold,
turtles at four thousand gold,
and black-and-white young ones worth a thousand gold.
In the tribute system,
these values matched two Qí territories'
revenues. The use of tribute:
in national danger, treasures are deployed;
in national stability, they circulate.'
Duke Huán asked:
'What is meant by circulation?'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'If goods are hoarded,
then the ruler loses control and the people lose their livelihood.
Thus, those skilled at governing the world
operate beyond two types of hoarding.'
Duke Huán said:
'What are the two types of hoarding beyond?'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'A state of ten thousand chariots
must not lack reserves worth ten thousand gold;
a state of a thousand chariots
must not lack reserves worth a thousand gold;
a state of a hundred chariots
must not lack reserves worth a hundred gold.
Using this to order advance or retreat,
this is called seizing the moment.'
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
'Liáng Jù told me:
"In ancient times, they lightened taxes and reduced levies,
and there was no better way to govern the people."
What about Liáng Jù's words?'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'Liáng Jù's words are wrong.
If taxes are lightened,
granaries will be empty;
if levies are reduced,
tools and weapons will not be supplied,
and the lords' fur and silk gifts will not be worn;
empty granaries
mean officials and commoners have no stipends.
Externally, fur and silk gifts are not worn in the realm;
internally, the state's officials and commoners are impoverished.
Liáng Jù's words are wrong.
If you possess mountains,
and the mountains have metal, you can establish currency.
Using currency to value grain and assign stipends,
thus the state's grain is controlled above,
and grain prices increase tenfold.
Farmers rise early and retire late, without needing to be ordered,
and the five grains multiply tenfold.
Officers serve their lord unto death on half stipends,
farmers rise early and retire late,
laboring without cease.
Those skilled at governing the state
do not say "make them serve,"
but make it so they cannot but serve;
do not say "use them,"
but make it so they cannot but be used.
Thus, the people have no choice but to serve.
Liáng Jù's words are wrong.'
Duke Huán said:
'Good.'
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ again:
'Someone advised me,
calling it "seeking talents."
Saying:
"Why not appoint a hundred skilled men?"'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'What is meant by a hundred skilled men?'
Duke Huán said:
'Make the wise exhaust their wisdom,
strategists exhaust their schemes,
artisans exhaust their skills.
Can the state be governed thus?'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'The advice on seeking talents is wrong.
If stipends are generous, officers will not die for duty;
if currency is devalued, officers will disdain rewards;
if goods are cheap, officers will seek easy gains.
With three indolences in the state,
what strategy is there?
If grain is seven-tenths stored above,
and three-tenths circulates below,
strategists will exhaust their plans,
wise men will exhaust their knowledge,
brave men will lightly face death.
The advice on seeking talents is reckless talk.
Those who do not understand light and heavy
speak recklessly.'
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
'In the past, the Zhōu ruled the world,
lords paid homage,
their teachings spread throughout the realm,
yet they were overthrown by their subordinates.
What strategy caused this?'
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'The ruler allocated territories for tribute,
and markets and courts flowed together.
Gold was one measure;
pearls from Jiāngyáng were another;
céngqīng from the Míng Mountains of Qín was another.
This is called making little into much,
narrow into broad.
It pertains to light and heavy.'
Duke Huán said:
'Are the world's strategies all encompassed
in light and heavy?'
Guǎnzǐ said: 'Now, if state grain is valued tenfold and other goods are light,
senior officials tell merchants: "Transport grain for us and gather wealth."
Grain's weight is one,
but now nine parts are surplus.
With grain heavy and goods light,
thus,
nine-tenths of state wealth lies with senior officials.
When the state's harvest reverses to one,
the nine-tenths of goods
all double in weight and flow out.
With goods below,
nine-tenths of currency is with senior officials.
Thus, currency and grain surplus rest with them.
The Son of Heaven acts as a guest,
issuing orders seasonally.
Those skilled in grain matters vanish,
and lords take them into office.
They form cliques and gather allies,
manipulating goods' prices
to suit public use.
Internally, senior officials act for themselves and lack loyalty;
externally, lords form cliques and alliances.
Those skilled in grain matters then flee.
Hence, the Son of Heaven loses his authority.'
Duke Huán said:
'Good.'
Duke Huán again asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Is there a way to possess the realm for life without losing it?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I ask that you not apply it to the realm,
but apply it solely to our state."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The breadth and narrowness of the state,
the fertility and barrenness of its soil
have their measures,
as does the surplus of food year-round.
Those who guard the state merely guard its grain.
Say: the soil of such a county is broad to such extent,
the soil of such a county is narrow to such extent,
then we must accumulate stored currency,
whereby the counties, districts, and villages receive public funds.
In great autumn, when the state's grain decreases by one-third,
the ruler orders the commanderies, counties, and subordinate officials
in every village and town to register how much grain is collected.
The price of grain is unified,
and what is stored by the superiors:
of the state's grain, two-thirds
are then in the hands of the superiors.
In great spring, the state's grain doubles in price—this is strategic.
In great summer,
grain is levied to regulate the market,
and the people all receive grain from the superiors to cultivate the fields.
In great autumn,
it is declared:
'The grain stored with us amounts to such and such,
now the superiors collect grain using currency.'
The people say:
'We have no currency,
we use grain.'
Then two-thirds of the people's grain returns to the superiors.
Price fluctuations influence each other,
seasonal changes are utilized—
all serve the state's strategies.
The ruler uses the reserves of the high officials to circulate back to the superiors.
The ruler employs the people,
timely returning to the ruler.
Storing when light,
releasing light to become heavy—this is strategic.
Then how could there be high officials who independently hoard their reserves?
If the grain of other feudal states is ten,
and our state's grain is twenty,
then the grain of feudal states flows to our state;
if the grain of feudal states is twenty,
and our state's grain is ten,
then our state's grain flows to the feudal states.
Therefore, those skilled at governing the realm
carefully maintain the flow of high prices,
and the realm does not drain from us.
That flow toward high prices
is like water seeking lower ground.
Our state's harvest is not poor,
but we store it using currency,
thus the state's grain doubles in price,
hence the grain of feudal states arrives.
This is storing one part to attract one part from the feudal states.
Benefits are not seized by the realm,
and high officials cannot become extravagantly wealthy.
Storing light with heavy,
the state constantly possesses the strategy of ten states.
Thus feudal states submit without end,
and ministers follow with loyalty.
This is the way to control the realm through light and heavy policies,
called strategic response."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"May I ask about state administration?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"If the ruler loses the high officials, he has no organization;
if he loses the people, he loses his foundation.
Therefore, control the high officials with county strategies,
control a county with township strategies,
control a township with household strategies,
control a household with individual strategies."
Duke Huán said:
"How are these administrative measures calculated?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The measure of currency standards:
a county must have a strategy for medium-grade land,
a township must have a strategy for medium-grade land,
a household must have provisions for suitable individuals.
Thus, not guarding the commandery in time means having no support,
not guarding the township in time means having no organization."
Duke Huán said:
"How is this implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Kings store wealth among the people,
hegemons store wealth among the high officials,
while ruined states and perished families store wealth in coffers."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'storing among the people' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Take the money from Zhàntái
and distribute it in Chéngyáng;
take the cloth from Lùtái
and distribute it in Jǐyīn.
The ruler should issue an order to the common people:
'When the people are wealthy, the ruler is not poor;
when the people are poor, the ruler is not wealthy.
Therefore, we levy no money or cloth taxes,
the treasury stores no wealth,
all assets are stored among the people.'
In abundant years, when the five grains are harvested,
the five grains become very cheap,
grain prices drop compared to previous years, so we support them with currency,
grain belongs to the ruler,
currency belongs to the people.
When state currency is entirely among the people,
currency becomes light, grain becomes heavy—the superiors' share.
Two parts from abundant years remain with the people,
two parts from lean years go to the superiors,
thus over two years, four parts accumulate with the superiors.
Then only one part of the state's grain remains with the people,
and grain becomes three times more expensive.
The state cloth tax
amounts to ten coins per year.
Households receiving food: ten mu plus ten,
this means ten households per unit.
This emerges from state grain strategies and storage through currency.
Using the state currency share to again distribute among the people,
reduces state grain by four parts,
three with the superiors,
one with the people.
This is counter-strategy.
When high officials pile up coffins for burial,
accumulating goods while arrogantly opposing the superiors,
we request to seize them through administration."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'seizing through administration' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When two-thirds of the grain is with the superiors,
meaning the common people all receive grain from above,
measure what the ruler stores.
When the five grains compete and become heavy,
reduce by thirty percent,
the remainder uses state currency to counter grain standards,
leaving high officials no leverage over prices.
The ruler uses currency to pay salaries,
keeping seventy percent with the superiors.
The ruler releases grain,
seventy percent distributed,
the ruler collects thirty percent,
superiors levy seventy percent,
distributing to aid the destitute—
this is benevolence and righteousness.
When the five grains compete and become light,
this is strategic;
using township management to stabilize prices and register the state,
this is strategic;
releasing real wealth,
spreading benevolence and righteousness,
all goods become light,
this is strategic.
Advance and retreat according to the timing.
Therefore it is said:
'Kings ride the timing,
sages ride the changes.'"
Duke Huán said:
"Excellent."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"I was specially instructed:
'The Son of Heaven has three hundred burial garments,
extremely frugal.
And distribute to high officials
according to this standard.'
What about this?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
The people cannot weave fine silks
and bury them in the ground.
Those adept at governing a state
merely adapt to the times with measured pace.
This is called the state's fiscal policy. "
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ,
"May I ask how contention and seizure occur?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"It begins with kinship."
Duke Huán said,
"What does 'beginning with kinship' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ answered,
"A ruler of men,
if he has ten brothers,
divides the state into ten;
if he has five brothers,
divides it into five.
After three generations, ancestral temples share the same lineage;
after ten generations, they become ancestral shrines.
Thus, corpses fill the plains,
and warfare decides without cease.
Experts in economic balance
wander among them again.
Hence it is said:
'Do not grant others land,
nor bestow upon them wealth.
Wealth ends only to begin anew,
rising and falling with the four seasons.
The sage regulates it with measured pace,
guards it with openings and closures,
seizes it through economic balance,
and implements it with benevolence and righteousness.
Thus, it aligns with the eternity of heaven and earth,
this is the great reins of a true king.' "
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ,
"May I ask about the currency chariot system?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"Start with a household of three men,
an area of six lǐ provides one chariot,
with twenty-seven men supporting one chariot.
The currency chariot system means:
for an area of six lǐ,
considering the quality of the land,
the amount of grain produced,
the price of grain,
the total currency used in six lǐ,
the weight of grain
determines the currency used.
Thus, the currency chariot system
distributes currency throughout the state,
with currency matching the land area of the state,
called the currency chariot system."
Duke Huán said,
"How is the currency chariot system implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"Officials receive stipends in currency,
nobles receive fiefs in currency,
men and horses receive provisions in currency,
then all grain assets of the state are with the ruler,
while currency assets are with the people.
State grain prices increase tenfold,
this is strategic.
All goods and assets decrease by two-tenths,
this is policy.
Leather, sinews, horns,
feathers, bamboo arrows,
tools, and assets,
if suitable for state use or the ruler's needs,
all have contracts with the government.
The ruler stores them in villages and districts.
Saying:
'On such month and day,
those fulfilling obligations,
villages and districts settle accounts.'
Hence it is said:
'Hire labor and settle in a day.
State policy derives from grain standards,
the state's policy on goods,
is the currency chariot system.
Now coins are stored in government offices,
the value of currency and all goods
lies with merchants.
When currency is heavy, goods are light;
when currency is light, goods are heavy.
When currency is light, grain is heavy;
when currency is heavy, grain is light.
If the ruler controls grain, currency, and standards,
the world can be stabilized.
This is the method to maintain the realm.' "
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ,
"Standards, economic balance, and state fiscal policy—
I have heard of these.
May I ask about the district administration system?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"From Lángmǔ to Fénghuì's pass,
north of Lóngxià
to Hǎizhuāng,
these are lands for wild animals, sheep, and cattle—
why not use this to implement state policy?"
Duke Huán said,
"What does 'implement state policy' mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"At Féng market gate, an official records livestock
on duty. If those managing
stable and pasture workers
care for them without loss or death,
remove their capital salaries
and district salaries.
Nobles not gathering for village livestock inspections,
are deemed without ritual propriety;
nobles are restricted in seasonal ceremonies,
commoners restricted in gate and mountain sacrifices.
Fénghuì and Lóngxià cattle and sheep for sacrifice
cost ten times more monthly than before.
This emerges from ritual propriety,
drawing resources from unused lands,
through pen and stable policies.
This is called implementation."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ,
"May I ask about state terrain types?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"There are mountainous states,
low-lying watery states,
states with mixed mountains and plains,
states with flooding waters,
and states with leaky soil.
These are the five terrain types of states,
which rulers worry about.
Mountainous states
should store one-third of grain.
Low-lying watery states
should control one-third of state grain.
States with mixed terrain
should control three-tenths of state grain.
Where water sources cause damage,
flooding states
should control two-tenths.
Leaky soil states
carefully acquire grain from other lords.
Using crafted carved catalpa utensils
to obtain grain from the realm,
this is the method for balancing the five terrain types."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ,
"Now with the realm within the seas,
administering over lords,
are state terrain types no longer relevant?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"Now treat the lords as pipes
for surplus from public districts,
to ride the four seasons,
implement pen and stable policies,
interconnect east, west, south, and north,
using balance for standardization.
Hence it is said:
'As a lord among lords,
adjust goods' prices to respond to them.
Ruling the entire realm,
then use currency taxes to stabilize goods' fluctuations,
merely adjusting.
When profits suffice, act;
when insufficient, halt.
The king inspects villages and districts timely,
so profits don't conflict,
and districts stabilize firmly.
The ruler maintains great support unified,
called the state ledger.' "
Duke Huán said,
"May I hear about geographical numbers?"
Guǎnzǐ replied,
"The land spans twenty-eight thousand lǐ east-west,
twenty-six thousand lǐ north-south.
Eight thousand lǐ have outflowing waters,
eight thousand lǐ receive waters.
There are 467 mountains yielding copper,
3,609 mountains yielding iron."
This is the reason for dividing land to cultivate grains,
the origin of spears and halberds,
and the beginning of coinage.
The capable have surplus,
while the inept face shortages.
Those who performed the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tài
and the Shàn sacrifice on Liángfù,
the kings who conducted these ceremonies
numbered seventy-two families.
The principles of gain and loss
all lie within this.
This is called state expenditure."
Duke Huán asked:
"What does it mean that the principles of gain and loss all lie within this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In the past, Jié dominated the world
yet faced insufficient resources,
while Tāng possessed only seventy lǐ of Bó
but had abundant resources.
Heaven did not exclusively rain beans and millet for Tāng,
nor did earth uniquely produce wealth for him.
Yī Yǐn excelled at circulation, balancing values,
opening and closing, and regulating blockages,
mastering strategies for adjusting prices and flows
through timely interventions.
Huángdì asked Bó Gāo:
'I wish to mold the world into one family,
is there a way to achieve this?'
Bó Gāo replied:
'Please cut the reeds and plant anew,
I carefully avoid their sharp edges,
then the world can be molded into one family.'
Huángdì said:
'Can I hear more about this?'
Bó Gāo replied:
'Where cinnabar is found above,
gold lies below;
where magnetite is found above,
copper and gold lie below;
where hill stones are found above,
lead, tin, and red copper lie below;
where ochre is found above,
iron lies below,
these are the manifestations of the mountain's vitality.
If a mountain shows such vitality,
the ruler should strictly enclose it and offer sacrifices.
Establish an altar ten lǐ from the enclosure,
requiring riders to dismount,
and walkers to hasten.
Those who violate the order
shall be executed without pardon.
Thus, unauthorized extraction is prevented.'
After ten years of cultivation,
Gélú Mountain erupted with water,
and metals followed,
which Chī Yóu received and forged,
into swords, armor, spears, and halberds.
That year, nine feudal lords were annexed.
When Yōnghú Mountain erupted with water,
and metals followed,
Chī Yóu received and forged them,
into Yōnghú halberds and Ruì spears,
that year, twelve feudal lords were annexed.
Hence, when the rulers of the world
raise their halberds in anger,
corpses fill the fields,
this reveals the root of weaponry."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"May I ask where natural wealth emerges?
Where the benefits of the earth lie?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Where ochre is found on mountains,
iron lies below;
where lead is found above,
silver lies below.
Another saying:
'Where lead is found above,
lump silver lies below;
where cinnabar is found above,
lump gold lies below;
where magnetite is found above,
copper and gold lie below.'
These are the manifestations of the mountain's vitality.
If a mountain shows such vitality,
strictly enclose it and prohibit access.
Those who disturb the sealed mountain
shall be executed without pardon.
Those who violate the order:
if the left foot enters,
cut off the left foot;
if the right foot enters,
cut off the right foot.
Thus, violations are deterred.
This is where natural wealth and earthly benefits reside."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Who has achieved merit and fame under heaven
through natural wealth and earthly benefits?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"King Wén and King Wǔ are such examples."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Jade originates from Niúshì Border Mountain,
gold from the marshes on the right of Rǔ and Hàn Rivers,
pearls from the distant light of Chìyě.
These are all seven to eight thousand lǐ from Zhōu,
with long and difficult routes.
Thus, the ancient kings utilized what was most valuable,
using pearls and jade as high currency,
gold as medium currency,
and knife coins and cloth money as low currency.
When decrees are urgent, gold becomes heavier;
when decrees are relaxed, gold becomes lighter.
The ancient kings measured the urgency of their decrees,
adjusted the value of medium currency
to regulate upper and lower uses,
thus King Wén and King Wǔ did so."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"I wish to conserve the state's wealth
without taxing the people,
yet externally rely on the world, is this possible?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Yes.
Just as water, when agitated, forms channels,
so decrees, when urgent, make goods valuable.
The ancient kings managed the urgency of their decrees,
internally conserving state wealth
while externally relying on the world."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"How was this done in practice?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In the past, King Wǔ had the grain of Jùqiáo,
and the method of expensive grain purchases."
Duke Huán said:
"How was it done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"King Wǔ established the Chóngquán garrison,
decreeing:
'Those among the people who own a hundred gǔ of grain are exempt from service.'
The people competed to hoard grain
to avoid the Chóngquán garrison duty,
causing state grain prices to rise twentyfold,
and Jùqiáo's grain also increased twentyfold.
King Wǔ used Jùqiáo's grain, now twenty times more valuable, to trade for silk,
so the army did not requisition clothing from the people for five years.
Using Jùqiáo's grain at twentyfold value to balance a million in gold,
he never had to tax the people again.
This is the method of balancing."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Can this be implemented now?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Yes.
Chǔ has the gold of Rǔ and Hàn Rivers,
Qí has the salt of Qúzhǎn,
Yān has the boiled salt of Liáodōng.
These three can also serve like King Wǔ's method.
A family of ten,
ten people consume salt;
a family of a hundred,
a hundred people consume salt.
Regarding salt consumption,
adult men use five shēng and a small half per month,
women three shēng and a small half,
infants two shēng and a small half.
For the weight of salt,
adding a fēn hào per shēng makes the fǔ fifty,
adding one hào per shēng makes the fǔ a hundred,
adding ten hào per shēng makes the fǔ a thousand.
The ruler cuts marsh firewood
to boil Jǐ water into salt,
properly accumulating thirty thousand zhōng,
until spring
then impose a levy at that time."
Duke Huán said:
"What is meant by 'taxing according to the season'?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In spring when farming work is just beginning,
order the people not to build walls,
not to repair grave mounds;
officials should not construct palaces,
nor erect towers and pavilions.
The masses in the northern sea regions should not hire laborers to boil salt.
Then the price of salt will inevitably increase fortyfold.
With this fortyfold price increase,
follow the flow of the Hé and Jǐ rivers,
transporting south to Liáng, Zhào, Sòng, Wèi, and Púyáng.
Poor food without salt causes swelling,
the foundation of defending borders,
makes salt particularly important.
You can gather reeds and firewood
to boil river water and thereby tax the world,
yet the world will not diminish."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"I wish to enrich agriculture and have abundant grain, is this possible?"
Guǎnzǐ responded:
"It is not.
If agriculture is wealthy and goods are plentiful, but cannot be protected,
then you will be taxed by the world.
Even if the five grains flourish abundantly,
if our prices are low while the world's are high,
we will be taxed by the world,
and thus our people will constantly be preyed upon by others.
Those skilled in using fundamentals,
are like crossing the sea by boat,
observing where the wind rises.
When the world's prices are high, ours should be high;
when the world's prices are low, ours should be low.
If the world's prices are high while ours are low,
then wealth and profits will be taxed away by the world."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Is this all there is to governing?"
Guǎnzǐ responded:
"Not yet.
Qí's position as a transportation hub,
is where all routes converge,
the path for travelers and successful merchants.
Those who come to our base,
consume our grain,
use our currency,
then fine horses and gold
flow out. By adjusting policies with flexibility,
and manipulating commodity values,
then all treasures under heaven can be used for our benefit.
The skilled use what they don't possess,
and employ those who aren't their people."
Duke Huán of Qí asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Since Suìrén's time,
can you tell me about the great assemblies?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Since Suìrén, none have failed to use economic control to govern the world.
During Gònggōng's reign,
water covered seven-tenths of the land,
land only three-tenths,
yet he used natural advantages to control the world.
By the time of Huángdì's rule,
he carefully restrained his military forces,
blunted their weapons,
burned forests,
destroyed marshes,
set fire to lush wetlands,
drove away wild beasts,
to enrich human settlements,
only then could the world be governed.
As for Yáo and Shùn's rule,
their method of transforming the realm was:
using jade from Yùshì in the north,
valuing pearls from Jiāng and Hàn rivers in the south,
their superiority over wild beasts
was maintained by having officials follow them."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The order stated:
'All sons of feudal lords presenting themselves for service,
must bring pairs of tiger skins,
high officials use leopard trim,
regular officials use leopard aprons.'
Officials would disperse their grain stores
and their wealth
to purchase tiger and leopard skins,
thus mountain dwellers hunted fierce beasts
as if pursuing family enemies.
Thus while the ruler wore ceremonial robes at court,
fierce beasts were subdued abroad.
Once officials had dispersed their wealth,
thousands could benefit from its circulation.
This was Yáo and Shùn's method."
Duke Huán said:
"'Two categories of affairs,
five standards of correctness
bring order to the world' -
what are the 'two categories of affairs'?"
He replied:
"Heavenly measures
pertain to yang,
earthly measures
pertain to yin -
these are the 'two categories of affairs'."
"What are the 'five standards of correctness'?"
He replied:
"Scale, balance, compass, square, and level -
these are the 'five standards of correctness'.
In colors they are:
green, yellow, white, black, and red.
In sounds they are:
gōng, shāng, yǔ, zhǐ, and jué.
In tastes they are:
sour, pungent, salty, bitter, and sweet.
These two fives,
even with barren mountains and drained marshes,
enable rulers to control people through measurement.
Tastes
control what enters people's mouths,
sounds
control what reaches people's ears,
colors
control what meets people's eyes.
If rulers lose these two fives,
they lose their states;
if officials lose them,
they lose their power;
if commoners lose them,
they lose their homes.
This is the state's crucial mechanism,
called the state's pivot."
The law of economic control states:
"Those who claim ability to be Marshal but prove incapable,
shall be killed and their blood used to anoint drums;
those who claim ability to manage farmland but prove incapable,
shall be killed and their blood used to anoint altars;
those who claim ability to be officials but prove incapable,
shall be mutilated and made gatekeepers."
Thus none dare falsely claim ability to deceive the ruler for salary.
Therefore when recommending officials for positions,
even those failing at basic duties like gatekeeping,
are dealt with according to law.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Please explain losing economic control."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Losing economic control means
the whole world controls us while we have no control ourselves.
This is called
losing economic control."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"If now the world raises armies against us,
ministers who can strategize to strengthen the state and stabilize the people,
will be granted territories;
ministers who achieve success and fame through military campaigns,
will be granted territories.
Thus the whole world ends up enfeoffing your ministers,
not you enfeoffing them.
When the world has already enfeoffed your ministers with ten lǐ,
every time the world moves,
it doubly enfeoffs your people with twenty lǐ.
Your people don't become wealthy themselves,
neighboring states make them wealthy.
Every time neighboring states act,
they doubly enrich your people,
making the poor poorer,
the rich richer.
This is the method of losing economic control."
Duke Huán said:
"What does that mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Now if the world raises armies against us,
the people abandon their plows,
and take up weapons abroad,
then the state cannot farm.
This is not a calamity from Heaven,
but a calamity from man.
When the ruler issues orders in the morning and demands fulfillment by evening,
the people recklessly sell their goods
and grain
to enemies, then leave in disgust.
Merchants take and store them,
so one portion of the state's wealth ends up with merchants.
When the army is disbanded,
the people return to their work,
and all goods return to their proper weight.
Merchants release their stored goods,
and a small portion of state currency is stored with merchants.
In this way,
currency becomes three-tenths heavier,
while goods become three-tenths lighter.
When merchants trade within this three-tenth margin,
the state's wealth
entirely falls to merchants,
and the ruler has no strategy.
The people control each other,
and the ruler has no involvement.
This is losing the standard of light and heavy."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"If the ruler grasps the root,
the people cannot grasp the branches;
if the ruler controls the beginning,
the people cannot control the end.
For those on the roads,
tax them at passes;
for grain,
control it in spring and autumn;
for all goods,
set prices for circulation.
Thus when goods move, respond accordingly.
So if you block their routes in advance,
the people have no way to follow;
if the ruler controls the flow,
the people lose their advantage.
Therefore, by controlling the highs and lows across the land,
the state has no wandering merchants,
prices are balanced,
this is called state balance.
With mutual benefit maintained,
profits repeatedly return to the ruler."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Those who properly regulate commerce
reduce market stalls,
reducing market stalls
makes markets orderly,
orderly markets
fill the fields,
filled fields
make people's wealth sufficient,
sufficient people's wealth
means the ruler's taxes are endless.
Now it's not so,
when people value something, the ruler values it,
valuing but unable to lighten;
when people lighten something, the ruler lightens it,
lightening but unable to value.
The skillful under heaven do otherwise,
when people value, the ruler lightens,
when people lighten, the ruler values.
This is using surplus wealth to fill shortages.
So those who cannot balance people's benefits
cannot achieve great order;
those who don't examine beginnings and ends
cannot reach perfection.
Moving left and right with weight interconnected,
is a strategy for twenty states.
Salt and iron are a strategy for twenty states.
Tin and gold are a strategy for twenty states.
The five officials' methods,
do not tax the people."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Where does the method of light and heavy end?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Like the succession of four seasons,
it has no end.
When the state has worries,
adjust grain's lightness and heaviness to regulate use,
store surplus for rewards.
When all under heaven submit,
and you possess the realm,
enrich sincere, trustworthy, benevolent, and righteous scholars,
so people highly value courtesy,
with no strange behaviors.
That lightness and heaviness,
when feudal lords are disobedient,
use it to go to war;
when feudal lords submit,
use it to practice benevolence and righteousness."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"One year of farming,
supports five years of food,
grain price is fivefold.
One year of farming,
supports six years of food,
grain price is sixfold.
Two years of farming
supports eleven years of food.
To be able to take from the rich,
and give to the poor,
then one can govern the world.
Moreover, the world,
resides here and acts here,
thus
the world can be unified.
The world,
employ them without seeming to employ,
use them without seeming to use.
So those skilled at governing the world,
don't say 'employ them',
but make them unable not to be employed;
don't say 'use them',
but make them unable not to be used."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Those skilled at governing a state,
are like metal and stone balancing -
when weights are equal, metal tips.
So governing with authority brings strong power,
governing by morality brings weak power.
Now if grain is heavy in our state,
but light in the world,
then feudal lords will drain it,
like water seeking low ground.
So when goods are heavy, they come;
when light, they leave.
When something comes because it's heavy
but stays where it's light,
I act and adjust it,
and the world is already under my control.
Goods stored become heavy,
released become light,
dispersed become abundant.
Currency heavy makes people die for profit,
currency light makes them reject its use,
so light and heavy must be balanced by measure."
"The five grains
are the people's lifeline.
Knife-shaped currency
is the channel.
Commands
are the speed control.
"'Commands are heavier than treasure,
the state is heavier than relatives.' What does this mean?"
He replied:
"When city walls are breached,
the state sacrifices cease,
no ministers survive;
after parents pass away,
no sons need die.
This is why the state is heavier than relatives.
So having people without cities
is called guarding emptiness;
having people without armor, weapons, or food
is called dwelling with disaster."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"I hear there are seven strategies for jade currency within the seas;
may I hear about them?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Ruǎnmín from Yīnshān,
is one strategy;
white metal from Yān's Zǐshān,
is one strategy;"
The patterned furs of Fā and Cháoxiǎn,
are one kind of resource;
the yellow gold from the right route of the Rǔ and Hàn rivers,
is one kind of resource;
the pearls from Jiāngyáng,
are one kind of resource;
the azurite from the Qínmíng Mountains,
is one kind of resource;
the jade from the border mountains of the Yùshì,
is one kind of resource.
This is called making the few into many,
and the narrow into broad.
The calculations of the world
are fully encompassed by the principles of light and heavy."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ, saying:
"The horses of Yīnshān
can equip a thousand chariots.
The average price of a horse is ten thousand,
the average price of gold is ten thousand,
I have stored a thousand jīn of gold,
what should I do about this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request that you order those who pay regular taxes to all use currency to redeem gold,
so that we reach forty thousand.
This turns one into four.
It is not that I am molding clay or blowing bellows to create gold;
now the weight of gold turning one into four is a matter of calculation.
Pearls originate from the distant glow of the Chìyě,
gold originates from the right route of the Rǔ and Hàn rivers,
jade originates from the border mountains of the Yùshì.
This distance is seven thousand eight hundred lǐ from Zhōu,
the journey is far,
and the arrival is difficult.
Therefore, the former kings measured the use of their weight and relied on it,
taking pearl and jade as the high currency,
gold as the medium currency,
and knife and cloth coins as the low currency.
The former kings adjusted the value of the medium currency,
to regulate the use of the high and low."
A state of a hundred chariots,
establishes a market in the center,
measuring fifty lǐ east, west, north, and south.
On the first day, plans are settled,
on the second day, loads are determined,
on the third day, they exit the borders,
and on the fifth day, they return.
The regulation for a hundred chariots
in light and heavy matters should not exceed five days.
A hundred chariots correspond to
ten thousand qǐng of cultivated land,
ten thousand households,
a population of one hundred thousand people,
ten thousand people eligible for service,
one hundred light chariots,
and four hundred horses.
A state of a thousand chariots,
establishes a market in the center,
measuring over a hundred and fifty lǐ east, west, north, and south.
On the second day, plans are settled,
on the third day, loads are determined,
on the fifth day, they exit the borders,
and on the tenth day, they return.
The regulation for a thousand chariots
in light and heavy matters should not exceed one xún (ten days).
A thousand chariots correspond to
a hundred thousand qǐng of cultivated land,
a hundred thousand households,
a population of one million people,
a hundred thousand people eligible for service,
a thousand light chariots,
and four thousand horses.
A state of ten thousand chariots,
establishes a market in the center,
measuring five hundred lǐ east, west, north, and south.
On the third day, plans are settled,
on the fifth day, loads are determined,
on the tenth day, they exit the borders,
and on the twentieth day, they return.
The regulation for ten thousand chariots
in light and heavy matters should not exceed two xún (twenty days).
Ten thousand chariots correspond to
a million qǐng of cultivated land,
a million households,
a population of ten million people,
a million people eligible for service,
ten thousand light chariots,
and forty thousand horses."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"A man without a wife is called a widower,
a woman without a husband is called a widow,
and the elderly without children are called the solitary.
If you inquire and there are those whose sons or younger brothers died in military service,
leaving their parents solitary,
the state must bury them:
with three sets of burial clothes,
coffin wood of three cùn thickness,
local officials overseeing the affairs,
buried in public land.
If someone has no brothers at birth,
the state must grant them land for a horse.
Thus, parents sacrificing their sons for the state's use
do not suffer.
The ruler travels through cities and villages all year.
Those whose人力 (labor power) is the same but have beautiful houses
are good subjects,
diligent workers;
grant them two bundles of dried meat
and one dàn of wine.
Those with sufficient strength
who wander idly and do not work,
the elderly should admonish them,
and those in their prime should be sent to guard the borders.
Those without means of livelihood should be loaned garden land.
Thus, all tasks are accomplished,
with no people retaining strength or losing time.
These are all methods of state policy."
Superior farmers support five,
average farmers support four,
inferior farmers support three.
Superior women clothe five,
average women clothe four,
inferior women clothe three.
Farmers have constant occupations,
women have constant tasks.
If one farmer does not plow,
there will be people who starve because of it;
if one woman does not weave,
there will be people who freeze because of it.
Hunger, cold, and freezing starvation,
must arise from the soil,
so the former kings were cautious at the beginning.
If endeavors double their capital,
the people will not sell their children.
If they triple their capital,
they have enough to eat.
If they quadruple their capital,
then the villages are supplied.
If they quintuple their capital,
then near and far communicate,
and only then can the dead be buried.
If endeavors cannot double their capital,
and the ruler's demands are endless,
then the path of crime
cannot be avoided alone,
and goods and wealth are not secure in storage.
If law follows,
it then internally harms the people.
If light and heavy are not regulated,
the people without gruel cannot be held responsible for order,
those who sell their children cannot be employed,
the ruler loses his people,
fathers lose their sons,
this is the way to a doomed state.
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Shénnóng's method says:
'If one grain does not harvest,
reduce one grain;
the price of grain increases tenfold.
If two grains do not harvest,
reduce two grains;
the price of grain increases twentyfold.'
Fill it with coarse grains,
give the old grain to those without food,
lend new grain to those without seed,
thus there will be no tenfold prices,
and no people paying double interest."
Duke Huán of Qí asked Guǎn Zhòng:
"May I hear about the state's economic regulation?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"State economic regulation
establishes measures according to the times."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'establish measures according to the times' mean?"
He replied:
"When the Yellow Emperor ruled,
he carefully kept his military forces hidden.
When Yǒuyú ruled,
he drained marshes and denuded mountains.
When the Xiàhòu rulers governed,
they burned thick marshes
and set fire to lush wetlands,
not increasing the people's benefits.
When the Yīn people ruled,
the feudal lords had no enclosures for oxen and horses,
and did not sharpen their tools.
When the Zhōu people governed,
they appointed capable officials to prepare resources.
These five ruling houses' methods differed but their purpose was the same."
Duke Huán said:
"Then among these five houses' methods, which was best?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Burning mountains and forests,
destroying thick marshes,
and setting fire to lush wetlands
were because wild animals were numerous.
Denuding mountains and draining marshes
showed the ruler's wisdom was insufficient.
Burning thick marshes
and setting fire to lush wetlands
without increasing the people's benefits,
hiding weapons and tools,
and suppressing knowledge and ability
were to strengthen oneself.
The feudal lords having no enclosures for oxen and horses
and not sharpening their tools
was to prevent excessive implements and unify the people's hearts.
Using men to control men,
keeping weapons hidden,
elevating benevolence and righteousness,
and relying on natural advantages
were to secure oneself.
These five houses' methods differed but their purpose was the same."
Duke Huán said:
"What should the current ruler
establish as appropriate?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"I request to use all five methods combined but not exhaustively."
Duke Huán said:
"What does that mean?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Establish sacrificial sites to secure mountains and marshes,
establish tools and implements to utilize all things,
benefit all under heaven
while carefully controlling important policies.
Denude mountains and drain marshes,
increase benefits and concentrate flows.
Produce metal from mountains to establish currency,
preserve marshy mounds,
establish paired enclosures,
to provide abundance for the people.
Those marshy and weedy lands,
though not suitable for growing the five grains,
are grounds for elk, deer, oxen and horses.
In spring and autumn collect taxes on livestock and manage aging,
establish distribution to protect the five grains,
thereby using useless land to store the people's surplus.
The methods of the five houses
should all be used but not exhaustively."
Duke Huán said:
"The kings of five dynasties
have exhausted the methods of all under heaven;
may I hear about
the kings of future generations?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Be fond of criticism but not chaotic,
frequently change but not capricious,
act when the time comes,
abandon when past.
The king's methods cannot be predetermined.
This is the state economic regulation of the five houses."
Duke Huán said:
"Are there fixed measures for light and heavy?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"There are no fixed measures for light and heavy.
Respond as things emerge,
ride opportunities as signals are heard.
Therefore, if governing a state cannot attract the wealth of all under heaven,
or gather the people of all under heaven,
then the state cannot be established."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'attract the wealth of all under heaven' mean?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"In the time of Jié of old,
he had thirty thousand female musicians,
whose noisy morning music
could be heard in the three main streets,
and there were none who didn't wear embroidered clothing.
Yī Yǐn had the wandering women of Bó
skillfully make embroidered silks and woven bands,
exchanging one bolt for a hundred zhōng of grain from Jié's state.
Now Jié's state
was the Son of Heaven's state.
Jé had no concern for all under heaven,
adorning himself with the music of women, bells and drums,
so Yī Yǐn obtained his grain and diverted its flow.
This is called attracting the wealth of all under heaven."
Duke Huán said:
"What does 'gather the people of all under heaven' mean?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Have each district maintain a storehouse,
each neighborhood accumulate five cellars.
For people unable to pay regular taxes
grant long-term loans,
for those who die without burial
grant long-term assistance.
When the hungry get food,
the cold get clothing,
the dead get burial,
and the destitute get relief,
then those under heaven will come to us like flowing water.
This is called gathering the people of all under heaven.
Therefore the sage is good at using what isn't his,
employing those who aren't his people,
moving them with words and swaying them with speech,
so that the myriad people can be won over and become close."
Duke Huán said:
"Excellent."
Duke Huán asked Guǎn Zhòng:
"Tāng with his seventy lǐ of Bó
annexed Jié's empire -
what was the reason for this?"
Guǎn Zhòng replied:
"Under Jié,
no bridges were built in winter,
no rafts bound in summer,
so he could watch people freeze and drown.
He let loose tigresses to fill the markets,
to watch people panic in terror.
When it came to Tāng, it wasn't like this.
He gathered and stored grain from distant lands,
fed the hungry,
clothed the cold,
relieved the destitute,
and all under heaven came to Tāng like flowing water.
This is why Jié lost his empire."
Duke Huán said:
"Jé allowed Tāng to accomplish this -
what was the reason?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"Nǚ Huá
was loved by Jié,
and Tāng served her with a thousand pieces of gold;
Qū Nì
was favored by Jié,
and Tāng served him with a thousand pieces of gold.
Internally there was Nǚ Huá's feminine influence,
externally there was Qū Nì's masculine influence,
when the counsel of feminine and masculine joined,
he was able to become the Son of Heaven.
This was Tāng's hidden scheme."
Duke Huán said:
"The principles of economic control,
the distinctions in national standards,
I have already heard about them.
May I ask how to employ military force?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Five battles lead to the use of soldiers."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this statement mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I refer to battling in market balance, battling in standards, battling in flow, battling in authority, and battling in momentum.
This is what is meant by 'five battles lead to the use of soldiers'."
Duke Huán said:
"Excellent."
Duke Huán wished to reward the descendants of those who died in service,
saying:
"Our state,
being a crossroads country,
a capital dependent on imported food,
is a dwelling place for tigers and wolves.
Now in every battle,
we carry back the dead and support the wounded.
As for orphans:
the grandchildren with heads like thistledown,
looking up to the treasures of erected halberds,
I have no means to provide for them.
What should be done about this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The powerful families of our state:
those who dwell with transferred fiefs and food estates,
if the ruler marks them with goods,
then goods become heavy;
if not marked with goods,
then goods become light;
if guarded with goods,
then goods become heavy;
if not guarded with goods,
then goods become light.
Thus those with transferred fiefs, food estates,
wealthy merchants, hoarding traders,
accumulators, storers of surplus and reserves—these hoarding families,
these are the powerful of our state.
Therefore, I ask the ruler to don plain white silk and go to the scholars' chamber,
summon the meritorious officials, hereditary families, those with transferred fiefs, food estates, accumulators, storers of surplus and reserves—these hoarding families,
and say:
'Fat city walls attract assaults,
cities without supplies invite sieges.
When the world has concerns,
how can Qí alone not participate in the planning?
My lords who have the five grains and beans,
do not dare to move them left or right,
I ask to purchase them from you at fair prices.'
With them, fix the notches on the tallies and contracts.
The measures in fǔ and qú,
must not be excessive or deficient.
The impoverished people,
hearing of this, will come to buy grain,
and the fǔ and qú measures will not cease,
reaching far without pushing.
The price of the state's grain
will rise fortyfold while sitting still.
The ruler then takes out this fortyfold-priced grain
to relieve the orphans and widows,
gather in the poor and sick,
look after the solitary aged,
the destitute without sons,
so that they need not sell themselves to be cared for,
and prevent them from ending up in the ditches and canals.
If this is done,
then soldiers will compete to advance in battle in the front lines,
not idly but being useful,
carrying back the dead and supporting the wounded,
even if the dead exceed half.
What is the reason for this?
Soldiers do not love war and lightly regard death;
the distinctions in economic control make it so."
Duke Huán said:
"The levies on hides, sinews, and horns are very heavy.
Heavily taxing the people
and making the market prices high for
hides, sinews, and horns
is not a method for governing the state."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I ask to order high bridges and thicketed ponds,
so that east and west cannot see each other,
north and south cannot meet."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
After implementing this for a full year,
the levies on hides, sinews, and horns were reduced by half,
and the people's taxes were reduced by half.
Duke Huán summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When bridges and ponds were level,
husband and wife could pull a cart,
lightly traveling a hundred lǐ.
Now with high bridges and thicketed ponds,
east, west, north, and south cannot see each other,
when the sky darkens with rain,
the strength of ten men cannot ascend;
encountering rain in vast marshes,
the strength of ten men cannot be relied upon.
Apart from the strength of oxen and horses, there is no other means.
Oxen and horses become utterly exhausted, and those dying in succession are seen everywhere,
so hides, sinews, and horns
are simply given away with none to take them.
The price of oxen and horses
must rise a hundredfold while sitting still.
When the world hears of this,
they will surely bring their oxen and horses
and flow back to Qí.
Thus, high bridges and thicketed ponds
are the means to attract the world's oxen and horses
and reduce the people's taxes.
The 'Dào Ruò Mì' says:
'What things are produced
is not as good as where they are gathered.'"
Duke Huán said:
"There are many warped crossbows,
yet we heavily tax the people
to support the artisans, and still the crossbows are often warped.
What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The dwellings of ducks and geese are near,
while the paths of pheasants and swans are far.
Where the swans and pheasants are found,
I ask the ruler to go with jade discs and engage them."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
After implementing this for a full year,
there were no deficiencies above,
and no one hurried ahead.
In three months, the archery range was dismantled,
and there were no warped crossbows.
He summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Where the swans and pheasants are found,
the ruler went with jade discs and engaged them.
The people of the marshy lands heard of this,
and crossed plains to shoot far.
Without a crossbow of ten jūn strength,
one cannot hit pheasants and swans.
For such a crossbow of ten jūn,
without a support frame,
it cannot straighten itself.
Thus, in three months the archery range was dismantled
and there were no warped crossbows.
What is the reason for this?
Because their families became practiced in their craft."
Duke Huán said:
"I wish to levy taxes on houses."
Guǎnzǐ replied: "That cannot be done,
for it would destroy what is built."
"I wish to levy taxes on the myriad people."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"That cannot be done,
for it would conceal their true situation."
"I wish to levy taxes on the six domestic animals."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"That cannot be done,
for it would kill the living."
"I wish to levy taxes on trees."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"That cannot be done,
for it would cut down the living."
"Then what may I tax that would be acceptable?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I ask the ruler to levy taxes on the spirits and ghosts."
Duke Huán suddenly changed countenance and said:
"If even the common people, their houses,
livestock, and trees
cannot be taxed,
how could ghosts and spirits possibly be taxed?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Appropriate adaptation to circumstances
brings the benefit of affairs;
planning according to power
determines the scope of affairs.
The king rides circumstances,
the sage rides subtlety,
and both are appropriate to all things."
Duke Huán said:
"How should this be implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In former times, Yáo's Five Elders
and Five Officials had no sustenance,
so I ask you to establish sacrifices to the Five Ghosts,
sacrificing to Yáo's Five Officials.
Offer orchids in spring,
collect fallen leaves in autumn;
make dried fish from lake fish,
and use salamanders as delicacies.
If you do this,
then the fish tax from the marshes
will be several times higher than before,
and you won't need the taxes on housing grain or state currency.
This is called establishing rituals to seek blessings,
extending them through ritual and righteousness.
Thus being self-sufficient,
what need is there to demand from the people?"
Duke Huán said: "Among the states under heaven,
none is stronger than Yuè.
Now I wish to campaign north against Gūzhú and Lízhī,
but fear the Yuè people might come,
is there a way to prevent this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I ask you to dam the river's source,
have your ministers build ponds,
and order people to enjoy swimming.
Then how would the Yuè people dare come?"
Duke Huán said:
"How should this be implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Please order the damming of three rivers,
establish round cities,
build cities of great boats.
The cities of great boats
should have deep pools, ten ren deep.
Issue an order:
'Those who can swim will be rewarded ten pieces of gold.'
Before spending even a thousand in gold,
the Qí people's swimming skills
will surpass those of Wú and Yuè."
Duke Huán eventually campaigned north against Gūzhú and Lízhī.
The Yuè people indeed came,
hiding at Qǔzī to flood Qí.
Guǎnzǐ had fifty thousand skilled swimmers,
waiting
to battle at Qǔzī,
where they heavily defeated the Yuè people.
This is called water preparation.
When the northern marshes of Qí caught fire,
the flames illuminated the hall.
Guǎnzǐ entered and congratulated Duke Huán saying:
"Our fields have been cleared,
the farmers will surely reap hundredfold profits."
That year taxes were collected by September,
and the grain was excellent.
Duke Huán summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied: "States of ten thousand chariots,
states of a thousand chariots,
cannot cook without firewood.
Now the northern marshes burned, with nothing to replenish it,
so farmers can stockpile
and sell their kindling,
getting ten times the price per bundle.
Thus in spring they have means to prepare plows,
in summer to weed fields.
This is why taxes were collected by September."
Duke Huán worried about the poverty of the northern suburb people,
summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"The northern suburb
is full of sandal-weaving peasants,
who depend on garden plots for livelihood,
is there a way to help them?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Please order: households with hundred zhǒng cannot make shoes,
households with thousand zhǒng cannot maintain gardens,
and within three hundred steps of the market no malva may be planted.
If this is done,
then the idle will have means to supply resources,
and the northern suburb peasants
will have market for their handiwork.
The profit from garden plots
will thus increase tenfold."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"There are three shadow king states,
and Qí is among them."
Duke Huán said:
"May I hear about this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Chǔ has the gold of Rǔ and Hàn rivers,
while Qí has the salt of Qúzhǎn,
and Yān has the boiling salt of Liáodōng,
these are the shadow king states.
Moreover, Chǔ's possession of gold
is like Qí's possession of Zīshí.
If handled unskillfully,
used unwisely,
the world will look down upon it.
If I could control Chǔ's gold,
I could make farmers eat without plowing,
women dress without weaving.
Now Qí has Qúzhǎn salt,
I ask you to cut marsh firewood,
boil Jǐ water for salt,
and properly accumulate it."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Starting in October,
until the first month,
they produced thirty-six thousand zhǒng of salt.
He summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"How should this salt be used?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When early spring arrives,
farming work will begin.
Ministers may not repair tombs,
renovate palaces,
build towers,
or construct walls.
The northern sea people
may not gather laborers to boil salt.
If this is done,
salt prices will surely rise tenfold."
Duke Huán said:
"Good.
How should this be implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Please order its sale to Liáng, Zhào, Sòng, Wèi, and Púyáng.
Those states all depend on imported food.
Without salt they swell,
and border defense states
use salt particularly heavily."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He then ordered its sale,
gaining over eleven thousand jīn of gold.
Duke Huán summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"How should this gold be used?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Please order that tribute offerings
and tax payments must use gold,
gold prices will then rise hundredfold.
Using gold's weight to measure
all things, everything returns to the ruler.
Thus this method
is like dipping from rivers and seas,
like supplying a horse.
This is the enterprise of shadow kings."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"A state with ten thousand chariots
must have merchants worth ten thousand gold,
a state with a thousand chariots
must have merchants worth a thousand gold,
a state with a hundred chariots
must have merchants worth a hundred gold,
yet these are not what the ruler relies on,
but what he shares with.
Therefore, if a ruler does not carefully regulate his decrees,
then within one state there will be two rulers and two kings."
Huán Gōng asked:
"What does it mean to have two rulers and two kings in one state?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"If now your levies are collected
justly, yet the prices of all goods
fall away from their proper share,
all flowing into the merchants' hands,
this is having two rulers and two kings in one state.
Thus, merchants take advantage of the crisis to control the people's timing,
the poor lose their wealth,
which deepens their poverty;
farmers lose their grain,
which exhausts them further.
Therefore, a ruler who cannot carefully guard his mountains and forests,
marshes, and grasslands,
cannot be established as a king under heaven."
Huán Gōng said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Mountains, forests, marshes, and grasslands
are where firewood and reeds come from,
and where sacrificial animals are raised.
So let the people seek from them,
let them be registered,
and thereby supplied.
If the ruler's private care for the people
is like that of a younger brother to an elder,
or a son to a father,
then wealth and goods can be exchanged.
Thus, I request to take your surplus wealth,
and distribute it among the villages and hamlets.
In warm spring, when silkworms and mulberries are about to come,
please use it to supply their food and strengthen their baskets and frames.
In this way,
the levy on silk thread will be removed and collected fairly.
Moreover, for those from all directions who do not come,
regulate them by the six seasons:
spring is for setting plows,
next is for harvesting wheat,
next is for weeding fields,
next is for planting hemp,
next is for clearing marshes,
next is when heavy rains approach,
hasten to weed, mound, and cultivate.
Regulate by the six seasons,
to supply up to the capital.
A good ruler adjusts according to the fluctuations,
guarding his stored reserves,
so when events occur, there is no chaos.
Then he can be established as a king under heaven."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"If one farmer does not plow,
some people may starve because of it;
if one woman does not weave,
some people may suffer cold because of it.
So if production doubles its base,
then no one will sell their children;
if it triples its base,
then food and clothing will be sufficient;
if it quadruples its base,
then taxes can be met;
if it quintuples its base,
then near and far will communicate,
and the dead can be buried.
Now if production cannot double its base,
and the ruler's demands are endless,
this makes it impossible to walk alone on treacherous paths,
and leftover wealth cannot be retained.
If laws follow,
then it is cutting down the people.
If they have only three shēng of food,
then villages will have those lacking food who turn to theft;
if two shēng,
then neighborhoods will have them;
if one shēng,
then households will have them.
Now, engaging in unprofitable affairs,
while consuming forty times the grain,
and expecting the people not to fail,
is impossible.
Moreover, if the ruler orders in the morning and demands completion by evening,
those who have will give their wealth,
those who have not will sell their clothes and sandals,
farmers will sell their grain,
at a third of its value.
Thus, with one angry morning decree from the ruler,
cloth and silk flow away to the world.
If the ruler's demands are endless,
and the people have no means to cope,
they will flee and hide in the mountains.
Soldiers bearing spears
will find no one close to care for,
families will be lost and scattered.
The people fleeing within
and soldiers deserting outside,
this leads to internal defeat without a battle."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Now, those who govern the land and people in a state
must focus on the four seasons,
and guard the granaries.
If the state is wealthy,
then distant people will come;
if the land is fully opened,
then the people will stay and settle;
if granaries are full,
then they know礼节;
if food and clothing are sufficient,
then they know honor and shame.
Now, if you personally plow and open fields,
cultivating the soil,
and obtain grain,
and the people have food,
each with a certain amount of land,
then why are there still hungry people in the streets and alleys?
Because grain is hoarded.
Now, if you mint coins and establish currency,
and people trade,
each having tens or hundreds,
then why are there still those who sell their children?
Because wealth is monopolized.
Therefore, if a ruler cannot disperse accumulations,
adjust prices,
and divide monopolized wealth,
even if he strengthens agriculture and promotes farming,
and endlessly opens land and issues currency,
the people will still be in need."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Now, I wish to adjust prices,
divide monopolized wealth,
and disperse accumulations.
Otherwise,
the world will endlessly engage in monopolies,
hoarding surplus without rest,
and the poor, lowly, widowed, orphaned, and lonely elderly will not get any.
Is there a way to disperse it,
a method to divide it?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Only masters of轻重 can disperse it,
I ask to order the masters of轻重."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
He prepared five carriages,
and welcomed Guǐ Yǐ from Xiàyuán in Zhōu.
Huán Gōng then
sat with Guǐ Yǐ, Guǎnzǐ, and Nìng Qī, the four together.
Huán Gōng said:
"I ask about the methods of轻重."
Guǐ Yǐ said:
"Heavy taxation loses the people,
frequent deception of feudal lords loses allies."
Guǎnzǐ, leaning shoulder to shoulder, asked:
"If I do not tax my people,
how can I supply chariots and armor?
If I do not tax my people,
how can I deal with neighboring states?"
Guǐ Yǐ said:
"Only a benevolent heart is acceptable!
For with a benevolent heart, all things connect;
all things connecting leads to all things circulating;
all things circulating leads to all things becoming affordable;
all things affordable means all things can be utilized.
Knowing that all things can be utilized yet failing to utilize them
results in losing the world.
Losing the world
is the greatest thief of the state."
Huán Gōng said:
"May I ask how a benevolent heart makes all things utilizable?"
Guǐ Yǐ replied:
"Those with surplus wealth but no surplus chariots—
demand them from the feudal lords.
Satisfy their needs,
but do not bribe their followers;
demand this from the high officials.
If this is done,
then all things connect;
all things connecting
leads to all things circulating;
all things circulating
leads to all things becoming affordable;
all things affordable
means all things can be utilized.
Hence, those who understand the three standards and unified policies
can govern the world;
those who do not understand the three standards and unified policies
cannot govern the world.
Therefore, issue commands and decrees,
regulate them with urgency and leisure,
and the people will flock to me like flowing water.
This is the method of balancing light and heavy."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"Now, with a hundred thousand halberds planted,
the consumption of firewood and provisions
daily empties the resources of ten lǐ of land;
with each rally of halberds,
the expenditure on worn-out materials
daily depletes a thousand jīn's worth of reserves.
In the long run, how shall we cope?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When grain prices are stable, one fǔ is forty coins,
and gold is priced at four thousand.
With grain at forty coins per fǔ,
one zhōng is four hundred coins;
ten zhōng are four thousand,
twenty zhōng amount to eight thousand.
With gold priced at four thousand,
two units of gold equal eight thousand coins.
Thus, the work of one farmer
farming a hundred mǔ all year,
the harvest from a hundred mǔ
does not exceed twenty zhōng,
meaning the labor of one farmer
is equivalent to the value of two units of gold.
So, when grain is heavy (valuable), gold is light (less valuable);
when gold is heavy, grain is light;
the two do not balance equally.
Hence, the adept raise the price of grain.
At four hundred coins per fǔ,
then one zhōng is four thousand;
ten zhōng are forty thousand,
twenty zhōng are eighty thousand.
With gold priced at four thousand,
ten units of gold are forty thousand,
twenty units are eighty thousand.
Therefore, issue decrees and orders, saying
the work of one farmer
yields the value of twenty units of gold.
Thus, land need not be vast or narrow,
the state need not be poor or rich;
it depends on issuing commands and orders,
and mastering the method of balancing light and heavy."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"With a booming drumbeat,
soldiers grow furious;
with a clanging gong,
soldiers become orderly.
Following the drum's rhythm,
carrying the dead and aiding the wounded,
they advance relentlessly.
Mouths full of provisions,
hands full of coins—
it's not for the sake of avenging grandparents,
but driven by heavy salaries and rewards.
Thus, if high positions are established at court
but ranks and emoluments do not follow,
ministers will not be loyal;
in the midst of battle,
if promised rewards are not given,
soldiers will not die in formation.
So, ministers are bound by the court,
and soldiers in formation are bound by rewards.
Hence, fathers cannot keep their sons,
brothers cannot keep their younger brothers,
wives cannot keep their husbands—
only heavy salaries and rewards make it so.
Therefore, without traveling far,
one can awe the people of remote lands;
without braving treacherous mountains and rivers,
one can subdue fortified states that rely on defenses.
Strike like thunder,
move like wind and rain,
acting alone in and out,
with none able to obstruct."
Huán Gōng said:
"If the four barbarians do not submit,
I fear their rebellious policies
may spread across the world
and harm me.
Is there a way
for me to handle this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"If Wú and Yuè do not pay tribute,
use their pearls and ivory as currency.
If Fà and Cháoxiǎn do not pay tribute,
request their patterned furs and fine garments as currency.
If Yúshì does not pay tribute,
ask for white jades as currency.
If the Kūnlún region does not pay tribute,
request qiú lín and láng gān as currency.
For what is held but not seen in the hand,
contained but not seen in the mouth,
yet worth a thousand gold—
are pearls;
then, Wú and Yuè eight thousand lǐ away can be made to pay tribute.
A single leopard skin can be worth a thousand gold;
then,
Fà and Cháoxiǎn eight thousand lǐ away can be made to pay tribute.
What is carried but not seen in the arms,
tucked but not seen under the arm,
yet worth a thousand gold—
are white jades;
then, Yúshì eight thousand lǐ away can be made to pay tribute.
Hairpins and ear ornaments worth a thousand gold—
are qiú lín and láng gān;
then, the Kūnlún region eight thousand lǐ away can be made to pay tribute.
Thus, if goods have no owners,
affairs have no connections,
and distances cannot interact,
then the four barbarians cannot be made to pay tribute."
Huán Gōng said:
"Can the world's fluctuations be stabilized?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"They can never be stabilized."
Huán Gōng said:
"May I hear the reasoning for this instability?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The land spans twenty-eight thousand lǐ east to west,
twenty-six thousand lǐ north to south.
The Son of Heaven stands in the center,
with the state's four sides
each over ten thousand lǐ.
The people within the tax registers
also extend over ten thousand lǐ.
Thus, some with a hundredfold strength cannot reach,
some with tenfold strength cannot reach,
while others are nearby.
Then, the distant become estranged, swiftly resentful of the ruler.
Border lords take in the ruler's resentful people,
befriend them,
and defiantly refuse tribute.
This blocks the Son of Heaven's paths.
If the grain producers leave,
how can one dominate the world?"
Duke Huán said:
"How should this be implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I propose establishing a territorial hierarchy
across the realm,
with the Son of Heaven at the center,
governing a domain of a thousand lǐ square.
The territories of hegemonic lords extend over three hundred lǐ,
ordinary feudal lords measure about a hundred lǐ,
while coastal viscounts and barons measure approximately seventy lǐ.
Under such a system,
it would be like the chest directing the arms,
and the arms directing the fingers.
Thus,
the minor lords cannot take from the people,
(regulating) the pace and adequacy,
surpluses and shortages,
so even those below cause no worry to the ruler.
For the sea produces salt without cease,
the mountains yield metal and timber without rest.
Plants and trees grow in their seasons,
utensils wear out over time,
and the salt from Jǐshuǐ is consumed daily.
As one cycle ends, another begins,
competing with heaven and earth,
this is what is called establishing a territorial hierarchy."
King Wǔ asked Guǐ Dù:
"If tributes are not substantial,
one cannot be close to the ruler;
if the court's needs are unmet,
(support from) friends among the ministers is lacking.
Thus, without wishing to levy heavy household taxes
to supply the court's expenses,
is there a way to achieve this?"
Guǐ Dù replied:
"Our state is a hub state,
a thoroughfare for distant grain transports,
a route for traveling merchants and stored goods,
a passage for wealth and commodities.
So, if they consume our grain,
use our currency,
then they export gold.
Thus, the ruler should value the heavy and balance the light,
circulate goods interdependently,
then state policies can succeed.
Therefore, carefully maintain this measure without fail,
is it not so?
Can the people be governed?"
King Wǔ said:
"How should this be implemented?"
Guǐ Dù said:
"Gold comes from the mountains to the right of Rǔ and Hàn,
pearls from the barren edges of Chìyě,
jade from the side mountains of Yúshì.
These are all over 7,800 lǐ from Zhōu,
the routes are long,
the arrivals difficult.
Thus, the former kings allocated resources based on value,
using pearls and jade as high currency,
gold as medium currency,
knife and cloth coins as low currency.
The former kings skillfully adjusted the value of medium currency,
regulated upper and lower uses,
and the realm was thus sufficient."
Duke Huán said:
"Héng told me:
'For one farmer's work,
there must be one plow, one spade, one sickle, one hoe, one hammer, one scythe,
then he can be a farmer.
For one cart, there must be one axe, one saw, one hub, one drill, one chisel, one file, one axle,
then it can be a cart.
For one woman, there must be one knife, one awl, one needle, one shuttle,
then she can be a woman.
I propose ordering the felling of mountain timber,
smelting mountain iron,
thus we can have sufficient resources without taxation.'"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"This cannot be done.
If we conscript convicts for this,
they will flee and not remain.
If we mobilize the people,
they will resent the ruler,
and if the borders see conflict,
they will harbor old grievances and not fight.
Before seeing the benefits of mountain iron,
internal collapse would occur.
Thus, a better approach is to involve the people,
weigh the costs,
calculate the profits,
with the people taking seven parts,
and the ruler three.
Balance it with monetary policies,
maintain it through price adjustments.
In this way,
the people will work diligently and become subjects of the ruler."
Duke Huán said:
"May I ask about the principles of land?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The feudal lords along the Héwù,
are states of a zhōng per mǔ.
The feudal lords of rocky mountains are different.
The Héwù lords often do not surpass the mountain lords,
because of preparation."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The Héwù feudal lords,
with a zhōng per mǔ,
thus have abundant grain
but lack management,
so they cannot retain it.
As for the mountain feudal lords,
they gather and store vegetables,
this is called preparation."
Duke Huán said:
"Are the principles of land fully covered here?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Not yet.
Formerly, the Dí feudal lords,
with a zhōng per mǔ,
thus ten zhōng of grain equaled a zī of gold.
The Chéng feudal lords,
being mountain states,
had five fǔ of grain for a zī of gold.
So the Dí lords with ten zhōng could not afford weaponry,
while the Chéng lords with five fǔ could,
tenfold being insufficient,
or one-fifth being ample,
demonstrates mastery of the principles of value and price.
If a state has ten years' reserves,
yet the people lack food,
it is because all rely on their occupations expecting the ruler's support.
If the ruler has wealth from mountains and seas,
yet the people lack resources,
it is because all use their occupations to curry favor with the ruler.
Thus, customary taxes are what the ruler rightly deserves;
direct levies are what the ruler forcibly demands.
A failing ruler abandons what he deserves
and collects what he forcibly demands,
so the people resent the ruler and orders are not followed.
The people, if deprived, become angry;
if given, they rejoice—
such is human nature.
