The former kings knew this,
thus showing the act of giving,
hiding the appearance of taking.
Hence, the five grains and millet
are the people's lifeline;
gold, knife, and cloth coins
are the people's currency.
The former kings skillfully regulated their currency
to control their lifeline,
thus the people's efforts could be fully utilized."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"If spring rain falls five feet,
the ruler will surely be disgraced.
A state that consumes beyond its means will perish.
For many depend on the five grains.
Thus, trees that withstand frost and dew
do not heed heaven's commands,
households that are self-sufficient
do not follow the sages.
So, take before giving,
raise before lowering,
anger before delighting,
then the realm can be uplifted."
Duke Huán said:
"By strengthening the foundation and economizing on expenditures,
can the state be preserved?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"It can improve the situation,
but is insufficient to ensure preservation.
In the past, the state of Jìshì
practiced strengthening the foundation and economizing,
its five grains were abundant
but it could not manage them properly,
so they flowed out in all directions and went to the world.
In this case,
Jìshì's strengthening the foundation and economizing
only served to make its people
exhaust their grain without proper management and become captives of the world.
Thus the state perished
and they had nowhere to settle.
Therefore it can improve the situation
but is insufficient for preservation.
Hence, those skilled at governing a state
make what the world lowers
we elevate,
what the world轻视
we value,
what the world has in abundance
we make scarce.
Only then can they make the world pay homage."
Duke Huán said:
"I wish to not kill a single soldier,
not blunt a single halberd, yet open up two square capitals.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When the Jīng River's upper and lower reaches are empty,
make the Wèn, Sì, Zhū, and Yán rivers three times full. Then
request an order to plant wheat in the ninth month,
harvest at the winter solstice,
so before the seasonal rains fall, farming benefits are secured."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He ordered wheat planting in the ninth month,
harvesting at the solstice.
Measuring the yield,
the accumulation from one harvest
equaled two square capitals.
This is what's called skillfully following heavenly timing,
understanding earthly advantages
to open square capitals.
Guǎnzǐ went in and reported to Duke Huán:
"The annual land tax is forty-two thousand gold,
I propose to reward the troops in one morning without prior notice."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
An order was issued to drum assemble at Tàizhōu's field to gather the troops.
Duke Huán stood at the altar,
Níng Qì, Bào Shū, Xí Péng, Yì Yá, and Bīn Xūwú all stood shoulder to shoulder.
Guǎnzǐ held a drumstick and saluted the troops:
"Who can break through enemy formations?
Award one hundred gold."
Three asks, no reply.
One man stepped forward with sword,
asking:
"How many in the enemy host?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"A thousand men."
"A thousand men,
I can break them."
He was awarded one hundred gold.
Guǎnzǐ continued:
"When weapons clash and crossbows draw,
who can capture the squad leader?
Award one hundred gold."
Asked:
"How many men in the squad?"
Guǎnzǐ said: "A thousand men's leader."
"A thousand men's leader,
I can capture him."
Awarded one hundred gold.
Guǎnzǐ added:
"Who can follow the banner's direction
and capture the general's head?
Award one thousand gold."
Ten men claimed they could,
each given one thousand gold.
Others claiming to behead externally
were awarded ten gold each.
In one morning's unannounced rewards, forty-two thousand gold
was completely emptied.
Duke Huán sighed anxiously:
"How can I understand this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Do not worry, my lord.
This makes them famous in their villages externally,
meritorious to their parents internally,
and virtuous to their wives and children at home.
Thus,
soldiers will compete for fame and repay virtue,
with no thought of retreat.
When we raise troops to attack,
break their army,
and annex their land,
the gain far exceeds forty-two thousand gold."
The five ministers said:
"Excellent."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Then instructed the generals:
"For leaders of a hundred men,
you must hold court ceremonies.
For leaders of a thousand men,
you must bow and see them off,
descending two steps.
Those with parents
must be given four shí of wine,
four dǐng of meat.
Those without parents
must be given three shí of wine for their wives and children,
three dǐng of meat."
After half a year of this training,
fathers taught sons,
elder brothers taught younger brothers,
wives advised husbands,
saying:
"Seeing such generous treatment,
if you don't die in battle formation,
can you return to your village?"
Duke Huán eventually raised troops to attack Lái,
battling at Jǔ's Bìshìlǐ.
Before drums and flags were fully visible,
before troop numbers were known,
the Lái people largely fled.
Thus their army was crushed,
their land annexed,
and their general captured.
So without granting lands or titles,
without spending gold on rewards,
the Lái army was defeated,
their land merged,
their ruler captured.
This was the strategy of unannounced rewards.
Duke Huán said:
"During the Qūfáng battle,
many people borrowed to supply government needs.
I want to repay their debts—
how to do it?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Issue an order:
require wealthy merchants to provide one horse per hundred tallies,
those without
obtain from the government.
Thus,
horses will appreciate a hundredfold.
Then government horses needn't leave their stables,
and Qūfáng battle debts are covered."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"For the merits of Chóngdì, Jiǎngdì, Dīng, and Huì's generations,
my annual income is lacking.
I cannot collect even a dou or shēng,
losing one part.
Marshes, saline land, alkaline swamps,
and barren hillside soil unusable,
I cannot collect from there either,
losing another part."
Crops line the borders across the fifteen-mile plain,
forced to cultivate yet believing they prosper on their own,
so the common people cannot contribute even a peck or pint to the state,
diminishing its resources by one part.
Thus, in my state,
out of five parts, I cannot control even two,
bearing the title of ten thousand chariots yet lacking the substance of a thousand.
With this, how can I balance with the Son of Heaven
and contend for rank among the feudal lords?
Is there a way to achieve this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Only by leveraging commands and decrees can it be done."
Huán Gōng asked:
"How should it be carried out?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request an order to dispatch troops and establish garrisons, registering farmers.
Households with ten dàn need not go,
those with a hundred dàn need not go,
those with a thousand dàn need not go.
Fewer than one in a hundred of those who go
and ten in a thousand
will have their granary stores
fully revealed to the authorities.
Your Majesty, based on the granary counts, issue a decree:
'The state is poor and resources insufficient;
we request to purchase from you at standard prices,
all according to your granary stores without reduction.'
You determine the amount by adjusting the currency's value,
ensuring no debt contracts are needed,
and then the stored grain in all granaries will belong to the ruler.
Thus, the state will be invincible across the nine regions,
and the borders will be free from worry."
The Duke said:
"Dismiss the troops and return them to farming—
there's no use for this."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"If there is war in the world,
the stored grain is sufficient to prepare rations.
If there is no war,
it can be bestowed upon the poor peasants.
In this way,
even marshlands, saline soils, barren wetlands,
and rugged mountainous terrain will all be cultivated.
This is called leveraging commands and decrees."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"If the grain in Téng and Lǔ costs a hundred per fǔ,
make the grain in our state cost a thousand per fǔ.
Then the grain from Téng and Lǔ will flow to us in four streams,
like descending into a deep valley.
Not due to famine or people's hunger,
but guided by commands and decrees,
led by pacing and urgency,
it will come to us
as if flowing water."
Huán Gōng said:
"I wish to curb the profits of legitimate merchants
and benefit the farmers' work.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When grain is expensive, all other goods are cheap;
when grain is cheap, all other goods are expensive—
the two do not balance.
So to curb merchants' profits
and benefit farmers' work,
I propose raising the price of grain to three hundred per fǔ.
If so,
the fields will be greatly expanded,
and farmers will be encouraged in their tasks."
Huán Gōng said:
"Is there a way to increase its price?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Request an order for senior officials to store in cities,
having ministers and feudal lords store a thousand zhōng,
senior officials store five hundred zhōng,
lesser officials store a hundred zhōng,
and wealthy merchants store fifty zhōng.
Internally, it can serve as state reserves;
externally, it can benefit the farmers' work."
Huán Gōng said:
"Good."
He ordered ministers, feudal lords, and senior officials to store in cities.
Farmers expanded their grain production,
and its price tripled,
so legitimate merchants lost their business,
while farmers gained a hundredfold profit.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Is there a fixed measure for balance?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"There is no fixed measure for balance.
Balance means making things rise and fall alternately,
not allowing them to remain constant."
Huán Gōng said:
"Then, can the measure of balance not be regulated?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"It cannot be regulated.
To regulate is to stagnate;
stagnation leads to constancy;
constancy means no fluctuation in highs and lows;
without such fluctuation,
goods cannot be utilized effectively."
Huán Gōng said:
"Then how to adhere to timing?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The year has four harvests,
and the seasons are divided into four periods.
Thus it is said: When farming is about to begin,
organize farmers in groups to provide plows and iron tools—
this is called the autumn of spring.
When great summer approaches,
it's time for silk and floss production—
this is called the autumn of summer.
When great autumn arrives,
it's the gathering of the five grains—
this is called the autumn of autumn.
In deep winter, when construction indoors is done,
it's time for women's work of spinning and weaving—
this is called the autumn of winter.
So the year has four harvests,
and the seasons are divided into four periods.
Once the sequence of these four is understood,
issuing commands and decrees,
the values of goods will vary tenfold or a hundredfold.
Thus, goods cannot remain constant.
Therefore, it is said there is no fixed measure for balance."
Huán Gōng said:
"If hides, frames, sinews, horns, bamboo arrows, feathers, ivory, and leather are insufficient,
is there a way to address this?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Only the method of indirect balance can be used."
Huán Gōng said:
"How should it be carried out?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request an order to establish guesthouses for merchants of the feudal lords.
For one carriage, provide food;
for three carriages, provide fodder and beans;
for five carriages, provide a full entourage.
Then merchants from all under heaven will flock to Qí like flowing water."
(The chapter is lost here.)
Huán Gōng said:
"I wish to go west to pay homage to the Son of Heaven,
but my tribute offerings are insufficient.
Is there a method for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request an order to build a wall in Yīnlǐ,
making its walls triple-layered and its gates ninefold.
Then have jade craftsmen carve stone into bi discs:
one-chǐ discs valued at ten thousand quán,
eight-cùn discs at eight thousand,
seven-cùn discs at seven thousand,
guī tablets at four thousand,
and yuàn rings at five hundred."
Once the bi discs were prepared,
Guǎnzǐ went west to see the Son of Heaven and said:
"The ruler of our humble state
wishes to lead the feudal lords to pay homage at the temples of former kings
and visit the Zhōu court.
I request an order that all feudal lords under heaven
wishing to pay homage at the temples of former kings
and visit the Zhōu court
must present red bows and stone bi discs.
Those without red bows and stone bi discs
may not enter the court."
The Son of Heaven agreed, saying: "So be it."
He issued the command throughout the land.
Feudal lords from all under heaven loaded gold, pearls, jade, grains, patterned silks, cloth, and coins to send to Qí
in exchange for the stone bi discs.
The stone bi discs flowed out to all under heaven,
and the wealth and goods of all under heaven flowed into Qí.
Thus, for eight years the state required no taxation.
This was the stratagem of Yǐnlǐ.
Above: the stone bi stratagem.
Huán Gōng said:
"The Son of Heaven's resources are insufficient,
yet if he issues decrees to levy taxes throughout the realm,
the feudal lords will not trust him.
Is there a way to handle this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Between the Jiāng and Huái rivers,
there grows a kind of mao grass with three ridges,
never reaching its root,
named jīngmáo.
I request that officials of the Son of Heaven encircle and guard it.
When the Son of Heaven conducts the fēng sacrifice at Tàishān,
and the shàn sacrifice at Liángfù,
he should decree to the feudal lords:
'All who follow the Son of Heaven to the fēng sacrifice at Tàishān and shàn sacrifice at Liángfù
must bring one bundle of jīngmáo as a mat for the sacrifices.
Those who do not comply with the order
may not follow.'"
The feudal lords of the realm loaded their gold, competing to obtain it and rushing forth.
The jīngmáo from the Jiāng and Huái
immediately increased tenfold in price,
its value
reaching one hundred gold per bundle.
Thus, the Son of Heaven assumed his position in three days,
and the gold of the realm flowed in all directions back to Zhōu like running water.
Therefore, the Zhōu Son of Heaven did not need to seek tributes for seven years—
this was the stratagem of the jīngmáo.
Above: the jīngmáo stratagem.
Huán Gōng said:
"I have many duties,
and now the authorities are registering the wealthy merchants, hoarders, and moneylenders of our state,
to benefit our poor commoners
and farmers, so they do not neglect their fundamental tasks.
Is there a way to reverse this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Only by using decrees to reverse it is feasible."
Huán Gōng said:
"How should we proceed?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request sending Bīn Xūwú to gallop south,
Xí Péng to gallop north,
Nìng Qì to gallop east,
and Bào Shū to gallop west.
Once the four men's journeys are decided,
I, Yíwú, will issue a decree telling them:
'You shall all inspect the moneylending activities in the four directions for our lord,
and report back to me how many thousand households of commoners are paying interest.'"
Bào Shū galloped west.
He returned and reported:
"The commoners in the west,
bordering the Jǐ River and near the Hé River,
are dwellers of marshes and wetlands.
They fish, hunt, gather firewood,
and steam food for sustenance.
Among the moneylenders,
the largest have a thousand hú,
the smallest six to seven hundred hú.
When they lend out, for each hú,
they charge one hú in interest. There are over nine hundred households of commoners paying interest."
Bīn Xūwú galloped south.
He returned and reported:
"The commoners in the south
dwell in mountains and valleys,
living on high and low grounds.
They craft wheels and axles above,
gather acorns and chestnuts below,
and hunt for food.
Among the moneylenders,
the largest have ten million,
the smallest six to seven million.
When they lend out, they charge fifty percent interest.
There are over eight hundred households of commoners paying interest."
Nìng Qì galloped east.
He returned and reported:
"The commoners in the east,
nestled among mountains and near the sea,
reside in harsh valleys,
craft tools above,
and are fishing and hunting folk.
They process kudzu vines for sustenance.
The moneylenders: Dīng, Huì, Gāo, Guó,
the largest have five thousand hú,
the smallest three thousand hú.
When they lend out, they charge five fǔ per hú.
There are eight to nine hundred households of commoners paying interest."
Xí Péng galloped north.
He returned and reported:
"The commoners in the north,
living on plains near the sea,
boil brine for salt,
and are folk who fish in the Jǐ River.
They rely on firewood and food,
and among the moneylenders,
the largest have ten million,
the smallest six to seven million.
When they lend out, they charge
twenty percent interest.
There are over nine hundred households of commoners
paying interest."
In total, the moneylenders
lent out thirty million coins,
and several tens of millions hú of grain.
Thirty thousand households of commoners were paying interest.
After the four men reported,
Guǎnzǐ said:
"I had not realized that our lord's commoners
within one state bear the burdens of five rulers' taxes.
Yet, to hope that the state not be poor,
and the military not weak—
how could that be possible?"
Huán Gōng said:
"Is there a way to handle this?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Only by using decrees to reverse it is feasible.
I request an order that all tribute offerings must use jùzhī lángǔ,
which will certainly increase tenfold in value from their cost.
Your Majesty's silk stored in Zhàntái
will also increase tenfold in value.
Please order the moneylenders to be summoned,
and you, my lord, should toast them with wine,
with the Grand Steward presenting the cups.
Then, Huán Gōng raised his garment and asked:
'I have many duties,
and now the authorities are registering our state.
I hear that you lend to our poor commoners,
enabling them to fulfill the government's demands.
I have jùzhī lángǔ,
valued at ten thousand coins per roll.
I wish to use it to settle the interest debts for our poor commoners,
so they are free from the obligations of bonds and contracts.'
The moneylenders all bowed their heads and kowtowed, saying:
'Your concern for the commoners goes this far!
We beg to bow twice and offer it in your hall.'
Huán Gōng said:
'That will not do.
You enable our commoners to have plows in spring,
and to weed in summer.
My gratitude to you knows no bounds;
if you do not accept this,
I will be disheartened.'
Thus, the moneylenders all said: 'We accept with two bows.'
The silk given from Zhàntái
did not amount to three thousand rolls,
yet it settled the interest debts in all four directions,
freeing them from the obligations of bonds and contracts.
When the commoners from all directions heard of this,
fathers instructed their sons,
elder brothers taught their younger brothers,
saying:
'To cultivate fields and clear weeds diligently
is what the ruler urgently needs.
Can we not strive to multiply?
The ruler's concern for us goes this far!'
This is called reversing the standard."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"In the past, when Guǐ Dù resided in a state,
he would always look out to the four directions of the realm.
If others raised prices, he would raise them too.
If the realm raised prices and he alone kept them low,
he would surely lose his state to the realm."
Duke Huán said:
"What does this statement mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"In the past, the people of Lái were skilled at dyeing.
Purple-dyed silk from Lái cost one pure zī,
and patterned ribbons from Lái also cost one pure zī.
In the capital, they were worth ten jīn.
When the people of Lái learned this,
they hoarded the purple dye, creating a shortage.
The capital then collected horses
and made a display before the people of Lái, manipulating the situation.
Lái thus established a standard based on horses.
This caused Lái to lose their purple dye monopoly and instead be regulated by horses.
Therefore, what can be utilized should be utilized,
what can be leveraged should be leveraged—
this is using All-under-Heaven to control All-under-Heaven.
This is called the state's regulation."
Duke Huán said:
"In western Qí
floods have caused famine among the people,
while eastern Qí
has abundant harvests and cheap grain.
How can we use the cheap grain of the east to relieve the high prices of the west?
Is there a way to accomplish this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Now the grain in western Qí
costs one hundred quán per fǔ,
which is twenty quán per ōu.
The grain in eastern Qí
costs ten quán per fǔ,
which is two quán per ōu.
I request an order to levy thirty quán per person,
allowing them to pay this levy with the five grains and legumes.
In this way,
western Qí would pay three dǒu to settle the levy,
while eastern Qí would pay three fǔ to settle the levy.
Thus the grain at ten quán per fǔ
would all be stored in granaries.
The hungry people in the west would get food,
the cold would get clothing;
those without capital would be given old grain,
those without seed would be given new grain.
Thus,
east and west would support each other,
and prices would be balanced between distant and nearby regions."
Duke Huán said:
"I have heard about balancing methods.
May I ask about the state's regulation?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"As the beginning of spring approaches,
if ditches and waterways are blocked and not flowing,
and waters from streams and valleys above dams are not safely contained,
they will destroy houses internally,
damage walls and enclosures,
and harm fields externally,
ruining crops.
Therefore, the ruler should carefully control the outflow of coin and goods,
and make appropriate allocations.
In high summer,
if curtains, canopies, clothing, and drapes are insufficient,
carefully control the outflow of silk and cloth goods,
and make appropriate allocations.
In high autumn,
when armor and weapons need maintenance,
bows and crossbows need strings,
carefully control the outflow of
silk and hemp goods,
and make appropriate allocations.
In deep winter,
when employing troops,
if provisions are insufficient,
and gold rewards are inadequate,
carefully control the outflow of the five grains and gold
goods,
and make appropriate allocations.
Once control over outflows is maintained,
wealthy merchants and hoarders cannot continue as before.
This is called the state's regulation."
Dragons fought north of the Mǎ (called) River,
south of Niú Mountain.
Guǎnzǐ repeatedly reported to Duke Huán:
"Heaven has sent envoys to the outskirts of your domain.
Should we have officials dress in uniform and attendants wear black to honor Heaven's envoys?"
All-under-Heaven heard of this and said:
"Divine indeed is Duke Huán of Qí,
that Heaven sends envoys to his outskirts."
Without raising troops, eight feudal lords came to pay homage.
This is the way to utilize Heaven's majesty and move All-under-Heaven.
Thus the wise employ ghosts and spirits
while the foolish believe in them.
Duke Huán ultimately deified them.
Guǎnzǐ entered and reported to Duke Huán:
"The earth shakes—
a portent of plague,
the state will suffer.
The wind moves—
a portent of plague.
If the state has a comet,
its ruler will surely be humiliated;
if the state has a broom star,
there will surely be bloodshed.
At the battle of Fúqiū,
where the broom star appeared,
we must subdue the enemies of All-under-Heaven.
Now the broom star appears in Qí's territory.
I request an order to summon meritorious ministers and noble families,
and issue a proclamation throughout the state:
'The broom star has appeared,
and I fear we must subdue the enemies of All-under-Heaven.
Those who possess the five grains, legumes, cloth, silk, or patterned silks
must not dare to dispose of them.
The state will have great affairs,
and we request to purchase them at fair prices.'
Meritorious families
and common people will all offer their grains, legumes, coins, and gold,
contributing their wealth
to assist the ruler's great affairs.
This is called utilizing heavenly disasters to seek the people's neighboring wealth."
Duke Huán said:
"Many officials hoard their wealth and do not release it,
letting the five grains rot without distribution."
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request an order to summon Chéngyáng the grandee and reprimand him."
Duke Huán said:
"Why?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
'Chéngyáng the grandee—
his favorites wear fine linen,
his geese and ducks eat leftover grain,
his halls echo with bells and drums,
and reed pipes play—
yet he admits no clansmen,
and his uncles, aunts,
and near and distant brothers
all shiver without clothing
and starve without food.
Can you claim to serve me with loyalty?
Therefore, do not see me again.'
Remove him from office
and block his gate so he does not go out."
The meritorious families
all competed to open their stores,
releasing their resources
to give to their near and distant brothers.
Considering this insufficient,
they also gathered the state's poor, sick, orphaned, solitary, and aged who could not feed themselves, and provided for them all.
Thus Duke Huán promoted benevolence and established righteousness,
and among the meritorious families
brothers cared for each other,
kin loved one another,
and the state had no starving people.
This is called ingenious methods.
Duke Huán said:
"During the Zhēngqiū campaign,
many people took loans
and bore interest burdens
to meet the government's urgent needs,
fulfilling the government's demands.
I wish to restore their livelihoods—
how can this be achieved?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Only ingenious methods can accomplish this."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He ordered the various districts:
"Mark the houses of moneylenders,
whiten their gates with plaster
and raise their lintels high."
The district masters took record tablets and said:
"The ruler will send envoys."
Duke Huán sent eight envoys with ceremonial jades to visit them,
providing for salt and vegetable expenses.
The moneylenders all bowed their heads and knocked their foreheads, asking:
"How have we earned this?"
The envoy said:
"The ruler commands:
I have heard in the Book of Songs:
'A kind and approachable gentleman
is like the parent of the people.
I have the war at Zhēngqiū.
I heard that you lent to our poor peasants,
enabling them to meet my urgent needs,
and fulfill my demands.
You allowed our peasants to have means to plow in spring,
and to weed in summer, thus supplying the government's needs.
This is thanks to your efforts.
Therefore, I present a jade disc to engage you,
for your expenses on salt and vegetables.
Hence, you truly are the parent of the people.'"
All the moneylenders broke their loan contracts and erased their records,
opened their stored reserves,
brought out their wealth and goods,
to relieve the poor and sick.
They distributed their original assets,
so the state was greatly supplied,
thanks to the strategy of Zhēngqiū.
This is called a clever calculation.
Duke Huán said:
"The people in the suburbs are poor,
while the merchants are rich.
I wish to curb the merchants to benefit the suburban people;
how can this be done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"I request an order to divert the waters of Huò Luò,
and channel them through the area between Kàng Zhuāng."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Before a year had passed since the order was implemented,
the suburban people had significantly grown richer,
while the merchants had clearly become poorer.
Duke Huán summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Diverting the waters of Huò Luò
through Kàng Zhuāng,
the waste from slaughterhouses and breweries flows with the water,
attracting large mosquitoes, giant beetles, and small birds like kingfishers and swallows.
They all gather there,
making it pleasant for evening drinks,
a delight on the water.
Merchants hoard goods to sell when prices are high,
and buy when they are low,
but before the market closes, they leave their stalls
to chase the large mosquitoes and beetles.
Young men with new hats and five-foot slings
come with弹弓s and pellets to the waterside,
shooting at kingfishers and small swallows,
until dusk falls.
Thus, they sell cheap and buy dear.
The suburban people sell at low prices;
how could they not become rich?
As for the merchants,
how could they not become poor?" Duke Huán said:
"Good."
Duke Huán said:
"The people in the five thoroughfares
look weary, many in worn clothes and broken shoes.
I wish to make the prices of silk,
cloth, thread, and floss cheaper;
is there a way to do this?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"I request an order to trim the branches of trees along the roads,
leaving not an inch of shade."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Before a year had passed since the order was implemented,
the people on the five thoroughfares were mostly dressed in silk and wearing intact shoes.
Duke Huán summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When the trees by the roads
were not trimmed,
the people of the five thoroughfares,
men and women fond of each other
going to the market,
after the market closed,
would meet under the trees,
chatting all day without returning home.
Young adults,
pushing carriages and carts,
would meet under the trees,
joking, leaping, and playing games,
spending the whole day without returning.
Elders would meet under the trees,
discussing profound topics,
all day without returning.
Thus, fields were not plowed,
the five grains not sown,
hemp and mulberry not planted,
and silkworms and thread not tended.
With one household having three groups not returning home,
how could the prices of silk, cloth, thread, and floss not be high?"
Duke Huán said:
"Good."
Duke Huán said:
"With grain prices low,
I fear the five grains will flow to other lords,
and I wish to store them for the common people;
is there a way to do this?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Recently, I passed through the market and
saw two families who had built new granaries.
Please present them with jade discs to honor them."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Six months after the order was implemented,
the people heard of it,
and more than half
abandoned their usual work to build granaries to store beans, millet, and the five grains.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎnzǐ said: "The two families who built granaries
were honored by you with jade discs,
their fame spread throughout the state,
and everyone in the state heard of it.
Thus, the people see that without official merit, they can gain fame among the populace,
achieving both merit and reputation;
practically, they fill their granaries,
and in service, they supply the ruler.
With one move gaining both name and substance,
why wouldn't the people do it?"
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"May I ask about the principles of royal calculations from start to finish?
Can I hear about them?"
Guǎnzǐ said:
"In the first month of the year,
it's the start of grain;
a hundred days after the solstice,
it's the start of millet and sorghum;
in the ninth month, when harvest is gathered, it's the beginning
of wheat and barley."
Guǎnzǐ asked Duke Huán:
"May I ask the area of Qí in square lǐ?"
Duke Huán said:
"Five hundred lǐ square."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"The land of Yīn Yōng and the Great Wall,
constitutes one-third of Qí's territory,
but it does not produce grain.
Hǎi Zhuāng and Lóng Xià,
make up one-fourth of Qí,
facing the sea,
with another one-fifth being damp land in Qí,
which also does not produce grain.
Then, are we not a state dependent on others for food?"
Duke Huán stood up abruptly and said:
"Then what should be done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Motivate with words,
influence with rhetoric,
and this can form the foundation of the state.
Moreover, if you rely on currency taxes,
then merchants alone control the state's trends;
if you rely on grain taxes,
then farmers alone hold the state's stability.
By using words and rhetoric,
you can independently utilize
the various currents around you."
I have witnessed the beginnings of things,
I have witnessed their ends,
and I have witnessed their prices.
Guǎnzǐ said:
"South of the Great Wall
is Lǔ.
North of the Great Wall
is Qí.
Those who suffered three defeats,
killed two rulers and important ministers,
yet stabilized the state
- I have enfeoffed them all with land at Hútū.
Thus, mountainous land is for hills,
watery land for marshes,
and land producing firewood and fodder for wastelands."
The Duke said:
"Is there a way for a ruler dependent on others for sustenance
to also possess land?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Guard the three fundamentals."
The Duke asked:
"What are the three fundamentals?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"If the ruler controls cloth,
then levy taxes on hemp,
making its price tenfold,
and cloth will become fifty times more valuable.
This is the method.
If the ruler taxes weaving,
levy on silk.
Before taxing silk,
promote weaving,
again making its value tenfold.
Similarly, this applies to grain taxes.
Therefore, taxing cloth requires promoting silk production,
taxing grain requires promoting mountain resources,
taxing livestock requires promoting breeding techniques.
Tax according to the complete cycle of things
and skillfully manage through policy."
The Duke said:
"Excellent."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"With a nationwide uniform tax,
storing ten thousand bolts of cloth on the right
while taxing hemp at forty times its price
will make cloth fifty times more valuable.
The Duke can use valuable cloth to compete with prices of other states,
thus gaining twenty times Qí's original wealth.
Therefore, those who lightly manipulate grain prices and control livestock
can make commodities follow the four seasons' support.
Those skilled at governing guard their state's wealth,
adjust it through price fluctuations,
regulate it with varying speeds,
making one become a hundred.
Without ever heavily taxing the people,
their resources flow like rivers and seas,
ending only to begin anew.
This is called guarding things to rule the world."
The Duke said:
"Then can non-existence become existence?
Can poverty become wealth?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Before things physically manifest,
kings and hegemon establish their merit.
Therefore, using people to seek people
makes people valuable.
Using methods to seek things
makes things valuable."
The Duke said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"If the whole state acts as one,
there is no capital.
If the whole state acts as ten,
there will be a hundredfold.
Thus I shall regulate it with varying speeds,
like left hand passing to right,
like right hand passing to left,
so internal and external don't conflict,
remaining blameless for life.
Kings and hegemon don't seek from people
but seek from beginnings and ends,
the seasonal fluctuations,
merely regulating the speed of decrees.
Springs may run dry,
spirits may rest.
Guarding things' beginnings and ends,
one never exhausts in lifetime.
This is called source mastery."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"How should price manipulation be implemented?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Since Fúxì's governance,
none have achieved kingship without price manipulation."
The Duke said:
"What do you mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"When Fúxì arose,
he created six methods
to correspond with yin-yang,
devised nine-nine mathematics
to match heavenly principles,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Shénnóng arose,
he planted five grains on Qí Mountain's south,
so people of nine provinces
learned grain food,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Suìrén arose,
drilling wood produced fire,
cooking meats and foul foods,
people ate without stomach illnesses,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Huángdì ruled,
he cleared mountains and drained marshes.
When Yǒuyú ruled,
he burned thick marshes,
eliminated various pests,
benefiting the people,
erected earthen altars,
set up village gates,
beginning people's knowledge of rites.
In that time,
people held no resentment or disobedience,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Xià people ruled,
they dug twenty channels outside,
deepened seventeen reservoirs,
dredged three rivers,
excavated five lakes,
channeled four streams' waters,
measured nine provinces' elevations,
managed nine marshes,
people then learned to build walls, gates, and houses,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Yīn people ruled,
they established corrals,
harnessed oxen and horses,
benefiting the people,
and the world transformed accordingly.
When Zhōu people ruled,
they followed six laws,
harmonized yin-yang,
and the world transformed accordingly."
The Duke said:
"Then what should contemporary rulers do?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Apply all methods but not exhaustively."
The Duke said:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The way of emperors and kings is complete,
nothing can be added.
Just practice righteousness, my Duke."
The Duke said:
"How does one practice righteousness?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The Son of Heaven is young and weak,
feudal lords are excessively powerful,
tributes aren't offered.
You should weaken the strong, continue severed lines,
lead feudal lords to revive Zhōu house's sacrifices."
The Duke said:
"Excellent."
Duke Huán said:
"Lǔ and Liáng to Qí
are like valleys between fingers,
like bee stings,
like lips to teeth.
Now I wish to subdue Lǔ and Liáng,
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The people of Lǔ and Liáng customarily weave tí silk.
If you, my lord, wear tí,
and order your attendants to wear it,
the people will follow and wear it too.
You can then order Qí to cease its production,
making it depend entirely on Lǔ and Liáng,
thus causing Lǔ and Liáng to abandon their farming and focus on weaving tí."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He then wore tí at the southern side of Tài Shān,
and within ten days, it became fashionable.
Guǎnzǐ informed the merchants of Lǔ and Liáng:
"If you bring me a thousand bolts of tí,
I will grant you three hundred jīn of gold.
For every ten deliveries, the gold amounts to thirty jīn."
Thus, without imposing taxes on the people, Lǔ and Liáng had sufficient resources.
When the rulers of Lǔ and Liáng heard this,
they instructed their people to weave tí.
Thirteen months later, Guǎnzǐ sent people to Lǔ and Liáng.
The people within the city walls of Lǔ and Liáng
raised dust on the roads,
obscuring visibility beyond ten steps,
dragging their hems and following in each other's footsteps,
with chariot hubs crammed and cavalry
riding in columns of five.
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Lǔ and Liáng can be subdued."
The Duke asked:
"How?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"You should switch to wearing silk,
leading the people to abandon tí. Close the borders,
and cease all diplomatic exchanges with Lǔ and Liáng."
The Duke said:
"Agreed."
Ten months later,
Guǎnzǐ sent people to Lǔ and Liáng,
where the people of Yúliáng
suffered from hunger and famine one after another,
and the immediate taxes
could not be paid to the authorities.
The rulers of Lǔ and Liáng
then ordered their people to abandon tí and resume farming. But grain
could not be harvested within three months.
The people of Lǔ and Liáng
had to buy grain at a hundred times the price,
while in Qí, it was sold for ten coins.
After twenty-four months,
six-tenths of the people of Lǔ and Liáng had defected to Qí.
In three years,
the rulers of Lǔ and Liáng submitted.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"The people are hungry with no food,
cold with no clothing,
the immediate taxes
cannot be paid to the authorities,
houses are leaky and unrepaired,
walls are crumbling and unbuilt—what should be done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Prune the branches of the trees along the roads."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He ordered the left and right chiefs to prune the branches of the trees along the roads.
The left and right chiefs undertook the pruning, and the branches along the roads were thinned.
That year,
the people wore white cloth,
their minds cleared and impurities removed, the immediate
taxes
were paid to the authorities,
leaky houses were repaired,
and crumbling walls were rebuilt.
The Duke summoned Guǎnzǐ and asked:
"Why did this happen?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Qí is
a country of the Yílái.
A single tree providing shade for a hundred chariots beneath it
is because its branches are not trimmed.
Numerous birds perch on it,
strong youths with pellets and slings stay below,
not returning home all day.
Elders lean on branches and chat,
not returning home all day.
Even those going to the market linger lazily,
not returning home all day.
Now that we've pruned the branches of the trees along the roads,
there is not an inch of shade at noon,
those coming and going shorten their time,
travelers hurry along,
elders return home to manage their livelihoods,
strong youths return to focus on their work.
By ending these three types of lingering,
the village is no longer impoverished."
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Lái and Jǔ have merged with the firewood fields—what should be done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"The mountains of Lái and Jǔ produce firewood.
You should lead untrained soldiers
to mint coins from the metal of Zhuāng Shān,
and raise the price of Lái's firewood."
The ruler of Lái heard this,
and told his attendants:
"Gold coins
are what people value.
Firewood is
a unique product of our country.
With our country's unique product,
we can exhaust Qí's treasures,
and then Qí can be annexed."
Lái immediately abandoned farming and focused on producing firewood.
Guǎnzǐ then ordered Xí Péng to return to farming.
Two years later,
Duke Huán stopped the firewood trade.
The price of grain in Lái and Jǔ rose to three hundred seventy,
while in Qí, it was sold for ten coins.
Seven-tenths of the people of Lái and Jǔ surrendered to Qí.
After twenty-eight months,
the rulers of Lái and Jǔ submitted.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"Chǔ is
a powerful state east of the mountains,
and its people are skilled in the ways of combat.
If we raise an army to attack it,
I fear our strength may not suffice.
Our troops would be exhausted by Chǔ,
and our achievements would not be recognized by Zhōu—what should be done?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Then use the way of combat against them."
The Duke said:
"What do you mean?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"You should offer high prices to buy their deer."
Duke Huán then built a hundred-lǐ walled enclosure,
and sent people to Chǔ to buy live deer.
In Chǔ, live deer were priced at eighty thousand per unit.
Guǎnzǐ then advised Duke Huán to regulate the currency with the people,
storing sixty percent of the grain.
He ordered Left Sīmǎ Bógōng to lead untrained troops and mint coins at Zhuāng Shān.
He ordered Grand Master Wáng Yì to transport twenty million in coins to Chǔ to purchase live deer.
When the King of Chǔ heard this,
he told his chancellor:
"That money
is what people value,
what sustains a state,
and how enlightened rulers reward the meritorious.
Wild animals
are a public nuisance,
abandoned and driven away by wise kings.
Now Qí is using its treasures to buy our nuisance—
this is a blessing for Chǔ.
Heaven is favoring Chǔ through Qí.
Inform our people
to urgently hunt live deer,
to exhaust Qí's treasures."
The people of Chǔ immediately abandoned farming and hunted deer.
Guǎnzǐ informed the merchants of Chǔ:
"If you bring me twenty live deer,
I will grant you a hundred jīn of gold.
For every ten deliveries, the gold amounts to a thousand jīn."
Thus, without imposing taxes on the people, Chǔ had sufficient resources.
The men of Chǔ stayed outdoors,
and the women filled the roads.
Xí Péng taught the people to store grain, increasing it fivefold.
Chǔ used the profits from selling live deer to amass wealth five times over.
Guǎnzǐ said:
"Chǔ can be subdued."
The Duke asked:
"How?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Chǔ's wealth has increased fivefold.
Their ruler will feel self-satisfied
and neglect grain cultivation.
With wealth multiplied five times,
this will actually weaken Chǔ."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Thereupon, he ordered the borders closed and ceased diplomatic relations with Chǔ.
The King of Chǔ indeed became complacent and neglected grain production.
Grain cannot be grown within three months,
and Chǔ's grain price rose to four hundred.
Qí then sent people to transport grain to the south of Chǔ's borders,
causing forty percent of Chǔ's population to surrender to Qí.
Within three years, Chǔ submitted.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"What special product does the state of Dài possess?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Dài's product
is the white fox fur.
Your Highness should purchase it at high prices."
Guǎnzǐ said:
"The white fox changes with yin and yang,
appearing only once every six months.
If you pay premium prices,
the people of Dài will forget its rarity,
delight in the high prices,
and surely compete to hunt for it.
Thus, Qí's money need not be spent,
while the people of Dài will abandon farming for the mountains.
When Lízhī hears of this,
they will invade from the north.
Once Lízhī attacks,
Dài will inevitably submit to Qí.
Your Highness should order Qí to transport money there."
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
He then commanded Grand Master Wáng Shī to lead a mission north
carrying money
to the valley of Dài,
seeking white fox furs.
When the King of Dài heard this,
he told his minister:
"The reason Dài is weaker than Lízhī
is our lack of money.
Now Qí is offering money for white fox furs—
this is Dài's fortune!
Quickly order the people to hunt white fox furs
to obtain Qí's currency.
I will use it to attract Lízhī's people."
The people of Dài indeed abandoned farming,
dwelling in the mountains
to hunt white fox furs.
After twenty-four months, not a single pelt was found.
When Lízhī heard of this,
they invaded from the north.
The King of Dài, upon hearing, was terrified.
He led his troops to defend the valley of Dài.
Lízhī then invaded the north,
and the king led his soldiers to surrender to Qí.
Qí did not spend a single coin,
and within three years, Dài submitted.
Duke Huán asked Guǎnzǐ:
"How can I control Héngshān?"
Guǎnzǐ replied:
"Have people buy Héngshān's weapons at high prices and resell them.
Yān and Dài will follow suit,
and when Qín and Zhào hear,
they will compete with you.
Héngshān's weapons
will double in price.
With everyone vying for them,
Héngshān's weapons
will increase tenfold or more."
The Duke said:
"Agreed."
He sent people to Héngshān to buy weapons,
not haggling over the high prices.
After Qí purchased weapons from Héngshān for ten months,
Yān and Dài heard
and sent envoys to buy weapons.
Yān and Dài bought for three months,
and when Qín heard,
they also sent envoys.
The ruler of Héngshān told his minister:
"The world competes for our weapons,
driving prices up twentyfold."
The people of Héngshān
abandoned farming to master weapon crafting.
Qí then ordered Xí Péng to purchase grain from Zhào.
Zhào sold at fifteen,
but Xí Péng bought at fifty per stone.
Hearing this,
others brought grain to Qí.
After seventeen months of weapon purchases
and five months of grain buying,
Qí closed its borders to Héngshān.
Yān, Dài, Qín, and Zhào recalled their envoys.
Héngshān's weapons were depleted,
Lǔ annexed its south,
and Qí took its north.
Héngshān, lacking weapons to defend,
surrendered to Qí.
Pure spirit gives rise to the mind,
the mind gives rise to the compass,
the compass gives rise to the square,
the square gives rise to correctness,
correctness gives rise to the calendar,
the calendar gives rise to the four seasons,
and the four seasons give rise to all things.
Sages order them accordingly,
and the Way is complete.
Starting from the winter solstice,
after forty-six days,
winter ends and spring begins.
The Son of Heaven proceeds forty-six lǐ east of his capital to build an altar,
dressed in green with a green ceremonial cap,
holding a jade scepter,
wearing a jade pendant,
receiving feudal lords, ministers, and officials,
addressing the common people.
This is called the Sun Sacrifice,
offering fish as sacrifice.
He issues the decree:
"Promote life, not killing;
reward, do not punish;
suspend criminal judgments
until the year's end."
He teaches people to repair houses, drill for fire,
clean stoves, and dredge wells
to prolong their lives.
Plows, harrows, hoes, baskets,
scythes, rakes, sickles, and flails,
tools for spring and summer work,
must be prepared. He teaches people to make wine and food
to show filial respect.
Those born without parents
are called orphans;
those without wife or children,
old bachelors;
those without husband or children,
old widows.
These three groups
are supported by the state.
Whether employable
or not,
they are fed as promised without neglect.
Officials are rewarded for high performance,
penalized for low.
Thus, no beggars are seen on the roads.
If beggars appear,
it is the minister's fault.
Such is the Son of Heaven's spring decree.
Starting from the winter solstice,
after ninety-two days,
it is called spring arrival.
The Son of Heaven proceeds
ninety-two lǐ east of his capital to build an altar,
receiving feudal lords, ministers, and officials,
It is practiced among the common people,
and is called the Sacrifice to the Stars.
Within ten days,
there are no maidens left in the houses,
no travelers on the roads.
Those who do not engage in planting
are called wrongdoers;
those who work the earth below
and emulate the heavens above
are called the disobedient people;
in the villages, they are placed in the lower ranks,
in the army, they are assigned to menial tasks,
and are called laborers.
Three types of non-planters are directed by the ruler.
This is the spring decree of the Son of Heaven.
Beginning from the spring equinox,
after counting forty-six days,
spring ends and summer begins.
The Son of Heaven wears yellow and resides in tranquility,
receiving the feudal lords, ministers, officials, and scholars in audience,
and practicing among the common people,
issuing commands and decrees:
"Do not gather large crowds,
do not set great fires,
do not cut down large trees
(punish high officials),
do not level great mountains,
do not destroy vast marshes.
To destroy these three great things brings harm to the state."
This is the summer prohibition of the Son of Heaven.
Beginning from the spring equinox,
after counting ninety-two days,
it is called the summer solstice,
and the wheat ripens.
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Tàizōng,
using wheat as the offering.
Wheat
is the first of the grains;
the ancestral temple
is the origin of the clan.
Members of the same clan enter,
while those of different clans remain outside.
All fast. With great talent,
he goes out to sacrifice to Wángmǔ.
This is how the Son of Heaven honors beginnings and observes taboos.
Beginning from the summer solstice,
after counting forty-six days,
summer ends and autumn begins,
and the millet ripens.
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Tàizǔ,
using millet as the offering.
Millet
is the finest of the grains.
The ancestor
is the most revered of the state.
Those with great achievements have a great ancestor,
those with minor achievements have a minor ancestor,
those without achievements have no ancestor.
Those with achievements all stand in their positions and perform the libation,
while those without achievements observe from outside.
The ancestral temple
is for sacrificing to achievements,
not for mourning sacrifices.
This is how the Son of Heaven distinguishes nobility from baseness and rewards the meritorious.
Beginning from the summer solstice,
after counting ninety-two days, it is called the autumn equinox.
At the autumn equinox, the grain ripens.
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Tàisuǒ,
going west from the capital
for one hundred thirty-eight lǐ to an altar,
dressed in white and wearing a white ceremonial cap,
holding a jade tablet,
girded with a tin mirror,
blowing the xūn and chí flutes in the wind,
striking the sounds of metal and stone,
receiving the feudal lords, ministers, officials, and scholars in audience,
practicing among the common people,
calling it the Sacrifice to the Moon,
with a pig as the sacrificial animal.
He issues commands and decrees:
punish but do not reward,
take but do not give,
in criminal cases, execute and do not spare,
for year-end crimes,
there shall be no pardons.
He who manages the livestock of oxen and horses in the wild becomes king.
This is the autumn reckoning of the Son of Heaven.
Beginning from the autumn equinox,
after counting forty-six days,
autumn ends and winter begins.
The Son of Heaven wears black and a black ceremonial cap, residing in tranquility,
receiving the feudal lords, ministers, officials, and scholars in audience,
practicing among the common people,
issuing commands and decrees:
"Do not set great fires,
do not level great mountains,
do not block great waters,
do not violate the majesty of heaven."
This is the winter prohibition of the Son of Heaven.
Beginning from the autumn equinox,
after counting ninety-two days,
the Son of Heaven goes north for ninety-two lǐ to an altar,
dressed in black and wearing a black ceremonial cap,
receiving the feudal lords, ministers, officials, and scholars in audience,
calling it the Issuance of Corvée.
Urge the mountain people to cut and gather,
preparing tools and equipment;
urge the marsh people to collect reeds and rushes,
ensuring ample stores.
After three months,
all exchange what they have for what they lack.
This is called the great circulation
of three months' reserves.
As for those who are urged to plow but do not plow,
the people suffer from disorder,
which is the harm of not plowing.
When it is time to weed but weeding is not done,
all sorts of weeds thrive,
and the people barely survive,
which is the harm of not weeding.
When it is time to harvest but harvesting is not done,
and wind and rain approach,
the five grains diminish,
the people scatter and decline,
which is the harm of not harvesting.
When it is time to store but storing is not done,
and the mist is thick,
those who should die live on,
those who should hibernate cry out,
which is the harm of not storing.
Use plowshares as crossbows,
hoes as swords and halberds,
baskets and channels as armor,
straw cloaks and hats as shields.
Thus, when farming tools are complete, weapons of war are prepared.
The chapter is lost.
